6. **הקצאת ה-setup matrix ל-PP/DS resource** — ב-resource master (Transaction /SAPAPO/RES01, Figure 2.62), נווטו ללשונית Time-Cont. Capacity. בשדה Setup Matrix, הזינו את ה-matrix הישים לחישוב המשך ל-orders/operations על ה-resource.
עם routings של S/4HANA, כשיש setup time בפעולה (Figure 2.63) ו-setup formula מתוחזק ב-work center, ה-PDS שנוצר יכלול setup activity המזוהה ב-activity type (Act. Type). אם ה-resource מוקצה ל-generated setup matrix, ב-PDS, ה-setup activity וכל ה-activities של אותה operation יקבלו את ה-indicator Setup group from the characteristics value assignment (Setup Grp) בערך X.
כש-master recipes משמשים (Figure 2.64), צריך setup phase ייעודי תחת ה-operation. בנוסף, כש-setup activity נוכח ב-PDS, חייבת לעקוב produce activity (phase נוסף). ל-setup phase ול-produce phase צריכה relationship ב-master recipe. בדוגמה, ‏0020-setup ו-0030-produce קשורים ב-FS (finish start). כשה-resource מוקצה ל-setup matrix וב-recipe תחת ה-operation באותו resource, ה-phase הראשון יועבר כ-setup activity. ה-setup activity מזוהה ב-Act. Type. אם ה-resource מוקצה ל-generated setup matrix, ה-setup activity וכל ה-activities יקבלו את ה-Setup Grp בערך X.

sections.title: Summary
sections.en: 2.9 Summary Figure 2.64 Setup Activity with Generated Setup Matrix in the SAP S/4HANA Master Recipe When an operation of an order is placed on a resource, the system will evaluate if there is a setup matrix assigned to the resource. If that is a generated setup matrix, the sys- tem evaluates the classification (class/characteristics values) of the product and deter- mines the setup group dynamically. When an operation of an order is followed by another order, the system derives the changeover (setup) time based on the data gen- erated by the setup matrix. 2.9 Summary In this chapter, we covered the basic and most commonly used master data objects in embedded PP/DS. In addition, we covered the various methods to integrate the differ- 2 Master Data 110 ent master data objects from SAP S/4HANA to embedded PP/DS and also the details on master data objects, which are maintained within embedded PP/DS. The material master and resource masters are transferred by simply activating the Advanced Planning checkbox in the master data in SAP S/4HANA. For locations and PDSs, the ABAP programs are executed to initiate the transfer of the data to embedded PP/DS. For external procurement, integration models need to be created and activated to transfer the master data for source supplies, such as purchase info records, schedul- ing agreements, and contracts, as well as classes used in the CDP scenario. For setup groups, such as the static setup groups, the setup groups/keys are integrated via inte- gration model. The setup matrix is created and maintained within embedded PP/DS for both static and dynamic setup matrices. We’ll cover other PP/DS master data objects, such as time-dependent safety stocks, in the upcoming chapters where we’ll cover the functionalities supported by those spe- cific master data objects. Next, we’ll cover the configuration for setting up and operating embedded PP/DS. ©
sections.he:
כשפעולת order מוצבת על resource, המערכת מעריכה אם מוקצה setup matrix. אם זה generated setup matrix, המערכת מעריכה את ה-classification (class/characteristics values) וקובעת את ה-setup group דינמית. כשפעולת order עוקבת אחרי order אחר, המערכת גוזרת את זמן ה-changeover לפי הנתונים שנוצרו.
בפרק זה כיסינו את אובייקטי ה-master data הבסיסיים והנפוצים ב-embedded PP/DS, וכן שיטות שילובם מ-S/4HANA ופרטי האובייקטים המתוחזקים בתוך embedded PP/DS. ה-material master וה-resource masters מועברים ע"י סימון ה-Advanced Planning checkbox. ל-locations ו-PDSs, תוכניות ABAP מבצעות את ההעברה. ל-external procurement, נדרשת יצירה והפעלה של integration models (purchase info records, ‏scheduling agreements, ‏contracts, ו-classes ב-CDP). ל-setup groups (static), ה-groups/keys משולבים דרך integration model. ה-setup matrix נוצר ומתוחזק בתוך embedded PP/DS (static ו-dynamic).
נכסה אובייקטי master data נוספים (כגון time-dependent safety stocks) בפרקים הבאים. בהמשך — התצורה להקמה והפעלה של embedded PP/DS.

sections.title: Activating PP/DS in SAP S/4HANA
sections.en: 3.1 Activating PP/DS in SAP S/4HANA In the SAP S/4HANA system, the PP/DS functionality isn’t activated in the standard delivered software. Explicit activation of the PP/DS functionality is done in the config- uration in the SAP S/4HANA system. Certain SAP Fiori apps that are relevant to the PP/DS functionality are usable only within the activation of PP/DS. Activating PP/DS will enable all advanced planning features as well as the following SAP Fiori apps:  Monitor Capacity Utilization  Production Scheduling Board  Create Optimal Order for Shipment There are technical prerequisites for activating PP/DS in the SAP S/4HANA system, and we’ll cover them at a high level as these activities are related to the installation of the SAP liveCache application software and setting up the database to enable the SAP liveCache 3 Configuration 112 connections. Appendix A provides the SAP Notes to the detailed setup guide for the integrated SAP liveCache in an SAP HANA database. The technical prerequisites are as follows:  Installation of SAP liveCache in the SAP HANA database  Creation of SAP liveCache connections and enabled execution of SAP liveCache pro- cedures  Execution of initialization report /SAPAPO/OM_LIVECACHE_SETUP_S4H or reports SLCA_INIT_FOLLOW_UP and /SAPAPO/OM_CREATE_LC_TABLES to prepare the SAP liveCache and create all the required database tables  Setup of the remote function call (RFC) connection for all the clients in the SAP S/4HANA system that are relevant for SAP liveCache After the technical prerequisites are performed, execute Transaction /SAPAPO/OM13 to do a basic health check on SAP liveCache. As shown in Figure 3.1, the Checks tab shows the result of the individual checks, and the information on the warnings and errors can be displayed by clicking on the information button next to them. When you execute Transaction /SAPAPO/OM03 in the system to test the SAP liveCache, you should see a success message. Figure 3.1 SAP liveCache Health Check Report in SAP S/4HANA © 113
sections.he:
ב-S/4HANA, פונקציית ה-PP/DS אינה מופעלת בתוכנה התקנית. הפעלה מפורשת נעשית בתצורה. אפליקציות Fiori מסוימות הרלוונטיות ל-PP/DS שמישות רק עם הפעלת PP/DS.
הפעלת PP/DS תאפשר את כל תכונות ה-advanced planning וכן את אפליקציות ה-Fiori:
• Monitor Capacity Utilization
• Production Scheduling Board
• Create Optimal Order for Shipment
יש תנאים מוקדמים טכניים, ונכסה אותם ברמה גבוהה (קשורים להתקנת תוכנת SAP liveCache והקמת מסד הנתונים לאפשור חיבורי SAP liveCache). ‏Appendix A מספק את ה-SAP Notes למדריך ההקמה המפורט ל-SAP liveCache המשולב במסד SAP HANA. התנאים המוקדמים:
• התקנת SAP liveCache במסד SAP HANA
• יצירת חיבורי SAP liveCache והפעלת הרצת פרוצדורות SAP liveCache
• הרצת דוח ה-initialization‏ /SAPAPO/OM_LIVECACHE_SETUP_S4H או דוחות SLCA_INIT_FOLLOW_UP ו-/SAPAPO/OM_CREATE_LC_TABLES להכנת ה-SAP liveCache ויצירת כל הטבלאות
• הקמת חיבור RFC לכל ה-clients הרלוונטיים ל-SAP liveCache
לאחר התנאים המוקדמים, הריצו Transaction /SAPAPO/OM13 ל-health check בסיסי על SAP liveCache. כפי שב-Figure 3.1, לשונית ה-Checks מציגה את תוצאת הבדיקות, ומידע על warnings ו-errors בלחיצה על כפתור המידע. בהרצת Transaction /SAPAPO/OM03 לבדיקת ה-SAP liveCache, אמורה להופיע הודעת success.

sections.title: Basic Settings for Embedded PP/DS
sections.en: 3.2 Basic Settings for Embedded PP/DS The next step is to activate PP/DS in Customizing. To perform this, execute Transaction SPRO, and then follow the menu path, SAP Customizing Implementation Guide  Advanced Planning  Basic Settings  Activate Advanced Planning and Scheduling  Acti- vate Advanced Planning and Scheduling. As shown in Figure 3.2, select the Activate Advanced Planning and Scheduling check- box, and click the Save button. This will complete the activation of the PP/DS advanced planning features in the SAP S/4HANA system. Figure 3.2 Activation of PP/DS in SAP S/4HANA After advanced planning is activated, you can set up the basic settings as explained in the next section of this chapter. 3.2 Basic Settings for Embedded PP/DS In this section, we’ll cover the basic settings required to set up embedded PP/DS. These settings aren’t specific to any functionality or features, but they are required to execute any PP/DS functions in the SAP S/4HANA system.
sections.he:
הצעד הבא — הפעלת PP/DS ב-Customizing. הריצו Transaction SPRO, ועקבו אחר menu path: ‏SAP Customizing Implementation Guide • Advanced Planning • Basic Settings • Activate Advanced Planning and Scheduling • Activate Advanced Planning and Scheduling. כפי שב-Figure 3.2, סמנו את ה-Activate Advanced Planning and Scheduling checkbox, ולחצו Save. זה משלים את הפעלת תכונות ה-advanced planning ב-S/4HANA.
בסעיף זה נכסה את ההגדרות הבסיסיות הנדרשות להקמת embedded PP/DS. אינן ספציפיות לפונקציה, אך נדרשות לביצוע פונקציות PP/DS כלשהן.

sections.title: Model Version Management
sections.en: 3.2.1 Model Version Management In embedded PP/DS, similar to the SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization system, all the master data objects are assigned to the supply chain model. All the master data elements should be assigned to a model for the system to consider this data in the plan- ning and scheduling functions and tools. Embedded PP/DS only supports the model 000, which is the default active model in the system. All the master data integrated from SAP S/4HANA using the transfer pro- grams, Advanced Planning checkboxes, or integration model are always assigned to model 000. The version is a subsection of the model. There can be multiple versions created under model 000 in embedded PP/DS. The 000 version is the active version in PP/DS. Other versions can be created for carrying out planning simulation with changed master data settings, if required. As part of the embedded PP/DS setup, the model and version must be created in the system. To create a model, you can use Transaction /SAPAPO/MVM or use the SAP 3 Configuration 114 menu path, Logistics  Advanced Planning  Master Data  Planning Version Manage- ment  Model and Version Management. You’ll arrive at the Model and Version Management screen, as shown in Figure 3.3. Click on the Create button, and select Model. Enter the model Name as “000”, enter a description for the model (here, Active Model), and click on the Create and Save button to save the model. Figure 3.3 Creating a Model in Embedded PP/DS After the model is created, the next step is to create the planning version as 000, which is the active version under the active model 000. To do so, click the Create button again, and select Planning Version. As shown in Figure 3.4, create the planning version “000”, and enter a description for the version. Figure 3.4 Creating the Planning Version and Relevant Settings for PP/DS © 115 3.2 Basic Settings for Embedded PP/DS Select the Change Planning Active checkbox, and make the following key settings:  Standard Planning Horizon (Days) The PP/DS horizon in days defines the number of calendar days within which the PP/DS system is allowed to create, change, and delete procurement proposals during a planning run execution. Beyond the PP/DS horizon, it’s possible to create procure- ment proposals manually using the PP/DS transactions. There is no option to set any material-specific planning horizon in embedded PP/DS, and all the advanced planning products will use the PP/DS horizon defined in the planning version set- tings. In SAP S/4HANA 2022, the PP/DS horizon is also available in the material mas- ter advanced planning view. If the PP/DS horizon isn’t maintained in the material master, the value from the planning version is used by the system.  Determine Priority In PP/DS, it’s possible to assign priorities to the procurement proposals (e.g., planned orders). These order priorities are used in PP/DS functions such as schedul- ing heuristics to reduce the delays in manufacturing an order that has higher prior- ity. Click on the value help button in the Determine Priority field, and you’ll see the following options: – In make to order from sales order otherwise from product With this setting, the priority of the orders that are created to cover a sales order requirement is derived from the priority assigned to the sales order. If the requirement element isn’t a sales order, the priority is derived from the value maintained in the product master under the advanced planning view. – Always adopt from requirement With this setting, the priority of the order created by PP/DS is always derived from the requirement element such as sales orders or orders belonging to higher level planned orders to which the particular order is linked. This linkage of orders in PP/DS is called pegging. Planned independent requirements (PIRs) or forecast ele- ments don’t have any priorities assigned to them, so no priority is assigned to orders pegged to such requirement elements. It’s also possible that one order is pegged to multiple requirements; in that case, a planning algorithm can be exe- cuted to reprioritize the orders. We’ll cover the details of this planning algorithm (heuristic) in Chapter 5. Tip In an SAP S/4HANA sales order, under the item details in the Shipping tab, the Delivery Priority can be maintained. This value is transferred to PP/DS as the order priority for that sales order and item.  Always adopt from the product With this setting, the orders will always derive the priority from the product master, irrespective of the priority assigned to the requirement element. 3 Configuration 116 Note The priorities in PP/DS are defined from numbers 0 to 255, with 1 as the highest priority. The priority 0 is equal to the least priority 255.  Take Safety Stock into Account Safety stock is the requirement element used in the plan to cover any unplanned demand that may result in a stock-out situation. PP/DS supports safety stock in planning. Click on the value help button for Take Safety Stock into Account to see the following options: – Don’t Consider Safety Stock The safety stock requirements aren’t considered in PP/DS, and no safety stock alerts are created in PP/DS. – Consider Virtual Safety Stock Elements In the SAP S/4HANA system, the safety stocks are only virtual elements, which means that the safety stock elements aren’t created as orders in SAP liveCache. Therefore, these safety stock elements are used only in calculation of the net requirements and aren’t pegged to an order or a receipt element.  No Order Without Source of Supply In PP/DS, when orders are created, the source of supply, such as a production data structure (PDS) or an external procurement relationship (e.g., info records), is assigned to the orders. If there are no suitable sources of supply found, the orders can still be created, but the order dates can’t be correct as the source of supply deter- mines the duration it takes to procure or produce a material. In the planning ver- sion, you can define whether you want to create orders when no suitable source of supply is available or how the system should react when no source of supply is deter- mined. In this field, click on the value help to select from the following options: – (Blank): Order Without Source of Supply Allowed – E: No Order Without Source of Supply with In-House Production – F: No Order Without Source of Supply with External Procurement – X: No Order Without Source of Supply Generally Then, click the Create and Save button to create the planning version. The Change Planning Active option is required for using the PP/DS functions productively. When there is a planning-relevant change, such as creation, change, or deletion of any receipt or requirement data, or a planning-relevant master data is produced in the system, the system reacts according to the planning procedures customized and assigned to the product master. We’ll cover the details of the planning procedure in Section 3.4.
sections.he:
ב-embedded PP/DS, בדומה ל-SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization, כל ה-master data objects מוקצים ל-supply chain model. כל אלמנט master data צריך להיות מוקצה ל-model כדי שהמערכת תתחשב בו בתכנון ובתזמון.
‏embedded PP/DS תומך רק ב-model 000 (ה-model הפעיל ברירת-המחדל). כל ה-master data המשולב מ-S/4HANA תמיד מוקצה ל-model 000. ה-version הוא תת-חלק של ה-model. ניתן ליצור versions מרובים תחת model 000. ‏version 000 הוא הפעיל. ניתן ליצור versions אחרים ל-simulation עם הגדרות master data משונות.
כחלק מההקמה, יש ליצור את ה-model וה-version. ליצירת model, השתמשו ב-Transaction /SAPAPO/MVM או menu path: ‏Logistics • Advanced Planning • Master Data • Planning Version Management • Model and Version Management.
תגיעו למסך Model and Version Management (Figure 3.3). לחצו Create, ובחרו Model. הזינו Name "000", תיאור (Active Model), ולחצו Create and Save.
לאחר היצירה, הצעד הבא — יצירת ה-planning version 000 (ה-active version תחת model 000). לחצו Create שוב, ובחרו Planning Version (Figure 3.4). צרו version "000" עם תיאור.
סמנו את ה-Change Planning Active checkbox, ובצעו את ההגדרות המרכזיות:
• **Standard Planning Horizon (Days)** — ה-PP/DS horizon בימים מגדיר את מספר ימי הלוח שבהם PP/DS רשאי ליצור/לשנות/למחוק procurement proposals בריצת תכנון. מעבר ל-horizon, ניתן ליצור ידנית. אין horizon ספציפי-חומר ב-embedded PP/DS, וכל המוצרים משתמשים ב-PP/DS horizon מהגדרות ה-version. ב-S/4HANA 2022, ה-horizon זמין גם ב-material master advanced planning view. אם לא מתוחזק שם, נעשה שימוש בערך מה-version.
• **Determine Priority** — ניתן להקצות priorities ל-procurement proposals (planned orders). משמשים בפונקציות כגון scheduling heuristics להפחתת עיכובים ב-order בעדיפות גבוהה. אפשרויות:
– **In make to order from sales order otherwise from product** — עדיפות ה-orders המכסים sales order נגזרת מעדיפות ה-sales order. אם לא sales order, מה-product master (advanced planning view).
– **Always adopt from requirement** — העדיפות נגזרת תמיד מאלמנט הדרישה (sales orders או orders של planned orders ברמה גבוהה שאליהם ה-order מקושר — קישור זה נקרא pegging). ל-planned independent requirements (PIRs) או forecast elements אין עדיפויות. ייתכן ש-order מקושר ל-requirements מרובים; אז ניתן להריץ אלגוריתם לתעדוף-מחדש (heuristic, פרק 5).
**טיפ:** ב-sales order של S/4HANA, תחת פרטי הפריט בלשונית Shipping, ניתן לתחזק Delivery Priority. ערך זה מועבר ל-PP/DS כ-order priority.
– **Always adopt from the product** — ה-orders תמיד גוזרים את העדיפות מה-product master, ללא קשר לאלמנט הדרישה.
**הערה:** העדיפויות ב-PP/DS מ-0 עד 255, כש-1 הגבוהה ביותר. ‏0 שווה לעדיפות הנמוכה ביותר 255.
• **Take Safety Stock into Account** — ‏safety stock הוא אלמנט הדרישה המכסה ביקוש לא-מתוכנן שעלול לגרום ל-stock-out. אפשרויות:
– **Don't Consider Safety Stock** — אינו נחשב, ואין safety stock alerts.
– **Consider Virtual Safety Stock Elements** — ב-S/4HANA, ה-safety stocks הם אלמנטים וירטואליים בלבד (אינם נוצרים כ-orders ב-SAP liveCache). משמשים רק בחישוב net requirements ואינם pegged.
• **No Order Without Source of Supply** — ביצירת orders, ה-source of supply (PDS או external procurement relationship) מוקצה. אם לא נמצא source מתאים, ה-orders עדיין ניתנים ליצירה, אך התאריכים לא יהיו נכונים. אפשרויות:
– (ריק): Order Without Source of Supply Allowed
– E: No Order Without Source of Supply with In-House Production
– F: No Order Without Source of Supply with External Procurement
– X: No Order Without Source of Supply Generally
לחצו Create and Save.
ה-Change Planning Active נדרש לשימוש פרודוקטיבי. כשיש שינוי רלוונטי-תכנון (יצירה/שינוי/מחיקה של receipt או requirement), המערכת מגיבה לפי ה-planning procedures המותאמים והמוקצים ל-product master (סעיף 3.4).

sections.title: Integration Settings
sections.en: 3.2.2 Integration Settings In the SAP S/4HANA system, to enable the transfer of master data and transaction data from SAP S/4HANA to embedded PP/DS and vice versa, you must make the following basic core interface settings, which we’ll discuss in this section: © 117 3.2 Basic Settings for Embedded PP/DS  Activate the business transfer event (BTE) indicator.  Create a system landscape.  Maintain business system groups (BSGs) and assign logical systems.  Set up core interface user parameters.  Make the publication settings.  Register the core interface queues. In embedded PP/DS, there are two sets of core interface settings that need to be made: one for the transfer of data from SAP S/4HANA to embedded PP/DS and another for the trans- fer of data from embedded PP/DS to the SAP S/4HANA side. Though some of the settings, such as creating the system landscape and RFC destinations, are the same for both sets of core interface settings, certain settings, such as maintaining BSGs, are only relevant under embedded PP/DS. In addition, a different set of settings is required under the assignment of logical system and queue types for embedded PP/DS and SAP S/4HANA settings. Activate the Business Transfer Events Indicators Changes to master data and transaction data in SAP S/4HANA that need to be trans- ferred to embedded PP/DS via online transfer without executing an explicit job or pro- gram to transfer the data uses the BTE framework. In embedded PP/DS, the BTE indicators New Dimension Integration (NDI) and New Dimension Plugin APO (ND-APO) need to be activated for enabling the online transfer of data. Figure 3.5 Activating BTE Indicators in Transaction BF11 3 Configuration 118 To enable these BTE indicators, execute Transaction BF11 (Change View “BTE Applica- tion Indicator”), and set the application active indicator for the applications ND-APO and NDI by checking the corresponding boxes in the A column, as shown in Figure 3.5. Create System Landscape In SAP S/4HANA, setting the landscape for the transfer of data between SAP S/4HANA and embedded PP/DS is achieved via the core interface framework. The core interface works based on the definition of the logical system, which represents the system ID of the SAP S/4HANA system and the client in which the transactions are performed. You can define the logical system via the Customizing menu path, SAP IMG Menu  Advanced Planning  Integration via Core Interface (CIF)  Integration  Basic Settings for Creating the System Landscape  Name Logical Systems. You’ll arrive at the screen shown in Figure 3.6, where you can define a Name for the logical system and click on the Save button to save the data. Figure 3.6 Defining the Logical System for the Core Interface After the logical system is defined, it must be assigned to the client to which it corre- sponds. To assign the logical system to the client, use the menu path, SAP IMG Menu  Advanced Planning  Integration via Core Interface (CIF)  Integration  Basic Settings for Creating the System Landscape  Assign Logical System to a Client. Then, link the client to the defined logical system by entering the client name in the Client field and the logical system defined in the previous step in the Logical system field, as shown in Figure 3.7. Tip There are other SAP S/4HANA applications that require the usage of logical systems, so if there is already a logical system defined in the SAP S/4HANA system for the system ID assigned to the client, that logical system can be used for the core interface as well. An RFC destination needs to be defined in the SAP S/4HANA system that will be used by the system to transfer data between SAP S/4HANA and embedded PP/DS. The core © 119 3.2 Basic Settings for Embedded PP/DS interface framework will leverage the RFC destination for data transfer. The RFC desti- nation can be defined using Transaction SM59 or the Customizing menu path, SAP IMG Menu  Advanced Planning  Integration via Core Interface (CIF)  Integration  Basic Set- tings for Creating the System Landscape  Set Up RFC Destination. Figure 3.7 Assigning a Logical System to the Client Note Creation of the RFC destination is a Basis/technical step. But ensure that the RFC desti- nation name exactly matches the logical system defined. This is the link for the system to use the correct RFC destination for data transfer using core interface. When data is transferred between SAP S/4HANA and embedded PP/DS, the system needs to recognize the software version of PP/DS in SAP S/4HANA for technical rea- sons. To define this, use the Customizing menu path, SAP IMG Menu  Integration with Other SAP Components  Advanced Planning and Optimization  Basic Settings for Set- ting Up the System Landscape  Specify APO Release. Here, enter the Log.System as the 3 Configuration 120 SAP S/4HANA logical system defined, Syst. Type as “SAP_APO”, and Release as “713”, as shown in Figure 3.8. Figure 3.8 Specifying the SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization Release for Embedded PP/DS in the Core Interface Note The SAP S/4HANA system can also act as an ERP system alongside a standalone SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization system; in that case, the Customizing settings need to be maintained for the standalone SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization system. In addition, for SAP Supply Chain Management (SAP SCM) applications such as SAP Transportation Management (SAP TM) and SAP Extended Warehouse Manage- ment (SAP EWM), separate entries with the corresponding system details need to be maintained. Maintain Business System Group In the embedded PP/DS side of the core interface settings, a BSG needs to be defined. In the SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization system, as multiple ERP systems such as SAP ERP and SAP S/4HANA can be integrated into one SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization system, the BSG is defined for all such connected ERP systems. In addi- tion, the data sets for each of these connected ERP systems are identified by their own BSGs. In the embedded PP/DS system, because it’s not possible to connect any other ERP systems and it can operate only with the same SAP S/4HANA system, the BSG defi- nition doesn’t have much significance. But it’s technically required to create one BSG system and link it to the logical system definition. To define the BSG, use the Customizing menu path, SAP IMG Menu  Advanced Planning  Integration via Core Interface (CIF)  Integration  Maintain Business System Group. In this screen, click on the New Entries button to see the screen shown in Figure 3.9. Here, enter a name for the BSG under the BusSystGrp column and a Description for the BSG. © 121 3.2 Basic Settings for Embedded PP/DS Figure 3.9 Defining a Business System Group in Embedded PP/DS Once the BSG is created, it needs to be linked to the logical system already defined, and, in this step, we’ll also maintain the software release for the ERP system. The software version here doesn’t correspond to the SAP S/4HANA release but instead to a technical setting required for the core interface to transfer data from embedded PP/DS to the SAP S/4HANA side. To define these settings, follow the Customizing menu path, SAP IMG Menu  Advanced Planning  Integration via Core Interface (CIF)  Integration  Assign Logical System and Queue Type. In the initial screen of this transaction, click the New Entries button, and, in the next screen, enter the BSG that was already created under the BusSystGrp column, enter “X” in SAP Ind. to denote that the ERP system is an SAP ERP system, and enter “700” under Rel, as shown in Figure 3.10. Figure 3.10 Assigning the Business System Group to the Logical System and Other Embedded PP/DS Core Interface Settings In addition, it’s recommended to set Queue Type as Inbound Queues, as shown in Fig- ure 3.10. If there are any errors raised during the transfer of data from embedded PP/DS to SAP S/4HANA, the core interface queues will fail in the inbound queue processing Transaction SMQ2 from which they can be processed further. Setting the queue type as Inbound Queue under both the SAP S/4HANA and embedded PP/DS sides of the core 3 Configuration 122 interface settings will make it easier to monitor all the queues from single Transaction SMQ2. Note For the Queue Type for the SAP S/4HANA to embedded PP/DS direction for data trans- fer, maintain it as Inbound Queue under the Customizing menu path, SAP IMG Menu  Integration with Other SAP Components  Advanced Planning and Optimization  Basic Settings for Setting Up the System Landscape  Set Target System and Queue Type. From embedded PP/DS, it’s recommended to activate the postprocessing so that if any transaction data transferred between SAP S/4HANA and embedded PP/DS fails for any reason, the data is logged in the Post Processing Framework (PPF) for reprocessing instead of the queues going into error mode and causing backed up queues. To activate postprocessing, select 1 Postprocessing for Errors, No Splitting of LUWs in the Err. Hndlg column for the corresponding SAP S/4HANA logical system, as shown previously in Figure 3.10. Set Up the Core Interface User Parameters User settings in the core interface Customizing define how the data transfer is handled in terms of activating or deactivating the data transfer for users, the level of logging for the data transfer, and technical settings to stop the execution of the transfer for debug- ging purposes. To define the user settings in the SAP S/4HANA side for the data transfer from the SAP S/4HANA to embedded PP/DS direction, use Transaction CFC2 or the Customizing menu path, SAP IMG Menu  Integration with Other SAP Components  Advanced Plan- ning and Optimization  Basic Settings for Data Transfer  Set User Parameters. Click on the New Entries button, and you’ll arrive at the screen shown in Figure 3.11. Figure 3.11 User Settings for the Core Interface in Embedded PP/DS © 123 3.2 Basic Settings for Embedded PP/DS There is no need to maintain the user settings for all user names in the SAP S/4HANA system. A generic wild card entry (*) can be made instead, as shown in Figure 3.12. Main- tain the RFC Mode as “Q”, which activates the transfer of data using the queued RFC (qRFC) protocol via the defined RFC destinations. For embedded PP/DS, the RFC desti- nation will point to itself (self-system). The Logging can be set to the required level of logging from the following available options:  [blank] (no logging) No logs are written to the application logs for the transfers.  X (normal) Only the number of records is recorded in the log.  D (detailed) The number of records as well as the content of the data are logged. The Debug setting can be used only for troubleshooting any problems in the data trans- fers; it should be switched off otherwise. The user settings for embedded PP/DS for the data transfer from embedded PP/DS to the SAP S/4HANA side are maintained under Transaction /SAPAPO/C4 or Customizing menu path, SAP IMG Menu  Advanced Planning  Integration via Core Interface (CIF)  Basic Settings for Data Transfer  Set User Parameters. As shown in Figure 3.12, like the Transaction CFC2 settings for SAP S/4HANA, the log- ging level and the debugging settings are made in embedded PP/DS core interface user settings as well. One difference is the additional setting available in embedded PP/DS for recording the data transfer. Under the Recording column, there are three options available:  Default The system will consider the configuration made in the PP/DS global settings and defaults as explained in Section 3.2.5.  Collect Changes The system won’t send the data immediately to SAP S/4HANA from embedded PP/DS. All changes performed manually or via automatic planning and scheduling in embed- ded PP/DS are collected in PP/DS. Transaction /SAPAPO/C5 needs to be executed man- ually or scheduled in the background to transfer this data to the SAP S/4HANA side. This setting can be useful in cases where the system performance is impacted due to the automatic/background planning or scheduling run happening, and the queues generated from this run are processed in parallel. With this setting during the plan- ning or scheduling runs, the system won’t process the queues to update or create the data in the SAP S/4HANA side, but the data transfer is executed as a separate step after the planning or scheduling run is completed. During the data transfer from embedded PP/DS to SAP S/4HANA, not only is the queue generated for updating/creating the data in the SAP S/4HANA side but also an 3 Configuration 124 acknowledgement from the SAP S/4HANA side with any new numbers determined for the transaction data such as planned order number and purchase requisition number is transferred back to the embedded PP/DS side. This acknowledgement process is called key completion.  Do Not Collect Changes As soon as any planning or scheduling data is changed in PP/DS manually or via background automatic planning/scheduling runs, the data is immediately trans- ferred via the core interface to the SAP S/4HANA side, and the key completion is also performed. Figure 3.12 Embedded PP/DS Core Interface User Settings Publication Settings The core interface publication settings, such as maintaining the distribution defini- tions, which are required in the SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization system, aren’t required in embedded PP/DS. However, the retransfer settings are still relevant in embedded PP/DS. When produc- tion orders are created in SAP S/4HANA and transferred to PP/DS, different order dates can be determined in PP/DS. In such cases, if you want to immediately update the pro- duction order in SAP S/4HANA with the new dates, you must maintain the retransfer settings. Example In PP/DS, a resource downtime is maintained from November 1st, 2022, to November 30th, 2022. If a production order with start and end dates of November 11th is created in SAP S/4HANA, when it’s transferred to PP/DS, the order will get new dates outside the month of November as the resource is blocked with a downtime in PP/DS. © 125 3.2 Basic Settings for Embedded PP/DS To maintain the retransfer settings, follow the Customizing menu path, SAP IMG Menu  Advanced Planning  Integration via Core Interface (CIF)  Basic Settings for Data Transfer  Maintain Object-Specific Settings. In the initial screen, click on the New Entries button, and then select the object type you want to make the retransfer settings for in the next screen. As shown in Figure 3.13, In-House Production is selected, and the Block Size can be left empty as it will be defaulted to the value of 100 by the system internally. Under the Retransfer column, you have the following options.  No Retransfer When a rescheduling is performed in PP/DS because orders are integrated from SAP S/4HANA, the new dates aren’t updated in SAP S/4HANA. But if there are subsequent changes to the orders performed in PP/DS either manually or via scheduling heuris- tics, then the changes made to those orders are sent to SAP S/4HANA.  Always Retransfer Any new dates determined in PP/DS when orders are integrated from SAP S/4HANA are immediately updated in the SAP S/4HANA side as well. This setting will ensure the dates are always synced between SAP S/4HANA and embedded PP/DS.  Only Retransfer After Online Transfer When an initial transfer of the orders are executed, for example, when a new mate- rial is activated for advanced planning, and the initial transfer report /SAPAPO/ PPDS_DELTA_ORD_TRANS is used to transfer the orders from SAP S/4HANA to embedded PP/DS, if a rescheduling occurs in PP/DS during the initial transfer, the new dates aren’t immediately sent to SAP S/4HANA. But when an online transfer (which is a subsequent change on the order in the SAP S/4HANA side that triggers the order change to be transferred to PP/DS) happens, then the retransfer of the new PP/DS dates to SAP S/4HANA will be triggered. Figure 3.13 Retransfer Settings in Embedded PP/DS 3 Configuration 126 In the example shown in Figure 3.13, Always Retransfer should be selected as the retransfer setting, which will ensure that the order dates are in sync. Register the Core Interface Queues The technical activation of queue processing can be performed from Transaction SMQS (QOUT Scheduler) and Transaction SMQR (QIN Scheduler). Activation of the inbound and outbound queue schedulers is required for the automatic processing of the core interface queues. To register the outbound queues, execute Transaction SMQS, and click on the Registra- tion button to arrive at the screen shown in Figure 3.14. Figure 3.14 Registration of Outbound Queues Here, enter the Destination as the logical system defined for the SAP S/4HANA system. The maximum connection (Max.Conn.) defines the number of parallel processes the outbound scheduler can use in the system and is defaulted to 10. The maximum run- time (Max. Runtime) defines the number of seconds the outbound scheduler runs when it’s activated and is defaulted to 60. Click on the Continue button. This completes the registration of outbound queues. © 127 3.2 Basic Settings for Embedded PP/DS To register the inbound queues, execute Transaction SMQR, and click on the Registra- tion button. This will take you to the screen shown in Figure 3.15. Because all the queue names start with “CF”, enter the value “CF*” in the Queue name field to find the queue names. The Mode field is defaulted to value D representing that the queues are pro- cessed in the system using dialog work processes. The Max. Runtime is the number of seconds the queue scheduler is active and is set at 30 by default. If there is a queue fail- ure due to communication issues, for example, the value defined in the Attempts field (defaulted to 10) determines how many times the system tries to execute the queue. Between each retry, the system will wait for the number of seconds defined in the Pause field (defaulted to 120). Click on the Continue button to complete the registration of the inbound queues. Figure 3.15 Registration of Inbound Core Interface Queues
sections.he:
ב-S/4HANA, לאפשור העברת master ו-transaction data בין S/4HANA ל-embedded PP/DS ובחזרה, יש לבצע את הגדרות ה-core interface הבסיסיות:
• הפעלת ה-business transfer event (BTE) indicator.
• יצירת system landscape.
• תחזוקת business system groups (BSGs) והקצאת logical systems.
• הקמת core interface user parameters.
• ביצוע publication settings.
• רישום ה-core interface queues.
ב-embedded PP/DS, שני סטים של הגדרות core interface: אחד להעברה מ-S/4HANA ל-embedded PP/DS, ואחד מ-embedded PP/DS ל-S/4HANA. חלק (system landscape, ‏RFC destinations) זהים, אך חלק (BSGs) רלוונטיים רק תחת embedded PP/DS.

**Activate the BTE Indicators:** שינויים שיש להעביר online ללא job מפורש משתמשים ב-BTE framework. יש להפעיל את ה-indicators New Dimension Integration (NDI) ו-New Dimension Plugin APO (ND-APO). הריצו Transaction BF11 (Change View "BTE Application Indicator"), וסמנו את ה-A column ל-ND-APO ו-NDI (Figure 3.5).

**Create System Landscape:** הגדרת הנוף נעשית דרך ה-core interface, העובד לפי הגדרת ה-logical system (מייצג את system ID של S/4HANA וה-client). הגדירו logical system דרך menu path: ‏SAP IMG Menu • Advanced Planning • Integration via Core Interface (CIF) • Integration • Basic Settings for Creating the System Landscape • Name Logical Systems (Figure 3.6). הקצו ל-client דרך Assign Logical System to a Client (Figure 3.7).
**טיפ:** אם כבר מוגדר logical system ל-system ID, ניתן להשתמש בו גם ל-core interface.
יש להגדיר RFC destination דרך Transaction SM59 או menu path: ‏... • Set Up RFC Destination.
**הערה:** יצירת ה-RFC destination היא צעד Basis/טכני. ודאו ששם ה-RFC destination תואם בדיוק ל-logical system המוגדר.
לזיהוי גרסת התוכנה של PP/DS, השתמשו ב-menu path: ‏SAP IMG Menu • Integration with Other SAP Components • Advanced Planning and Optimization • Basic Settings for Setting Up the System Landscape • Specify APO Release. הזינו Log.System (ה-logical system של S/4HANA), ‏Syst. Type = "SAP_APO", ו-Release = "713" (Figure 3.8).
**הערה:** ‏S/4HANA יכול לשמש כ-ERP לצד מערכת SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization עצמאית; אז יש לתחזק את ההגדרות למערכת העצמאית. בנוסף, ל-SAP SCM applications (SAP TM, ‏SAP EWM), נדרשות רשומות נפרדות.

**Maintain Business System Group:** בצד ה-embedded PP/DS, יש להגדיר BSG. ב-SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization, מכיוון שמערכות ERP מרובות משולבות, ה-BSG מוגדר לכולן, וסטי הנתונים מזוהים ע"י ה-BSGs. ב-embedded PP/DS, מכיוון שלא ניתן לחבר מערכות אחרות, הגדרת ה-BSG חסרת משמעות רבה אך נדרשת טכנית. הגדירו דרך menu path: ‏... • Maintain Business System Group. לחצו New Entries, והזינו שם תחת BusSystGrp ו-Description (Figure 3.9).
לאחר היצירה, יש לקשרו ל-logical system ולתחזק את גרסת התוכנה ל-ERP (הגדרה טכנית, לא תואמת לגרסת S/4HANA). דרך menu path: ‏... • Assign Logical System and Queue Type. לחצו New Entries, הזינו את ה-BSG תחת BusSystGrp, "X" ב-SAP Ind. (מציין SAP ERP), ו-"700" תחת Rel (Figure 3.10).
מומלץ לקבוע Queue Type = Inbound Queues (Figure 3.10). אם נוצרות שגיאות בהעברה מ-embedded PP/DS ל-S/4HANA, ה-queues ייכשלו ב-Transaction SMQ2 לעיבוד נוסף. קביעת Inbound Queue בשני הצדדים תקל על הניטור מ-Transaction SMQ2 יחיד.
**הערה:** ל-Queue Type בכיוון S/4HANA→embedded PP/DS, תחזקו Inbound Queue תחת menu path: ‏... • Set Target System and Queue Type.
מ-embedded PP/DS, מומלץ להפעיל postprocessing כך שאם transaction data נכשל, הנתונים נרשמים ב-Post Processing Framework (PPF) לעיבוד-מחדש במקום ש-queues ייכנסו ל-error mode. בחרו 1 Postprocessing for Errors, No Splitting of LUWs בעמודת Err. Hndlg (Figure 3.10).

**Set Up Core Interface User Parameters:** הגדרות ה-user מגדירות כיצד מטופלת ההעברה — הפעלה/השבתה למשתמשים, רמת logging, והגדרות לעצירה ל-debugging. לכיוון S/4HANA→embedded PP/DS, השתמשו ב-Transaction CFC2 או menu path: ‏... • Set User Parameters (Figure 3.11). אין צורך לתחזק לכל המשתמשים — ניתן wild card (*) (Figure 3.12). תחזקו RFC Mode = "Q" (מפעיל qRFC). ל-embedded PP/DS, ה-RFC destination מצביע לעצמו (self-system). ה-Logging:
• [ריק] (ללא logging)
• X (normal) — רק מספר הרשומות
• D (detailed) — מספר הרשומות ותוכן הנתונים
ה-Debug רק לטיפול בבעיות.
לכיוון embedded PP/DS→S/4HANA, השתמשו ב-Transaction /SAPAPO/C4 או menu path: ‏... • Set User Parameters (Figure 3.12). הבדל: הגדרה נוספת תחת Recording:
• **Default** — לפי התצורה ב-PP/DS global settings (סעיף 3.2.5).
• **Collect Changes** — המערכת לא תשלח מיד. כל השינויים נאספים ב-PP/DS. יש להריץ Transaction /SAPAPO/C5 ידנית או ב-background להעברה. שימושי כשהביצועים מושפעים מריצות אוטומטיות. בהעברה, לא רק queue נוצר אלא גם acknowledgement מ-S/4HANA עם מספרים חדשים (planned order, ‏purchase requisition) — תהליך זה נקרא key completion.
• **Do Not Collect Changes** — ברגע ששינוי נעשה, מועבר מיד עם key completion.

**Publication Settings:** הגדרות distribution definitions הנדרשות ב-SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization אינן נדרשות ב-embedded PP/DS. אך הגדרות ה-retransfer עדיין רלוונטיות. כש-production orders נוצרים ב-S/4HANA ומועברים, ייתכנו תאריכים שונים ב-PP/DS. אם רוצים לעדכן מיד את ה-production order, תחזקו את הגדרות ה-retransfer.
**דוגמה:** ב-PP/DS, ‏resource downtime מ-1 בנובמבר 2022 עד 30 בנובמבר. אם production order עם תאריכי 11 בנובמבר נוצר ב-S/4HANA, בהעברה ל-PP/DS ה-order יקבל תאריכים מחוץ לנובמבר כי ה-resource חסום.
תחזקו דרך menu path: ‏... • Maintain Object-Specific Settings. לחצו New Entries ובחרו את סוג האובייקט (Figure 3.13; ‏In-House Production נבחר, ‏Block Size יכול להישאר ריק = 100). תחת Retransfer:
• **No Retransfer** — בעת rescheduling ב-PP/DS, התאריכים החדשים אינם מעודכנים ב-S/4HANA. אך שינויים נוספים ב-PP/DS נשלחים.
• **Always Retransfer** — תאריכים חדשים מעודכנים מיד ב-S/4HANA — מבטיח סנכרון.
• **Only Retransfer After Online Transfer** — בהעברה ראשונית (חומר חדש מופעל; דוח /SAPAPO/PPDS_DELTA_ORD_TRANS), אם rescheduling מתרחש, התאריכים אינם נשלחים מיד. אך בעת online transfer, ה-retransfer מופעל.
בדוגמה (Figure 3.13), יש לבחור Always Retransfer.

**Register the Core Interface Queues:** ההפעלה הטכנית מ-Transaction SMQS (QOUT Scheduler) ו-SMQR (QIN Scheduler). נדרשת לעיבוד אוטומטי. לרישום outbound, הריצו SMQS, ולחצו Registration (Figure 3.14). הזינו Destination (ה-logical system של S/4HANA). ‏Max.Conn. (תהליכים מקבילים, ברירת-מחדל 10), ‏Max. Runtime (שניות, ברירת-מחדל 60). לחצו Continue. לרישום inbound, הריצו SMQR, ולחצו Registration (Figure 3.15). מכיוון שכל השמות מתחילים ב-"CF", הזינו "CF*" ב-Queue name. ה-Mode ברירת-מחדל D (dialog work processes). ‏Max. Runtime (30), ‏Attempts (10), ‏Pause (120 שניות). לחצו Continue.

sections.title: Transaction Data Transfer
sections.en: 3.2.3 Transaction Data Transfer In embedded PP/DS, the system internally uses the core interface framework for trans- ferring the transaction data between SAP S/4HANA and embedded PP/DS, which is why the basic core interface settings were required to be set up as detailed in the previous 3 Configuration 128 section. However, unlike the SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization system inte- gration, there is no need to create an integration model for the commonly used trans- action data for embedded PP/DS. The activation of the transaction data transfer is performed as a Customizing setting. To activate the transfer of transaction data, use the Customizing menu path, SAP IMG Menu  Advanced Planning  Basic Settings  Settings for Data Transfer. You’ll arrive at the screen shown in Figure 3.16, where you can select all the transaction data objects that need to be transferred between SAP S/4HANA and embedded PP/DS, and then click the Save button. Figure 3.16 Activation of Transaction Data Transfer in Embedded PP/DS Note The activation of the transaction data transfers as just explained, along with the acti- vation of the Advanced Planning checkbox in the material master, determine which transaction data is automatically transferred between SAP S/4HANA and embedded PP/DS. Material-independent transaction data, such as plant maintenance orders, requires an integration model creation and activation to transfer the data from SAP S/4HANA to embedded PP/DS. © 129 3.2 Basic Settings for Embedded PP/DS
sections.he:
ב-embedded PP/DS, המערכת משתמשת פנימית ב-core interface להעברת transaction data, ולכן נדרשו ההגדרות הבסיסיות. אך בשונה מ-SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization, אין צורך ב-integration model ל-transaction data הנפוץ. ההפעלה היא הגדרת Customizing. השתמשו ב-menu path: ‏SAP IMG Menu • Advanced Planning • Basic Settings • Settings for Data Transfer (Figure 3.16), בחרו את כל אובייקטי ה-transaction data, ולחצו Save.
**הערה:** ההפעלה, יחד עם ה-Advanced Planning checkbox ב-material master, קובעת איזה transaction data מועבר אוטומטית. ‏transaction data בלתי-תלוי-חומר (כגון plant maintenance orders) דורש יצירה והפעלה של integration model.

sections.title: Configuration Schema of the PP/DS System
sections.en: 3.2.4 Configuration Schema of the PP/DS System Configurable materials have classes and characteristics assigned that can be configured to set product specifications or characteristics when sales orders are entered or produc- tion orders are created. In the material master, the materials are marked as configurable, and the corresponding classes and characteristics are assigned. For the variant configu- ration (VC) scenario, a configuration profile is created and assigned to the material. Example A motorcycle with different body styles, engine capacities, and colors can be modeled as a configurable material so that at the time of order entry, the specific values for the characteristics (body style, capacity, and color) are selected. Embedded PP/DS supports configuration schemas similar to the SAP Advanced Plan- ning and Optimization system. As we touched on in Chapter 2, Section 2.6, the sup- ported configuration schema settings are as follows:  Characteristics-dependent planning (CDP) CDP is used in scenarios where the requirements, such as sales orders or PIRs, have the configuration values, and the system matches the configuration characteristics values to an existing supply element (e.g., planned order or production order) during planning. The system can also create a new receipt with the corresponding classification information to fulfill a demand. CDP can be used in make-to-stock (MTS) or make-to-order (MTO) scenarios. The CDP scenario uses class type 400 in PP/DS. Class types 300 and 023 are used in SAP S/4HANA, and they need to be trans- ferred to embedded PP/DS via an integration model. Upon transfer of these classes, class type 400 is created in embedded PP/DS.  Variant configuration (VC) VC is used in MTO scenarios, where the sales orders are created in SAP S/4HANA with the product configuration (assigned values for characteristics values), and the same is transferred to embedded PP/DS. Receipt elements, such as planned orders, are generated with the characteristics value in embedded PP/DS during the planning process. The configuration schema for embedded PP/DS is set via the configuration menu path, SAP IMG Menu  Advanced Planning  Basic Settings  Define Configuration Schema (CDP or Variant Configuration). Select the required Settings, as shown in Figure 3.17. The configuration schema is an editable field after the initial setting is made and saved, but it’s not recommended to switch the schema after transferring data from SAP S/4HANA to embedded PP/DS as this may lead to data inconsistencies with respect to the classification system data in embedded PP/DS. 3 Configuration 130 Figure 3.17 Setting Up the Configuration Schema in Embedded PP/DS
sections.he:
לחומרים configurable יש classes ו-characteristics להגדרת מפרטי מוצר בעת הזנת sales orders או יצירת production orders. ב-material master, החומרים מסומנים configurable וה-classes/characteristics מוקצים. ל-variant configuration (VC), נוצר configuration profile ומוקצה לחומר.
**דוגמה:** אופנוע עם body styles, engine capacities, וצבעים שונים ניתן למידול כ-configurable material, כך שבהזנת ה-order הערכים הספציפיים (body style, ‏capacity, color) נבחרים.
‏embedded PP/DS תומך בסכמות תצורה בדומה ל-SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization (פרק 2, סעיף 2.6):
• **Characteristics-dependent planning (CDP)** — לתרחישים שבהם לדרישות (sales orders או PIRs) יש ערכי תצורה, והמערכת מתאימה אותם ל-supply element קיים בתכנון. יכולה גם ליצור receipt חדש. ב-MTS או MTO. משתמש ב-class type 400. ‏class types 300 ו-023 משמשים ב-S/4HANA ויש להעבירם — בהעברה נוצר class type 400.
• **Variant configuration (VC)** — ב-MTO, שבו ה-sales orders נוצרים ב-S/4HANA עם תצורת המוצר ומועברים. אלמנטי receipt (planned orders) נוצרים עם ערך ה-characteristics בתכנון.
הסכמה נקבעת דרך menu path: ‏SAP IMG Menu • Advanced Planning • Basic Settings • Define Configuration Schema (CDP or Variant Configuration). בחרו את ההגדרות (Figure 3.17). השדה ניתן לעריכה לאחר ההגדרה הראשונית, אך לא מומלץ להחליף סכמה לאחר העברת נתונים (עלול להוביל לאי-עקביות).

sections.title: Global Parameters and Default Values
sections.en: 3.2.5 Global Parameters and Default Values PP/DS global parameters and default values are the parameters used by the PP/DS sys- tem when there is no overriding setting made in the master data or in the individual planning and scheduling tools. These parameters are delivered by default and can be changed depending on the usage of the PP/DS system. In this section, we’ll cover some of the important settings and their significance in the PP/DS system. Before setting up the global parameters and defaults, you need to create a number range for the PP/DS orders to be used within PP/DS. When planning is executed in PP/DS, the procurement elements such as planned orders and purchase requisitions will use this number range to generate PP/DS orders. When the embedded PP/DS order is trans- ferred to SAP S/4HANA, the number is assigned per the number range defined in the SAP S/4HANA side for the corresponding order object, such as the planned orders and purchase requisitions, and transferred back to PP/DS with the new SAP S/4HANA num- ber as part of the key completion. To create the PP/DS number range, use the Customizing menu path, SAP IMG Menu  Advanced Planning  Global Settings  Maintain Number Ranges for Orders. In the initial screen, click on the change Intervals button as shown in Figure 3.18 1. In the next screen, click on the Insert Line button 2; enter a Number Range No., From No., and To Number; and then save the transaction. You can execute Transaction /SAPAPO/RRPCUST1 or follow the Customizing menu path, SAP IMG Menu  Advanced Planning  Global Settings  Maintain Global Parame- ters and Defaults, to display and change the default delivered settings in the PP/DS global settings. The PP/DS global parameters are displayed in Figure 3.19. Logging determines the level of information generated in the application logs from the PP/DS planning and scheduling tools. There are three options available:  No Logging  Only Errors Terminations and Warnings  All Messages © 131 3.2 Basic Settings for Embedded PP/DS Figure 3.18 Creating Number Ranges for PP/DS Orders Figure 3.19 PP/DS Global Parameters and Default Values 3 Configuration 132 The Only Errors Terminations and Warnings option is recommended to avoid the log tables getting filled with PP/DS application log data quickly and requiring frequent reorganization jobs to delete the old log messages. However, the logging level can be changed from the planning tools to override this global setting. The Use Number Range checkbox makes the PP/DS system use a specific number range for the orders generated in the PP/DS transactions that aren’t yet synced up with SAP S/4HANA. If the PP/DS number range isn’t selected, the system will generate receipt elements without any external number, which means you can’t see an explicit order number in the PP/DS transactions. After the data is saved, the system syncs this order number with the SAP S/4HANA order number and updates the corresponding transac- tion screens. In embedded PP/DS, only the PDS is available as the source of supply for in-house man- ufacturing orders, so the value Production Data Structure Generated from R/3 is set by default for the Plan Explosion. The settings for the Transfer to R/3 In-House Production and Transfer to R/3 Ext. Pro- curement determine the timings of the transfer of the PP/DS orders to SAP S/4HANA when an order is created or changed in embedded PP/DS. The available options are as follows:  Don’t Create Transfer Events With this setting, the PP/DS orders aren’t transferred to SAP S/4HANA. For in-house production planned orders, if the orders aren’t available in SAP S/4HANA, no further planning of dependent components that aren’t set with advanced planning is possi- ble in SAP S/4HANA.  Create Transfer Events from Conversion Indicator With this setting, the orders are only transferred to embedded PP/DS when the con- version indicator is set to the order. For in-house production, the conversion indica- tor means the planned order will be converted to a production order; for external procurement, the purchase requisitions will be converted to purchase orders after the conversion indicator is set. Until the order is set with the conversion checkbox, it’s not available in SAP S/4HANA for planning any lower-level components that aren’t advanced planned.  Always Create Transfer Events (Default) This default setting is commonly used in planning and scheduling scenarios. With this setting, the planned orders and purchase requisitions created in embedded PP/DS are required to be available in SAP S/4HANA. This option will always transfer the orders to SAP S/4HANA when the orders are created or changed. Embedded PP/DS supports both dynamic and fixed pegging. Pegging is the relation- ship created between a receipt element, such as stocks, planned/production orders, purchase requisitions, and so on, and a requirement element, such as sales orders, PIRs, and so on. The system always creates a pegging relationship to dynamically link a receipt and requirement element, which is called dynamic pegging. © 133 3.2 Basic Settings for Embedded PP/DS With dynamic pegging, when the planning situation changes, the requirement ele- ment can be pegged to a new receipt element other than the originally pegged element if the original pegged element is no longer available. These dynamic pegging relation- ships can be changed to fixed pegging relationships in the PP/DS system. After a fixed pegging relationship is in place, the original pegging is retained as long as the supply element isn’t deleted, irrespective of the planning situation. When the supply elements, such as planned orders and purchase requisitions, are fixed pegged to the requirement element and the order is converted to production orders or purchase orders, the fixed pegging relationships are lost. If you want the fixed pegging to be retained even after the order conversion, set the Activate Fixed Pegging (Retain Fixed Pegging for Product on Document Change) accordingly. This setting can be over- ridden with the material master setting. You can change this setting in the material master by using Transaction MM02 for the material and plant and then navigating to the Advanced Planning tab, as shown in Figure 3.20. Figure 3.20 Material Level Fixed Pegging Setting in the Advanced Planning View A strategy profile is a collection of settings regarding how an order will be scheduled when it’s created, changed, or scheduled using PP/DS planning and scheduling tools. The individual planning and scheduling tools can have their own strategy profiles when you use those tools. But in the PP/DS global parameters under the Schedule 3 Configuration 134 Orders: Strategy Profiles section (refer to Figure 3.19), the default strategy profiles are maintained so that they can be used by default if the specific planning or scheduling tool or transaction doesn’t have an assigned strategy profile. In addition, the back- ground processes, such as transferring an order from SAP S/4HANA to embedded PP/DS, use these default strategies. Let’s move on to the ATP Categories tab in the PP/DS global settings and defaults. These settings map SAP S/4HANA–specific available-to-promise (ATP) elements (receipt and requirement) to the PP/DS-specific elements. For example, a planned order is repre- sented as category “PA” in SAP S/4HANA, and the same planned order, depending on if it’s firmed or ATP confirmed, will have a corresponding category in embedded PP/DS. As shown in Figure 3.21, for certain categories, such as planned orders and purchase req- uisitions, the default delivered category mapping can’t be changed, but for some ele- ments, it’s possible to map a different ATP category in embedded PP/DS other than the standard delivered mapping. In most cases, however, the standard delivered ATP cate- gory mapping is enough to execute the planning in embedded PP/DS. Figure 3.21 ATP Categories in PP/DS Global Settings and Defaults Tip The detailed mapping of the PP/DS and SAP S/4HANA ATP category mapping can be displayed from view /SAPAPO/V_ATP03 via Transaction SM30. © 135 3.2 Basic Settings for Embedded PP/DS
