sections.title: Transaction Data with Flexible Integration
sections.en: 4.11 Transaction Data with Flexible Integration Flexible integration is the ability to define how SAP S/4HANA transaction data is inte- grated with PP/DS and what kind of changes are allowed or not allowed for the transac- tion data within PP/DS, which is determined in the Scope Limitation field in the Advanced Planning tab of the material master. We’ve already discussed the basic con- cept of this scope limitation in Chapter 2, Section 2.3. In this section, we’ll cover how the transaction data behaves with the different scope limitation options. Following are the scope limitation options and how they influence the transaction data within PP/DS:  1 PP/DS Display Only With this scope limitation, as shown in Figure 4.29 1, all the transaction data is transferred to PP/DS, including in-house and external procurement orders. But within PP/DS, no change is allowed for any of the transaction data, including any manual or automated planning/scheduling runs changing the transaction data. All the transaction data changes are managed within SAP S/4HANA with this scope lim- itation. In the product view in PP/DS (Transaction /SAPAPO/RRP3), in change mode, all the transaction data is available in display only mode 2. The scope limitation configuration is already discussed in Chapter 2, Section 2.3. Figure 4.29 Scope Limitation: 1 PP/DS Display Only © 209 4.11 Transaction Data with Flexible Integration  2 PP/DS Restricted for Inhouse Only With this scope limitation as shown in Figure 4.30 1, all the transaction data, includ- ing in-house and external procurement orders, is integrated to PP/DS. However, within PP/DS, only the in-house procurement elements (planned orders and manu- facturing orders with certain statuses) can be changed, and automated or interactive planning 2 and scheduling can create and change existing in-house procurement orders. The external procurement elements, such as purchase requirements, are respected as valid procurement elements for planning but can’t be changed or deleted either manually 3 or via automated planning runs. In addition, in interac- tive or automated planning runs, only the heuristics, which is part of the scope pro- file 4 defined in the material master, is allowed within PP/DS. Figure 4.30 Scope Limitation: 2 PP/DS Restricted for Inhouse Only  3 PP/DS Restricted As shown in Figure 4.31 1, with this scope limitation, all transaction data is inte- grated to PP/DS from SAP S/4HANA. Within PP/DS, manual change is allowed for in- house 2 and external procurement 3 elements. However, for automated planning runs, it’s only possible to execute heuristics that are part of the scope profile 4. If you attempt to execute a heuristic that isn’t part of the scope profile, an error is raised, and the execution of the heuristics will be terminated 5. 4 Data Transfer for Transaction Data 210 Figure 4.31 Scope Limitation: 3 PP/DS Restricted  4 PP/DS Entire Scope for Inhouse Only With this scope limitation option shown in Figure 4.32 1, all the in-house and exter- nal procurement elements are integrated from SAP S/4HANA to PP/DS. Figure 4.32 Scope Limitation: 4 PP/DS Entire Scope for Inhouse Only © 211
sections.he:
‏flexible integration היא היכולת להגדיר כיצד transaction data של S/4HANA משולב עם PP/DS ואילו שינויים מותרים, הנקבעת בשדה Scope Limitation בלשונית Advanced Planning (פרק 2, סעיף 2.3). בסעיף זה — כיצד ה-transaction data מתנהג עם האפשרויות:
• **1 PP/DS Display Only** — (Figure 4.29) כל ה-transaction data מועבר (in-house ו-external), אך אין שינוי מותר ב-PP/DS (ידני או אוטומטי). כל השינויים מנוהלים ב-S/4HANA. ב-product view במצב change, הכל בתצוגה-בלבד.
• **2 PP/DS Restricted for Inhouse Only** — (Figure 4.30) כל ה-transaction data משולב, אך רק אלמנטי in-house procurement (planned orders ו-manufacturing orders בסטטוסים מסוימים) ניתנים לשינוי, ותכנון/תזמון אוטומטי או אינטראקטיבי יכול ליצור/לשנותם. ה-external procurement מכובדים כתקפים אך אינם ניתנים לשינוי/מחיקה. בנוסף, רק ה-heuristics ב-scope profile מותרים.
• **3 PP/DS Restricted** — (Figure 4.31) כל ה-transaction data משולב. שינוי ידני מותר ל-in-house ו-external. אך לריצות אוטומטיות, רק heuristics ב-scope profile. ניסיון להריץ heuristic שאינו ב-profile מעלה שגיאה ומסיים את ההרצה.
• **4 PP/DS Entire Scope for Inhouse Only** — (Figure 4.32) כל אלמנטי ה-in-house וה-external משולבים.

sections.title: Initial Transfer and Retransfer of Transaction Data to PP/DS
sections.en: 4.12 Initial Transfer and Retransfer of Transaction Data to PP/DS But within PP/DS, only the in-house procurement elements 2 can be changed man- ually or through automated planning and scheduling runs. There is no limitation applied for the possible list of heuristics that can be executed. In addition, all the automated planning and scheduling runs can only create/change/delete in-house procurement elements. The external procurement elements 3 are in display only mode in PP/DS and considered as a valid receipt in the planning runs. With no scope limitation set in the material master, all the transaction data will be integrated to PP/DS from SAP S/4HANA, and no restrictions are applied within PP/DS. Manual and automated planning runs can create/change/delete both in-house and external procurement orders in PP/DS. 4.12 Initial Transfer and Retransfer of Transaction Data to PP/DS In an operational SAP S/4HANA system where your logistics and manufacturing pro- cesses are already being leveraged, if you decide to activate PP/DS and set the Advanced Planning flag for materials, you’ll need to do an initial transfer of the transaction data from SAP S/4HANA to PP/DS. In addition, in cases where you have to delete the transaction data in PP/DS using appropriate processes and transactions (e.g., inconsistent data which isn’t correctable), you need to perform a retransfer of the transaction data from SAP S/4HANA to PP/DS. ABAP program /SAPAPO/PPDS_DELTA_ORD_TRANS can be used for the initial transfer and retransfer of the transaction data. There is no difference between initial and retransfer; this program reads all the SAP S/4HANA transaction data and transfers the data to PP/DS. For transaction/master data objects requiring the core interface integra- tion model, program RIMODINI can be used to do an initial transfer, and program RIMODAC2 can be used to do a delta transfer. To trigger an initial transfer of the transaction data objects that doesn’t require an inte- gration model, execute Transaction SE38, enter the program name “/SAPAPO/PPDS_ DELTA_ORD_TRANS”, and execute. In the next screen, you’ll have the option to enter the material number and plant for which the relevant transaction data needs to be transferred to PP/DS, as shown in Figure 4.33. Under the Parallelized Transfer sub- screen, the Parallelize Selection in S4 System checkbox determines if the selection of data in the SAP S/4HANA side is executed in a parallel processing mode. When this checkbox is selected, in the SAP S/4HANA side, the transaction data is read in parallel. The packet size (how many objects are read at once) for reading the data is determined by the Customizing settings made in Transaction CFC3. The Absolute Max. No. Pro- cesses or the Relative Max. No. Processes, along with the corresponding Server Group will determine how many parallel processes can be executed in the SAP S/4HANA side to select the data. The Parallel Processing in PPDS checkbox determines if the data pack- ets as selected in the SAP S/4HANA side are processed in parallel in the PP/DS side. 4 Data Transfer for Transaction Data 212 Figure 4.33 PP/DS Delta Transfer Report When the Parallelize Selection in S4 System is activated, the defined number of work processes can be leveraged in the SAP S/4HANA side. Without parallel processing, only one work process will be used by the system to select the data in SAP S/4HANA. As shown in Figure 4.34, when parallel processing is activated for SAP S/4HANA selection, multiple work processes 1 are executed in the system to select the SAP S/4HANA data, whereas when it’s switched off, only one work process 2 is leveraged by the system. The work processes can be displayed from Transaction SM66. Figure 4.34 Parallel Selection and Processing versus Serial Selection and Processing: Work Processes © 213 4.12 Initial Transfer and Retransfer of Transaction Data to PP/DS In addition, as shown in Figure 4.35, when Parallelize Processing in PP/DS is activated, multiple core interface queues 3 are generated by the system to process the data in parallel in PP/DS. When Parallel Processing in PP/DS is switched off, only one core inter- face queue 4 is generated, and all the transaction data objects are processed by just using one core interface queue. The inbound core interface queues can be displayed from Transaction SMQ2. Figure 4.35 Parallel Processing versus Serial Processing: Core Interface Queues This program transfers all transaction data that is activated in the configuration of the data transfer under advanced planning. However, you can transfer only specific objects such as sales orders, stock, planned orders, and so on, in Transaction SE38 by entering the program name “/SAPAPO/PPDS_DELTA_ORD_TRANS” and executing. As shown in Figure 4.36, enter the material and plant selection 1. Then, in the dropdown field in the header, enter “ORD_TYP” 2 and press (Enter). This opens new selection options in the Order Types for Transfer area 3. Now, you can unselect the transaction data objects that you don’t want to retransfer to PP/DS. This option is useful when you want to retrans- fer specific transaction data for a large number of materials to PP/DS and want to avoid all other transaction data being transferred, which is a performance-intensive action. 4 Data Transfer for Transaction Data 214 Figure 4.36 Object-Specific Retransfer of Transaction Data

sections.title: Summary
sections.en: 4.13 Summary In this chapter, we covered the important transaction data aspects during the integra- tion between SAP S/4HANA and embedded PP/DS. We also discussed the details of in-house manufacturing orders, external procurement orders, stocks, batches, sales orders, PIRs, inspection lots, plant maintenance orders, and production campaigns, as well as how the restriction mode impacts the processing of transaction data within PP/DS. Out of these, for the material-independent objects, there is a need to create and activate integration models, and for the other material- dependent transaction data objects, the transfer of data between SAP S/4HANA and embedded PP/DS is activated in Customizing. For the commonly used transaction data objects, such as the planned orders, produc- tion orders, purchase requisitions, and purchase orders, the data is transferred via syn- chronous RFC transfer from PP/DS to SAP S/4HANA, which minimizes the effort required to monitor the SAP S/4HANA inbound queues, and the errors are entered in the PP/DS planning logs. In addition, we covered how you can do an initial transfer and retransfer of transaction data from SAP S/4HANA to PP/DS. © 215 4.13 Summary We’ll cover the technical aspects of the transaction data within SAP liveCache in Chap- ter 10, where we’ll discuss administration of embedded PP/DS, including SAP live- Cache. So far, we’ve covered the basic required and commonly used configuration, master data, and transaction data details. In the next chapter, we’ll discuss how the production planning functionality is executed in embedded PP/DS. ©

sections.title: Determining When PP/DS Should Be Used for Planning
sections.en: 5.1 Determining When PP/DS Should Be Used for Planning In classic MRP, the basic concept is to fulfill the requirements with receipt elements by performing a net requirements calculation and calculation of the dates and quantities for the receipt elements per the set master data and Customizing settings. In addition, this process selects the source of supply for the receipt elements per the master data setup, such as quota arrangements and rules, validity dates, and lot sizes defined. The MRP functionality in SAP S/4HANA works with a set algorithm and provides flexibility in defining the MRP types that determine how the requirements and receipts are pro- cessed during the planning run, the lot sizing procedures that determine the quantity of the receipt elements, and various Customizing settings that can be used by the MRP algorithm during the planning run to handle planning situations. The MRP process guarantees material availability by balancing the inventory and receipts against the requirements. If your manufacturing and procurement processes require more sophisticated features to optimize the plan, then the PP/DS planning brings in a lot of features covering requirements across industries and processes. The basic decision to use PP/DS plan- ning depends on whether the material is critical to the supply chain and/or if the mate- rial is manufactured in a bottleneck resource. Let’s walk through some of the specific functions required in the planning process that PP/DS can support and that aren’t available in the SAP S/4HANA planning process, such as MRP:  Capacity-constrained production plan SAP S/4HANA MRP doesn’t consider the capacity of the resources on which the receipt orders are going to be manufactured or handled. If a resource-constrained production plan is required, PP/DS can support this via the Production Planning Optimizer. The production plan isn’t generally required to be constrained with the resource availability, but the Production Planning Optimizer can support a com- bined PP/DS optimization process. In scenarios where the PP/DS bucket capacity is used, finite capacity planning can be performed using planning heuristics.  Shelf-life planning PP/DS can be used if your materials are handled in batch management with shelf life defined, and you want the planning process to consider the shelf life. In PP/DS, the planning algorithm can consider the maturity time of the products received, the © 219 5.1 Determining When PP/DS Should Be Used for Planning shelf life of the product, and the requirements of the maximum and minimum shelf life required to fulfill the requirements. The shelf life also can be propagated throughout the order levels when there are multilevel orders present that handle materials with shelf life.  Variable lot sizes In MRP, the lot sizing throughout the planning horizon is defined in the material master lot sizing procedure if you want to plan using different lot sizes for short-, medium-, and long-term horizons so that the supply elements are planned to the granular lot size level, such as daily for the short term and a more aggregated weekly or monthly for the medium term or long term. Materials that have such require- ments are supported by PP/DS to achieve the desired results.  Characteristics-dependent planning (CDP) In MRP, the planning run only considers the quantity during planning and can’t ensure that components with the same characteristics values are netted against the demand elements that have characteristics values assigned to them. But with PP/DS CDP, you can make sure the characteristics matching is executed during planning, and new receipt elements are created to fulfill the demand of the requirement ele- ments with characteristics if there are no existing receipts with the same character- istics value available to fulfill the demand.  Realignment of supply and demand In MRP in SAP S/4HANA, the planning is unidirectional and recursive only if the master data setup requires such planning. Therefore, after the MRP execution, it’s possible that there are delays and earliness of receipts in covering the requirement elements. The MRP exceptions or the MRP Live cockpit needs to be reviewed manu- ally to actively address these situations. With PP/DS, functionalities such as top- down and bottom-up rescheduling can be used to realign the demand and receipt elements. PP/DS can be used for critical materials for which the alignment of the demand and supply needs to be ensured through the order network.  Optimization Critical materials, which require optimization from a production plan, and the scheduling perspective, needs to be planned by PP/DS, the Production Planning Optimizer, and the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer, or a combined PP/DS optimizer execution can be used to optimize the plan and schedule to arrive at an optimal plan and reduce setup costs and times, reduce delays, and optimize the production plan and schedule based on the costs defined for the Production Planning Optimizer and the objective functions defined for the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer.  Multistep planning The PP/DS planning run need not be just a one-step planning execution like MRP. In one planning run, multiple steps can be defined to execute multiple planning algo- rithms in sequence. For example, MRP PP/DS heuristics can be followed by a top- down or bottom-up rescheduling heuristics to realign the newly created and 5 Production Planning 220 changed receipts from the MRP heuristic. Scheduling heuristics or even an opti- mizer run can be scheduled in one planning run. Materials requiring such special planning and scheduling apart from MRP in SAP ERP should be activated for advanced planning.  Push production In push production in PP/DS, if materials with shorter shelf life are received or pro- duced in excess, they should be used up in producing materials with longer shelf life. This is applicable in food, dairy, chemical, and pharma industries. Such materials can be activated for PP/DS planning, so that they can be processed with PP/DS push pro- duction to avoid wastage of raw materials. PP/DS push production can identify the materials that can be produced using the expiring materials based in the production data structure (PDS) master data setup, and the planners can interactively plan the quantity of such material to be produced.  Product interchangeability PP/DS supports simple discontinuation, so if there are materials that are discontin- ued and being replaced by new materials, certain PP/DS planning heuristics can sup- port this by using up the old material before the requirements are passed on to the new material. Updating the master data, such as bills of material (BOMs) and PDSs, is the right way to handle material changes in production; however, during the interim, when there is existing stock available for the old material, PP/DS inter- changeability can be used for such materials to support the transition from the old to new material without causing wastage of the old product inventory.  Industry-specific functions PP/DS supports certain industry-specific functions such as order combinations where multiple orders going through the same operation can be combined, and a new order is created to simplify and optimize the planning and execution processes. As many of the industry solutions, such as discrete industry and mill products (DIMP), are part of the SAP S/4HANA core, PP/DS can be used to leverage the indus- try functions in SAP S/4HANA, which can be further optimized using PP/DS plan- ning and scheduling functions.  Alerts-based monitoring The MRP process in SAP ERP works based on exceptions in the planning situation that are preconfigured in the system. Limited options are available to enhance the exception management of MRP in SAP ERP. With MRP Live in SAP S/4HANA, the MRP cockpit is a set of SAP Fiori apps that provide more insights into the planning situa- tion based on key performance indicator (KPI) applications, which are based on mate- rial coverage and capacity consumption. PP/DS brings in a much more sophisticated alert framework that is customizable to add the tolerances for the alerts and can be embedded into almost all the planning and scheduling tools. The alerts can be config- ured for receipts, requirements, pegging, shelf life, capacity consumption, and so on, and the materials activated for advanced planning in SAP S/4HANA can leverage the Alert Monitor in PP/DS to manage the exceptions in planning and scheduling. © 221
sections.he:
ב-classic MRP, המושג הבסיסי הוא מילוי הדרישות ב-receipt elements ע"י net requirements calculation וחישוב תאריכים וכמויות לפי ה-master data וה-Customizing. בנוסף, התהליך בוחר source of supply לפי המאסטר (quota arrangements, ‏rules, ‏validity dates, ‏lot sizes). פונקציית ה-MRP ב-S/4HANA עובדת עם אלגוריתם קבוע ומספקת גמישות בהגדרת ה-MRP types, ‏lot sizing procedures, והגדרות Customizing. תהליך ה-MRP מבטיח זמינות חומר ע"י איזון מלאי ו-receipts מול דרישות.
אם תהליכי הייצור והרכש דורשים תכונות מתוחכמות יותר למיטוב, ‏PP/DS מביא תכונות רבות. ההחלטה הבסיסית להשתמש ב-PP/DS תלויה אם החומר קריטי ל-supply chain ו/או מיוצר ב-bottleneck resource. פונקציות ספציפיות הנתמכות ב-PP/DS שאינן ב-MRP:
• **Capacity-constrained production plan** — ‏MRP אינו מתחשב בקיבולת. ל-plan מוגבל-קיבולת, ‏PP/DS תומך דרך Production Planning Optimizer. בתרחישים עם PP/DS bucket capacity, ניתן finite capacity planning בעזרת planning heuristics.
• **Shelf-life planning** — אם חומרים מנוהלים ב-batch management עם shelf life, ‏PP/DS מתחשב ב-maturity time, ‏shelf life, ודרישות ה-shelf life המרבי והמינימלי. ה-shelf life ניתן להפצה על-פני רמות ה-order.
• **Variable lot sizes** — ב-MRP, ה-lot sizing לאורך ה-horizon מוגדר ב-material master. אם רוצים lot sizes שונים לטווח קצר/בינוני/ארוך (יומי לקצר, שבועי/חודשי לבינוני/ארוך), ‏PP/DS תומך.
• **Characteristics-dependent planning (CDP)** — ב-MRP, רק הכמות נחשבת. ב-PP/DS CDP, ה-characteristics matching מבוצע בתכנון, ו-receipts חדשים נוצרים אם אין קיימים בעלי אותו ערך.
• **Realignment of supply and demand** — ב-MRP, התכנון חד-כיווני. ב-PP/DS, ‏top-down ו-bottom-up rescheduling ליישור הביקוש וה-receipts. שימושי לחומרים קריטיים.
• **Optimization** — חומרים קריטיים הדורשים מיטוב מתוכננים ע"י PP/DS, ‏Production Planning Optimizer, ו-Detailed Scheduling Optimizer (או ריצה משולבת) לצמצום עלויות וזמני setup, הפחתת עיכובים, ומיטוב התוכנית והתזמון.
• **Multistep planning** — ריצת PP/DS אינה צריכה להיות צעד יחיד כמו MRP. בריצה אחת ניתן להגדיר צעדים מרובים (אלגוריתמים ברצף). למשל, ‏MRP PP/DS heuristics ואחריו top-down/bottom-up rescheduling, ‏scheduling heuristics, או optimizer.
• **Push production** — אם חומרים עם shelf life קצר מתקבלים/מיוצרים בעודף, יש להשתמש בהם לייצור חומרים עם shelf life ארוך (מזון, חלב, כימיה, פארמה). ‏PP/DS push production מזהה חומרים הניתנים לייצור מהחומרים הפגים לפי ה-PDS.
• **Product interchangeability** — ‏PP/DS תומך ב-simple discontinuation; אם חומרים מופסקים ומוחלפים, ‏heuristics מסוימים משתמשים בישן לפני העברת הדרישות לחדש.
• **Industry-specific functions** — כגון order combinations (איחוד orders דרך אותה operation). פתרונות תעשייה כגון discrete industry and mill products (DIMP) הם חלק מליבת S/4HANA.
• **Alerts-based monitoring** — תהליך ה-MRP ב-SAP ERP עובד על exceptions מוגדרים-מראש. עם MRP Live, ה-MRP cockpit (אפליקציות Fiori) מספק תובנות מבוססות-KPI. ‏PP/DS מביא alert framework מתוחכם הניתן להתאמה (tolerances) ומשובץ בכל הכלים. ה-alerts ניתנים להגדרה ל-receipts, ‏requirements, ‏pegging, ‏shelf life, ‏capacity consumption.

sections.title: Basic Functions in PP/DS Planning
sections.en: 5.2 Basic Functions in PP/DS Planning  Planning simulations In PP/DS, the interactive planning tools such as the product view or the product planning table are always launched in simulation mode, so that you can interac- tively change the procurement elements and see the effect of the changes on the inventory and capacity situation in simulation before you finalize the plan by saving the changes you made in the interactive planning tools. 5.2 Basic Functions in PP/DS Planning In this section, we’ll cover the basic concepts in production planning within PP/DS. These concepts are used widely by most of the planning heuristics and planning pro- cesses in PP/DS. The basic task of any planning tool is to consider the receipt elements and the requirement elements, and then perform a net requirements calculation. Then, based on the delta quantity and the dates on which the net quantity falls below zero, the planning tools should create a receipt element based on the quantity restrictions (lot sizes) maintained in the master data. In addition, this section will cover the terminology used in the PP/DS planning process. We’ve covered the planning procedures and day’s supply calculation in Chapter 3, where we discussed the configuration. In this section, we’ll cover the details about peg- ging, net requirements calculation, target stock levels, safety stock methods, and source of supply selection concepts.
sections.he:
• **Planning simulations** — ב-PP/DS, הכלים האינטראקטיביים (product view או product planning table) תמיד מופעלים ב-simulation mode, כך שניתן לשנות אלמנטי procurement ולראות את ההשפעה על המלאי והקיבולת בסימולציה לפני שמירה.
בסעיף זה נכסה מושגי הליבה ב-production planning ב-PP/DS, המשמשים את רוב ה-heuristics. המשימה הבסיסית: התחשבות ב-receipt וב-requirement elements, ‏net requirements calculation, ויצירת receipt לפי הגבלות הכמות (lot sizes). כיסינו planning procedures ו-day's supply בפרק 3. כאן — ‏pegging, ‏net requirements calculation, ‏target stock levels, ‏safety stock methods, ו-source of supply selection.

sections.title: Pegging
sections.en: 5.2.1 Pegging Pegging in PP/DS is used to signify the relationship or the link between a receipt (sup- ply) and a requirement (demand) element. By doing so for all the material BOM levels, the overall lead time for the finished material can be calculated. If there are any delays in fulfilling the requirements generated at any level of the BOM by the demand for the finished material, these delays can be identified, and an alert can be generated accord- ingly. The pegging process is executed by the system after every planning run and after any planning-relevant change in data, so that the receipt and requirements elements are linked at all times. The alerts also can be determined when any planning tool is being loaded with the planning data for any product location. PP/DS supports two kinds of pegging relationships:  Dynamic pegging In dynamic pegging, the system creates the pegging relationship between the sup- ply and demand element based on the current planning situation. If there is a change, or a new receipt or requirement is created manually or by the system in the planning process, the pegging relationship will be recalculated and re-created. 5 Production Planning 222 Under dynamic pegging, there are two pegging strategies available in the standard system, which can be set in the material master Advanced Planning view via the Peg- ging Strategy field: – Use Timely Receipts With this pegging strategy, the system goes through the requirement elements in chronological order of the date and time of the requirement. It then checks for the receipt element, which is closer to the date and time of the requirement element and assigns the receipt (creates pegging) to the requirement element. If one receipt element isn’t able to fulfill the requirement element, it checks for further receipt elements closer to the requirement element and creates the pegging. – Use Earliest Receipts (first in first out) With the first in, first out (FIFO) pegging strategy, the requirement elements and receipt elements are sorted by their date and time. Then, the earliest require- ments are assigned (pegged) to the earliest receipt elements. The pegging relationships can be displayed from the Pegging Overview tab of the product view transaction (Transaction /SAPAPO/RRP3). In addition, Transaction /SAPAPO/PEG1, directly loads the Pegging Overview tab of the product view. As shown in Figure 5.1, the Pegging Strategy 1 is assigned in the material master Advanced Planning view. The receipt elements 2 (planned orders – PlOrd.) and requirement element (forecast – FC req.) 3 in the product view are also shown. Figure 5.1 Pegging Strategy: Example As shown in Figure 5.2, with the Pegging Strategy 01 - Use Earliest Receipts, the sys- tem selects the earliest receipt element in the list of available receipts and assigns it to the requirement element. In this example, the first planned order is on 25.12.2022, so the system creates pegging between the first demand element on 01.01.2023 and the first planned order (PlOrd.) on 25.12.2022 1. With Pegging Strategy 00 (or blank value) – Use Timely Receipts, the system searches for a receipt element from the demand date (01.01.2023) in the backward © 223 5.2 Basic Functions in PP/DS Planning direction and the first element available to fulfill the demand is used to create the pegging relationship. In this example, the first receipt element closer to the demand date is the planned order (PlOrd.) on 31.12.2022. So, the demand date 01.01.2023 is pegged to the planned order on 31.12.2022 2. Figure 5.2 Pegging Strategy Example: Earliest Receipts versus Timely Receipts Note If there are stock elements present for the product/location in PP/DS, and if the earliest requirements can be covered by the stock elements irrespective of the pegging strat- egy, the stocks will be pegged to the early requirements.  Fixed pegging In fixed pegging, the dynamic pegging relationship created can be fixed so that any future planning situation change won’t alter the fixed pegging relationship. Manu- ally created fixed pegging can’t be changed or deleted by the system automatically during production planning, but the fixed pegging relationship created by the sys- tem during a planning run can be later changed in a subsequent planning run. How- ever, a mere change in the planning situation won’t change the fixed pegging relationship created by the system. Fixed pegging can be created via execution of the fixed pegging heuristics (covered in Section 5.4.4) or can be created manually from the Pegging Overview tab of the product view Transaction /SAPAPO/RRP3. As shown in Figure 5.3, you can select a row from the list of dynamic pegging relationships 1 and click on the Fix Complete 5 Production Planning 224 Quantity button 2 to create a fixed pegging of the complete dynamic pegging quan- tity. To partially fix peg a receipt element to a requirement element in the FixPegQty column 3, enter the quantity that you want the system to create fixed pegging for, and the remaining quantity will remain dynamically pegged. In this example, 25 out of the 100 dynamically pegged quantity were set for fixed pegging, so the remaining 75 remains with dynamic pegging. Figure 5.3 Fixed Pegging Options in the PP/DS Product View In the Pegging Type column 4, the system displays the nature of the pegging rela- tionship. Following are the possible values for this column: – D: Dynamic pegging. – M: Manually created fixed pegging relationship. – A: Automatically created fixed pegging using a heuristics or Business Application Programming Interface (BAPI). – C: Combined fixed pegging relationship. This could be a partial quantity dynami- cally pegged and the remaining quantity fixed pegged manually and/or a fixed pegged quantity using a heuristic or a BAPI. – Blank: No pegging has been created yet for the requirement element. To delete the fixed pegging interactively, select the relevant rows from the list of pegging relationships, and click on the Delete Fixed Pegging button 5. Once created, fixed pegging can stay intact when the document type changes. For example, if a sales order is fixed pegged to a planned order, the fixed pegging still can stay intact to the sales order even after converting the planned order to a production order. This is controlled by the configuration in the PP/DS global settings (Transaction /SAPAPO/RRPCUST1) and the settings in the material master. This is covered in Chapter 3, Section 3.2.5. © 225 5.2 Basic Functions in PP/DS Planning Tip The business add-in (BAdI) /SAPAPO/RRP_HEUR_DO can be used to create fixed pegging relationships during a PP/DS MRP run. However, the standard method for creating a fixed pegging relationship in planning is to execute the heuristics for creating fixed pegging as a subsequent step after the planning heuristics in the PP/DS planning run. For the pegging to be executed between a receipt and requirement element, the follow- ing conditions must be met:  Same pegging area The pegging area is the combination of a product and a location in a planning ver- sion with the account assignment if relevant. For example, for a make-to-stock (MTS) material in a plant, the pegging area in the active planning version 000 is the combination of the material and the location. For a make-to-order (MTO) material, every sales order from the customers forms a customer segment, and apart from the material and location, the sales order (as an account assignment object) also becomes a part of the pegging area. The receipt and requirement elements should be part of the same pegging area for them to get pegged to each other.  Pegging interval The receipt elements, including the stock elements, will be pegged to the require- ment element if they are within the pegging interval. The pegging interval is set by default as 277,000 hours, which is approximately 31.6 years. This is the maximum value technically allowed for this field. So, in embedded PP/DS, the pegging interval is a rolling defaulted 31.6 years (calculated from the requirement element date) and can’t be changed in the material master, as shown in Figure 5.4. Figure 5.4 Default Values of Pegging Interval in the PP/DS Product Master 5 Production Planning 226 Following are a few other settings in the material master that influence the way the pegging relationships are created:  Avoid Alerts When the Avoid Alerts checkbox in the material master is activated in the Advanced Planning tab, the system will respect the pegging strategy assigned, but will try to avoid violating the Alert Threshold for Earliness and Alert Threshold for Lateness. The alert threshold is defined in number of hours (up to six digits) and minutes (two digits). For example, a value of 50000:10 in these fields means 50,000 hours and 10 minutes. These threshold values must be less than the overall pegging interval, which is 277000 hours. In this example, as shown in Figure 5.5, the pegging strategy is 1 Earliest Receipt (FIFO) 1; with this strategy, the first requirement element on 03.03.2023 2 should be pegged to the earliest receipt planned order on 31.12.2022 3, but the difference in the date/time between these two elements exceeds the value set in the Threshold for Maximum Earliness, which is 48 hours 4. As the Avoid Alerts checkbox is selected, the system searches for another receipt element that is within the threshold. Another receipt element on 02.03.2023 5 is acceptable, so the requirement is pegged to the planned order on 02.03.2023 6. If there are no compatible receipt ele- ments respecting the thresholds, the system will follow the pegging strategy and will peg the earliest receipt element. Figure 5.5 Influence of Avoid Alerts in Pegging  Use Total Receipt/Use Total Stock When the Use Total Receipt and/or Use Total Stock checkbox is selected in the mate- rial master Advanced Planning view, during pegging, the system ensures that the one receipt element (it’s whole quantity) is assigned to only one requirement element. © 227 5.2 Basic Functions in PP/DS Planning That is, one receipt element can’t be pegged by more than one requirement element. The same applies to stock as well. In the example shown in Figure 5.6, there are two receipt elements 1, one stock ele- ment with 50 quantities and a planned order for 100 quantities. There are six requirement elements, which are forecasts for 25 quantities each 2. With Pegging Strategy 1 - Earliest Receipts (FIFO) 3, all of these requirement elements can be pegged to the existing receipt elements. But when Use Total Receipts and Use Total Stock 4 are activated in the material master, the system looks for exact quantities of requirement elements that can be pegged to the receipt elements (planned order and stock). As there are no such requirement elements, no pegging is created 5. Figure 5.6 Influence of Use Total Receipts and Use Total Stock Checkboxes on Pegging With the activation of Use Total Receipts and/or Use Total Requirements settings in the material master, thresholds can be applied on the receipt quantity, which is allowed to be pegged to a requirement element. The threshold is set in the under/ overdelivery tolerance values in the material master. As shown in Figure 5.7, in this example, the overdelivery tolerance (Overdely tol.) is set as 25% 1 in the Work scheduling view 2 of the material master. This means if there is a receipt element’s quantity (in our example, the stock element with 50 quantities 3) that is up to 25% more than the demand element (the forecast requirement for 40 quantities 4), the system can peg this receipt element to the requirement element 5. In addition, if there are no other requirement elements that are within the 25% tolerance of the other receipt element planned order for 100 quantities, this planned order isn’t pegged to any of the requirements. 5 Production Planning 228 Figure 5.7 Underdelivery and Overdelivery Tolerance for Use Total Receipts and Use Total Stock Checkboxes in Pegging In CDP scenarios, the characteristics values of the receipt and requirement elements are checked for compatibility for creating pegging relationships. For products that have a defined shelf life, minimum required shelf life, and matura- tion time after production, the dynamic pegging considers these values to make sure that when they are pegged to the requirement element, it’s out of the maturity period of the product and complies with the minimum required shelf life.
sections.he:
‏pegging ב-PP/DS מסמן את הקשר בין receipt (supply) ל-requirement (demand). בכך בכל רמות ה-BOM, ניתן לחשב את ה-lead time הכולל. עיכובים במילוי דרישות בכל רמה ניתנים לזיהוי ול-alert. ה-pegging מבוצע לאחר כל ריצה ולאחר כל שינוי רלוונטי, כך שהאלמנטים מקושרים תמיד. שני סוגי pegging:
• **Dynamic pegging** — המערכת יוצרת את ה-pegging לפי המצב הנוכחי. בשינוי, ה-pegging מחושב-מחדש. שתי אסטרטגיות ב-Pegging Strategy של ה-material master (Advanced Planning view):
– **Use Timely Receipts** — עובר על הדרישות בסדר כרונולוגי ובודק receipt הקרוב לתאריך ומקצה.
– **Use Earliest Receipts (FIFO)** — הדרישות וה-receipts ממוינים לפי תאריך; המוקדם מוקצה למוקדם.
ה-pegging ניתן להצגה מלשונית Pegging Overview של ה-product view (Transaction /SAPAPO/RRP3), או Transaction /SAPAPO/PEG1. כפי שב-Figure 5.1, ה-Pegging Strategy מוקצה ב-material master, וה-receipt elements (planned orders – PlOrd.) וה-requirement (forecast – FC req.) מוצגים. עם Pegging Strategy 01 - Use Earliest Receipts (Figure 5.2), המערכת בוחרת את ה-receipt המוקדם (planned order ב-25.12.2022 ל-demand ב-01.01.2023). עם Pegging Strategy 00 (או ריק) – Use Timely Receipts, המערכת מחפשת אחורה מתאריך הדרישה (ה-planned order ב-31.12.2022).
**הערה:** אם קיימים stock elements ואם המוקדמות ניתנות לכיסוי ע"י ה-stock ללא קשר לאסטרטגיה, ה-stocks pegged למוקדמות.
• **Fixed pegging** — ה-dynamic pegging ניתן לקיבוע כך ששינוי עתידי לא ישנה אותו. ‏fixed pegging ידני אינו ניתן לשינוי/מחיקה אוטומטית; ה-fixed שנוצר ע"י המערכת בריצה ניתן לשינוי בריצה הבאה. שינוי מצב לבדו לא ישנה fixed pegging שנוצר ע"י המערכת. ניתן ליצור דרך fixed pegging heuristics (סעיף 5.4.4) או ידנית מלשונית Pegging Overview (Figure 5.3) — בחרו שורה ולחצו Fix Complete Quantity, או הזינו כמות ב-FixPegQty לקיבוע חלקי. עמודת ה-Pegging Type:
– D: Dynamic pegging.
– M: Manually created fixed pegging.
– A: Automatically created fixed pegging (heuristics או BAPI).
– C: Combined fixed pegging.
– ריק: טרם נוצר pegging.
למחיקה אינטראקטיבית, בחרו שורות ולחצו Delete Fixed Pegging. ‏fixed pegging יכול להישאר בשינוי סוג מסמך (sales order fixed pegged ל-planned order נשאר גם לאחר המרה ל-production order). נשלט ב-global settings (Transaction /SAPAPO/RRPCUST1) וב-material master (פרק 3, סעיף 3.2.5).
**טיפ:** ה-BAdI /SAPAPO/RRP_HEUR_DO ליצירת fixed pegging בריצת MRP. אך השיטה התקנית היא הרצת ה-heuristics ל-fixed pegging כצעד אחרי ה-planning heuristics.
לביצוע pegging, התנאים:
• **Same pegging area** — ה-pegging area = שילוב product + location ב-version עם account assignment אם רלוונטי. ל-make-to-stock (MTS), הוא material + location. ל-make-to-order (MTO), כל sales order מהווה customer segment, וה-sales order (כ-account assignment) גם חלק. האלמנטים צריכים להיות באותו pegging area.
• **Pegging interval** — ה-receipts (כולל stock) pegged אם בתוך ה-pegging interval. ברירת-מחדל 277,000 שעות (~31.6 שנים — הערך המרבי). ב-embedded PP/DS, ה-interval מתגלגל ~31.6 שנים ואינו ניתן לשינוי (Figure 5.4).
הגדרות נוספות:
• **Avoid Alerts** — כשמסומן, המערכת מכבדת את האסטרטגיה אך מנסה להימנע מהפרת Alert Threshold for Earliness/Lateness (בשעות:דקות, למשל 50000:10). חייבים להיות פחות מ-277000 שעות. בדוגמה (Figure 5.5), ‏strategy 1 Earliest Receipt (FIFO), הדרישה ב-03.03.2023 אמורה להיות pegged ל-planned order ב-31.12.2022, אך ההפרש עולה על ה-Threshold for Maximum Earliness (48 שעות). מכיוון ש-Avoid Alerts מסומן, המערכת מוצאת receipt בתוך ה-threshold (02.03.2023).
• **Use Total Receipt/Use Total Stock** — כשמסומן, ‏receipt אחד (כל הכמות) מוקצה רק ל-requirement אחד. בדוגמה (Figure 5.6), שני receipts (stock 50 ו-planned order 100) ושש דרישות forecast של 25. עם Use Total Receipts/Stock, המערכת מחפשת כמויות מדויקות; מכיוון שאין, אין pegging. עם ה-tolerance ב-material master (Figure 5.7), ‏overdelivery tolerance 25% ב-Work scheduling view — ‏receipt עד 25% יותר מהדרישה ניתן ל-pegging.
ב-CDP, ה-characteristics נבדקים לתאימות. למוצרים עם shelf life, ‏minimum shelf life, ו-maturation time, ה-dynamic pegging מתחשב בערכים אלו.

sections.title: Planning Horizon and Planning Time Fence
sections.en: 5.2.2 Planning Horizon and Planning Time Fence In PP/DS, either the demand can be transferred from an SAP planning system, such as SAP IBP, or a non-SAP system can send in the forecast in the form of planned indepen- dent requirements (PIRs) to SAP S/4HANA, which will be transferred to embedded PP/DS if the material is activated for advanced planning. A planning tool such as SAP IBP is responsible for forecasting and planning the mid- to long-term forecasting and supply planning. However, embedded PP/DS is a short- to mid-term planning tool, and PP/DS is used for short-term detailed scheduling. To define the responsibility of PP/DS for planning only in the short term, a PP/DS plan- ning horizon is defined. Any demand that falls under the PP/DS planning horizon is planned by PP/DS planning tools. The planning horizon is defined in the model version master data (Transaction /SAPAPO/MVM) (see Chapter 3, Section 3.2.1). The horizon defined here is a global setting and considered by all the material locations. But this global value can be overwritten by the product-/location-specific PP/DS horizon. The © 229 5.2 Basic Functions in PP/DS Planning product-/location-specific PP/DS horizon is maintained in the material master Advanced Planning view as shown in Figure 5.8. In this example, the global setting (Transaction /SAPAPO/MVM) is 1200 days 1, and the product-/location-specific PP/DS Horizon is 365 days 2 as defined in the material master. In the product view, you can also see that the value of 365 days 3 is considered from the current date 22.12.2022 4. In a production planning run, the PP/DS planning heuristics only consider the demand and supply within this horizon for the calculation of the unfilled demand. Figure 5.8 Planning Version (Global) Level versus Product-/Location-Specific PP/DS Horizon The PP/DS planning time fence is the shorter horizon in the planning horizon within which the system isn’t allowed to make changes to the planning data during an inter- active or background production planning run. Manual changes are allowed within the planning time fence. When the planners adjust the plan and finalize the schedule for the near-term shorter time horizon, the plan must not be altered by the system, and the planning time fence can be defined to such a duration. The PP/DS time fence is defined in the material master by using Transaction MM02 and navigating to the MRP 1 tab, as shown in Figure 5.9. You can see the Planning Time Fence value of “21” set 1, in our example. This value defined in the material master is also used by the PP/DS plan- ning time fence if the material is activated for advanced planning and can be seen in the PP/DS product master 2 (Transaction /SAPAPO/MAT1). The planning time fence represented as a separate row 3 in the product view (Transaction /SAPAPO/RRP3). The planning time fence is calculated from the current time stamp by adding the time fence defined in the master data. 5 Production Planning 230 Figure 5.9 Planning Time Fence in the Material Master: PP/DS Product Master Data and Product View
sections.he:
ב-PP/DS, הביקוש מועבר ממערכת תכנון (SAP IBP) או ממערכת שאינה-SAP בצורת planned independent requirements (PIRs) ל-S/4HANA, המועברים ל-embedded PP/DS אם החומר מופעל. כלי כגון SAP IBP אחראי על חיזוי ותכנון בינוני עד ארוך-טווח; ‏embedded PP/DS לטווח קצר עד בינוני, ו-PP/DS ל-detailed scheduling קצר-טווח.
להגדרת אחריות PP/DS לטווח קצר, מוגדר PP/DS planning horizon. כל ביקוש בתוכו מתוכנן ע"י PP/DS. ה-horizon מוגדר ב-model version (Transaction /SAPAPO/MVM, פרק 3, סעיף 3.2.1) — הגדרה גלובלית לכל ה-locations. ניתן לדרוס ע"י PP/DS horizon ספציפי-product/location ב-material master Advanced Planning view (Figure 5.8). בדוגמה, גלובלי 1200 ימים, ספציפי 365 ימים. בריצה, ה-heuristics מתחשבים רק בביקוש ובהיצע בתוך ה-horizon.
ה-PP/DS planning time fence הוא ה-horizon הקצר יותר שבו המערכת אינה רשאית לשנות נתונים בריצה (אינטראקטיבית או background). שינויים ידניים מותרים. מוגדר ב-material master (Transaction MM02, לשונית MRP 1, ‏Planning Time Fence, Figure 5.9; בדוגמה 21). משמש גם את ה-PP/DS time fence, נראה ב-product master (Transaction /SAPAPO/MAT1) וכשורה נפרדת ב-product view. מחושב מה-time stamp הנוכחי + ה-time fence.

sections.title: Net Requirements Calculation
sections.en: 5.2.3 Net Requirements Calculation Net requirements calculation is the process of balancing the demand and supply quan- tities and arriving at the missing quantities so that new receipt elements can be created to cover them. In embedded PP/DS, you can customize the way the receipts and requirement ele- ments are treated by the net requirements calculation process. These customizations are made in the heuristics settings, so that when a planning heuristic is called in the planning run or interactive planning, the system uses the net requirements calculation procedure set in the heuristics to apply it on the planning. Don’t confuse the concept of pegging with the concept of net requirements calculation. The pegging only links the available receipt and requirement element. But the role of net requirements calculation is to find out when the net quantity (sum of receipts and requirements) falls below zero and trigger a receipt creation at that point in time to fill the open demand. During net requirements calculation, the system starts with the stock and the receipt elements and nets them against the open demand elements. The settings are made in the heuristics Customizing (Transaction /SAPAPO/CDPSC11), as shown in Figure 5.10. © 231 5.2 Basic Functions in PP/DS Planning Figure 5.10 Net Requirements Calculation Procedures in PP/DS Planning Heuristics The following options are available to influence the netting:  FIFO With the FIFO netting procedure, the earliest available requirement element is assigned to the stock element or the earliest available receipt element, and the same chronological order is followed for netting throughout the PP/DS planning horizon.  Avoid Surpluses This procedure will try to avoid new receipt elements creation by assigning the avail- able receipt and stock elements to the requirement elements, irrespective of whether this assignment will cause a delay for the requirement element being ful- filled on time. This procedure divides the planning horizon into two sections, one for the elements within the PP/DS time fence and another section for the elements outside the planning time fence.  Avoid Delays This netting procedure will try to avoid delays in fulfilling the requirement elements by assigning the stocks and fixed receipt elements to the requirements. If there is a delay, this procedure will propose creating a new receipt element. Thus, this proce- dure may lead to excess supply. This procedure is also referred to as alert minimiza- tion for net requirement calculation. The Alert Threshold for Lateness defined in the material master is considered by this procedure to determine if the system can assign an existing fixed receipt element to the demand. As shown in the example in Figure 5.11, 48:00 (48 hours) 1 is set as the Alert Threshold for Lateness in the mate- rial master. Before planning is executed, a demand element exists on 07.07.2023 for 5 Production Planning 232 250 quantities 2. There is a fixed receipt element (planned order) for 250 quantities on 10.10.2023 3. When executing net requirement calculation with the Avoid Delays procedure, the system checks the dates of the receipt and requirement elements. As the fixed planned order is delayed by more than 48 hours from the demand date, the system can’t assign the planned order to the demand during net requirement calcu- lation. This will cause the planning to create a new receipt element (planned order) 4 to cover the demand, irrespective of the fact that it will cause a surplus supply sit- uation 5 at the end of the PP/DS horizon. Figure 5.11 Example of Avoid Delays - Net Requirement Calculation Procedure The other options available to influence the net requirements calculation are as fol- lows:  Use Total Receipts With this setting active, when one receipt element is assigned to a requirement ele- ment irrespective of the quantity being assigned to the requirement element, the complete receipt element is consumed. If there are partial available quantities from the receipt element, those are left open and aren’t assigned to any other require- ment element.  Use Total Stocks With this option, when the stock element is assigned to a requirement element during the net requirements calculation, then the stock element is completely con- sumed for the purpose of the net requirements calculation, and no other require- ment element can be assigned to the stock element. © 233 5.2 Basic Functions in PP/DS Planning
sections.he:
‏net requirements calculation הוא תהליך איזון כמויות הביקוש וההיצע והגעה לכמויות החסרות, כך שניתן ליצור receipts חדשים. ב-embedded PP/DS, ניתן להתאים כיצד ה-receipts וה-requirements מטופלים — בהגדרות ה-heuristics, כך שכש-planning heuristic נקרא, המערכת משתמשת בנוהל.
אל תבלבלו pegging עם net requirements calculation. ה-pegging רק מקשר; תפקיד ה-net requirements הוא למצוא מתי הכמות הנטו (סכום receipts ו-requirements) שלילית ולהפעיל יצירת receipt. בחישוב, המערכת מתחילה ב-stock וב-receipts ומקזזת מול הביקושים. ההגדרות ב-heuristics Customizing (Transaction /SAPAPO/CDPSC11, Figure 5.10):
• **FIFO** — ה-requirement המוקדם מוקצה ל-stock או ל-receipt המוקדם, בסדר כרונולוגי.
• **Avoid Surpluses** — מנסה להימנע מ-receipts חדשים ע"י הקצאת קיימים, ללא קשר לעיכוב. מחלק את ה-horizon לשני חלקים (בתוך/מחוץ ל-time fence).
• **Avoid Delays** — מנסה להימנע מעיכובים ע"י הקצאת stocks ו-fixed receipts. אם יש עיכוב, מציע receipt חדש (עלול לעודף). גם נקרא alert minimization. ה-Alert Threshold for Lateness ב-material master נחשב. בדוגמה (Figure 5.11), ‏48:00 (48 שעות), דרישה ב-07.07.2023 ל-250, ו-fixed planned order ל-250 ב-10.10.2023. מכיוון שמעוכב מעל 48 שעות, המערכת לא יכולה להקצותו, ויוצרת planned order חדש (גם בעודף).
אפשרויות נוספות:
• **Use Total Receipts** — ‏receipt אחד נצרך במלואו; כמויות חלקיות נשארות פתוחות.
• **Use Total Stocks** — ה-stock נצרך במלואו; אין requirement אחר מוקצה.

sections.title: Procurement Quantity Calculation
sections.en: 5.2.4 Procurement Quantity Calculation When the net requirements calculation determines when to create a receipt element, the procurement quantity calculation will determine for what quantity the receipt quantity should be created. This is determined by the lot size definition. The lot size can be defined in the heuristics-specific settings and in the material master’s Advanced Planning tab. The heuristics-specific settings for lot size provide options that are only relevant for that heuristic. The lot size data maintained in the MRP 1 view and the Advanced Plan- ning view of the material master are considered by the PP/DS planning heuristics, which needs to determine a quantity for order creation. The lot sizing information from the MRP 1 view, such as lot sizing procedure, minimum and maximum lot sizes, and rounding factors, is considered by PP/DS in addition to the lot sizing unit of mea- sure and other lot sizing-specific fields from the Advanced Planning view of the mate- rial master. The standard planning heuristics, such as the planning of standard lots heuristics, sup- port several lot sizing procedures in the standard embedded PP/DS system. You can access the following procedures in the Lot Sizes tab, as shown in Figure 5.12:  Lot-for-Lot This procedure will propose a receipt quantity exactly the same as the requirement quantity per the net requirements calculation. However, this procedure will con- sider the minimum and maximum lot size settings and the rounding parameters maintained in the material master.  Fixed Lot Size This procedure will propose receipt quantities per the fixed lot size defined in the material master, irrespective of the net requirements quantity. If one receipt can’t cover the entire net requirements quantity, multiple receipts are proposed with the fixed lot size until the requirement can be covered with the new receipts.  By Period In periodic lot sizing procedures, the net requirements are grouped together per period (day, week, etc.), and one receipt element is proposed per period. This proce- dure also respects the minimum and maximum lot size settings and the rounding settings. Tip With periodic lot sizing procedures, the Period Factor in the Advanced Planning view of the material master and the Use Period Factor checkbox to influence the time of the receipt element availability. For example, if the period factor is 0.75, with the daily lot sizing proce- dure, the procurement proposals—such as planned orders or purchase requisitions—are created with a time stamp of 18:00 (instead of the default 12:00:00 time stamp). 5 Production Planning 234  Reorder Point The planning of standard lots heuristic (SAP_PP_002) only supports the Reorder Point Method 2, which is the Reorder Day’s Supply value maintained in the material master Advanced Planning tab. Figure 5.12 Lot Sizing Maintenance in PP/DS for Advanced Planning Materials Tip Irrespective of the lot sizing method maintained in the MRP 1 view of the material mas- ter, if Reorder Day’s Supply is maintained in the Advanced Planning view of the mate- rial master, then PP/DS planning heuristics will consider this material with a lot sizing procedure with the reorder order point method. The minimum and maximum lot sizes are maintained in the material master (Transac- tion MM02) MRP 1 tab in the Minimum Lot Size and Maximum Lot Size fields. In addi- tion, the PP/DS-specific lot sizing settings, such as the Reorder Day’s Supply, is defined in the Advanced Planning tab under the Lot Size section, as shown in Figure 5.13. © 235 5.2 Basic Functions in PP/DS Planning Figure 5.13 Lot Sizing Procedure Definition in MRP 1 and Advanced Planning Views

כשה-net requirements קובע מתי ליצור receipt, ה-procurement quantity calculation קובע לאיזו כמות — לפי הגדרת ה-lot size (בהגדרות ה-heuristics וב-material master Advanced Planning). הגדרות ה-heuristics רלוונטיות רק לאותו heuristic. נתוני ה-lot size מ-MRP 1 view וה-Advanced Planning view נחשבים. ה-planning of standard lots heuristic תומך בנהלים (לשונית Lot Sizes, Figure 5.12):
• **Lot-for-Lot** — receipt בדיוק כ-requirement (מתחשב ב-min/max lot size ו-rounding).
• **Fixed Lot Size** — לפי ה-fixed lot size, ללא קשר ל-net requirements. ‏receipts מרובים אם נדרש.
• **By Period** — ה-net requirements מקובצים לפי תקופה (יום, שבוע), ‏receipt אחד לתקופה.
**טיפ:** בנהלים תקופתיים, ה-Period Factor ב-Advanced Planning view וה-Use Period Factor checkbox משפיעים על זמן הזמינות. למשל, ‏period factor 0.75 עם daily — ‏time stamp 18:00 (במקום 12:00:00).
• **Reorder Point** — ה-planning of standard lots (SAP_PP_002) תומך רק ב-Reorder Point Method 2 (ה-Reorder Day's Supply ב-material master Advanced Planning).
ה-min/max lot sizes ב-material master (Transaction MM02) MRP 1, שדות Minimum/Maximum Lot Size. הגדרות PP/DS ספציפיות (Reorder Day's Supply) ב-Advanced Planning תחת Lot Size (Figure 5.13).
