sections.title: Interactive Production Planning
sections.en: 5.6.3 Interactive Production Planning Many of the planning tasks scheduled as planning run steps within the production planning run can be executed interactively to evaluate the results of the planning. In addition, actions such as creating an order, changing or deleting an order, changing the sources of supply, re-exploding the source of supply, setting and removing firming indicators, setting the conversion checkbox, and changing or creating fixed pegging relationships can be executed from the interactive planning tools. In embedded PP/DS, the following are the commonly used interactive planning tools for production planning purposes:  Product view  Receipts view  Requirements view  Order processing view  Product planning table  Product overview © 297 5.6 Triggering a PP/DS Planning Run We’ll cover the product view in detail in this section and also give an overview of the other tools and their specific use cases, if any. Some of the tools can be used to perform the detailed scheduling actions as well. But in this section, we’ll cover the functions related to production planning in the interactive planning tools. Product View The product view is the most commonly used transaction for interactive planning and evaluation of the planning results for individual material/locations. The product view can be accessed from SAP Easy Access menu path, Logistics  Advanced Planning  Pro- duction Planning  Interactive Production Planning  Product View. You can use Transac- tion /SAPAPO/RRP3 to access the product view as well. The initial screen of the product view, as shown in Figure 5.62, has the Plng Version, Product, and Location options. Entering these three values is the basic minimum requirement. If you work with special stock scenarios, such as sales orders or project orders, you can use the Special Stock indicator and the account assignment object. Figure 5.62 PP/DS Product View: Selection Screen The Selection Rule can be specified to filter out the receipt and requirements displayed in the product view by period restrictions or by excluding certain order categories from displaying in the results. For any action you perform within the product view, the system generates planning logs according to the PP/DS global settings. For performance reasons, the global set- tings may be set to just error messages. You can override this setting within the prod- uct view by setting the logging level via Settings  Planning Log, as shown on the right side of Figure 5.62, and setting the All Messages option in the dialog box. This setting is valid for the current session, and when you restart the product view transaction, it will be defaulted back to the original setting. 5 Production Planning 298 Tip The product view selection rule can be customized from the Customizing IMG menu path: SAP IMG Menu  Advanced Planning  Order View  Define Selection Rules for Product View. In addition, by using the Create Order button, the system will take you to the screen where you can create a new procurement element, such as a planned order or purchase requisition (depending on the procurement type of the material). After entering the required selection options, click on the Continue button or press (Enter) to view the result of the product view. The results screen of the product view has multiple tabs and features, as shown in Fig- ure 5.63. Click on the Change button on the menu bar to make the planning data edit- able in the product view. In edit mode, only the elements that can be changed in embedded PP/DS can be changed in the product view. Figure 5.63 PP/DS Product View Details Screen Following are the different tabs and the functionality and data contained in these tabs, which are used for interactive planning:  Elements The Elements tab has the list of stock, receipt, and requirement elements displayed in chronological order. The PP/DS planning time fence and the PP/DS planning hori- zon are marked accordingly. The resources on which the orders are manufactured, the dates/times, quantities, and order categories are some of the important fields © 299 5.6 Triggering a PP/DS Planning Run listed in the Elements tab. You can select individual or multiple orders (by pressing the (Ctrl) key and clicking on the Order Selection checkbox on the screen) to delete them. Double-clicking on the order will take you to the order details screen (see Figure 5.64) where you can perform actions such as setting or removing the firming checkboxes 1 and setting the Conversion Ind. for converting the planned orders to production orders or the purchase requisitions to purchase orders 2. For the manufacturing orders (production/process orders), the Life Cycle checkboxes are set according to their execution status in SAP S/4HANA 3. The list of available sources of supply can be displayed by clicking on the Change source of supply button 4. In addition, if required, a different valid source of supply can be selected for the order. Figure 5.64 Order Processing from the Order Details Screen Note The product view, receipt view, and requirement view work based on simulation (sim) sessions. Until the user saves the data, all the changes are only saved in the sim ses- sion, which allows multiple planners to work in parallel if required. Therefore, all the heuristics execution and changes are temporary in the product view until the user explicitly clicks on the Save button. 5 Production Planning 300  Periods/Quantities The Periods and Quantities tabs display the demand and supply situation in a peri- odic view. The Periods tab shows the data in a tabular periodic form with additional context, such as the day’s supply calculated for all the displayed periods. The Quan- tities tab shows the receipts supplies and the netted quantity in a graphical format.  Stock/Pegging Overview The Stock tab shows the inventory availability of the material across all available locations. In the Pegging Overview tab, you can display the current pegging over- view of the requirements and receipts. In change mode, you can create fixed pegging relationships or change already existing pegging relationships.  Product Master The Product Master tab displays the embedded PP/DS product master of the mate- rial master maintained in SAP S/4HANA. This is a display-only feature, and no changes can be directly made to the material master from embedded PP/DS.  Forecast The Forecast tab has the information about the requirements strategy master data. It also lists the forecasts (PIRs from SAP S/4HANA and forecast elements created in embedded PP/DS) and whether the forecasts are consumed by incoming sales orders or sales order deliveries according to the requirements strategy used. The product view display of tabs, alerts, and available heuristics to be executed are deter- mined by the user profile and other profiles assigned to the user profile. Settings can be maintained for controlling the display of the product view. As shown in Figure 5.65, you can click on the menu Settings  User Settings to bring up the display variant per the Cus- tomizing settings. You can change the values on the user settings and save the variant as a New Variant, which will be loaded by default when you open the product view. Note You can use ABAP program /SAPAPO/PPDS_USERSETTINGS_MAIN from Transaction SE38 or Transaction SA30 and choose the appropriate options to delete the variants saved for the user; this will also delete the variant saved by the user. When the product view is launched again, the system prompts you to choose a variant set in Customizing. In change mode within the product view, you can execute the product heuristics by clicking on the Product Heuristic button. Depending on the heuristic settings for inter- active planning, it will execute the heuristics. By clicking on the Variable Heuristics but- ton, you’ll be taken to a screen with a list of allowed heuristics from the assigned heuristics profile. You can also change the default heuristic settings for execution from this screen. If you want to execute a heuristic that isn’t in the list of heuristics, you’ll have to assign a heuristics profile to the user setting that has the desired heuristic assigned. © 301 5.6 Triggering a PP/DS Planning Run Figure 5.65 User Settings in the Product View: Changing the Default Variant When executing a heuristic, if the Generate Evaluation option is set as active in the Interactive Planning section under the Basic Settings tab for interactive planning of the heuristic, then you’ll see the Evaluation tab on the screen for executing the variable heuristics. This tab contains the details about the receipt and requirement elements the system has considered for planning. The details of the fixed receipts and the plan- ning file entries generated by the system are recorded in the evaluation, as shown in Figure 5.66. Tip By entering “GT_IO” in the transaction code box (top-left corner of screen) and pressing the (Enter) key, you can see the SAP liveCache representation of the elements dis- played in the product view. The SAP liveCache order GUIDs and order categories can be seen from this option as well. 5 Production Planning 302 Figure 5.66 Execute Variable Heuristics: Evaluation in the Product View Other Order Views Apart from the product view, the other order view tools also can be used for changing PP/DS planning data interactively. Following are these order views and the specific fea- tures they offer:  Receipts view (Transaction /SAPAPO/RRP4) This view lists all the receipt elements for the given selection. This can be used to mass-process the receipt elements and to set the conversion indicator for all the selected receipts when allowed by the order type and status. The order quantities and proprieties can be changed, and the variable heuristics can be used to execute heuristics (e.g., bottom-up and top-down rescheduling for the selected orders) from this view.  Requirements view (Transaction /SAPAPO/RRP1) This view lists all the requirement elements for the given selection. In change mode, the requirement quantities can be created, changed, or deleted for the allowed requirement elements, such as forecast elements. Variable heuristics can be exe- cuted for the selected requirement elements as well. © 303 5.6 Triggering a PP/DS Planning Run Product Planning Table (Transaction /SAPAPO/PPT1) The product planning table is a comprehensive planning tool that allows all the PP/DS tasks to be performed in the tabular form of the data. In addition, the graphical detailed scheduling planning board can be loaded into the planning table. Tools such as execu- tion of variable and product heuristics, Alert Monitor, and Detailed Scheduling Opti- mizer are also integrated into the product planning table. Although it can be used for any planning scenario, the product planning table is com- monly used for repetitive manufacturing planning as the production plan and the resource loads can be simultaneously performed from the product planning table. In the initial screen of this tool, as shown in Figure 5.67, you enter the Planning Version, the From and To dates for which you want to load the transaction data in the product planning table, and the Location. Under the Product tab, you can enter the materials that need to be selected and other selection options relevant to the material. Under the Source / Target tab of the section option, you can enter source locations such as ven- dors or source plants (locations) in case of stock transfer scenarios. If you want to restrict the selection by resources, you can use the Line / Resource tab to enter a list of Resources. The Production Line option under the Line / Resources tab is used with Inte- grated Product and Process Engineering (iPPE), which is commonly used in the auto- motive industry. Figure 5.67 Production Planning Table: Initial Screen 5 Production Planning 304 Under the Additional Selection Criteria, you can further filter the selection with the Extended Selection dropdown options, such as only loading receipt elements, require- ment elements, or only products with alerts. Evaluate PSD is only relevant for type con- tainer resources, which can store material in them and aren’t part of the PDS operations, but are defined in the product storage definition master data. Various charts and tools can be loaded in the product planning table. The default charts to be loaded and which charts are to allowed within the product planning table are defined under the user settings. Navigate to the menu Settings  User Settings, to change and save the assigned variant name. As shown in Figure 5.68, in the Charts tab of the User Settings for Product Planning Table screen, you can choose which charts and how many charts will be loaded in the product planning table. Figure 5.68 Production Planning Table: User Settings © 305 5.6 Triggering a PP/DS Planning Run In this example variant, three charts are selected to be loaded. Under Selection and Sequence of Charts, you can see the list of all available charts. There are other tabs in this screen where various other profiles such as the alert profile, heuristics profile, and so on can be assigned along with options to control the display of the data in the charts loaded in the product planning table. After the selection conditions are entered, execute the transaction. This will load the result screen shown in Figure 5.69. On the left of the screen, a tree view is created to group the materials. In this example, the grouping is done based on the Planner 1. In addition, you can change the grouping by clicking on the group button 2. Grouping is possible by material, planner, location, resources, and so on. On the left bottom of the screen, you can see all the possible charts 3. You can load up to three charts for analyzing and adjusting the planning and scheduling data. In the chart area 4, depending on the selection, the charts are loaded with the planning and/ or capacity details. In this example, the display-only charts—Production View: Periodic and Resource View: Periodic—are loaded, as well as Product View: Periodic, which is an editable chart. For this chart, you can add receipt elements or forecast elements by entering the quantities in the corresponding rows. Many of the cells in the charts are navigable as well. For example, if you double-click on the receipt quantity in the peri- odic chart, it will open a table below with the list of planned orders corresponding to the receipt quantity for that period. Figure 5.69 Production Planning Table: Details The transaction runs in simulation mode until you save the transaction. So, you can simulate changes and interactively see the impact of the changes you made immedi- ately in the other charts, such as resource capacity impacts or any new alerts. Once you finalize the plan and/or schedule, you can save the transaction to persist the data. 5 Production Planning 306 Product Overview (Transaction /SAPAPO/POV1) The product overview planning tool offers the option to load multiple products and monitor their planning status, alerts, and other KPIs (e.g., different day’s supply). Because this helps planners identify and focus on materials with specific issues, it can be the land- ing transactions for planners after a planning run to monitor the results of the plan. The selection screen of the product overview is similar to the product planning table selection options, as shown in Figure 5.70. In the product overview, the start date for selection is an optional field and needs to be explicitly activated using the Use Start Date checkbox. Without the start date, all past receipt and requirement elements are considered in the calculation of the columns displayed in the result screen. Compared to the product planning table, in product overview, an additional selection is available in the Production Planning Run tab. In this tab, you can analyze the specific planning runs by filtering on the planning run date and exceptions. If there are logs generated, you can set the level of severity of the application log messages raised during the plan- ning run to filter the problem materials and analyze them. Figure 5.70 Product Overview: Selection Screen After the selections are entered, executing the transaction will load the results, as shown in Figure 5.71. In the result screen the list of materials per the selection condi- tions are listed. You can click on the change view button 1 to switch between View : © 307 5.6 Triggering a PP/DS Planning Run Product Info. and View : Planning Run Info.. In the product info view, you can adjust the layout of the screen and view fields related to master data 2 such as the product and location information and some of the key fields from the material master that are rele- vant for PP/DS. The date/time, quantity, network alerts, and maximum of all the alerts 3 available for the material can be added to the columns. KPIs 4 for planning the list of materials, such as day’s supply information, total receipts, and requirements for the period of selection, are available in the layout to be added as columns. In addition, the planning run 5 info such as the planning date and the log type (error, warning, or info) generated for the material can also be displayed on the screen. If there are alerts or KPIs that aren’t satisfactory, you can navigate to the planning tools such as the product view or the product planning table 6 to adjust the plan. After you adjust the plan, if there are still alerts and you want to mark the row as a processed row, you can select the row, and click on the Change Processed Status button 7. This will set an indicator on the row with a status of Processed 8. In the selection screen under the additional selection, you can filter the materials by the processing status as well. Figure 5.71 Product Overview: Product Info View Details When you switch to the planning run info view, you can display details of the planning runs for the specific products such as the planning date, user executing the planning, heuristics executed, and some of the KPIs (e.g., runtime of the planning for the mate- rial, number of orders created to cover the demand on time, delayed orders, etc.), as shown in Figure 5.72. Figure 5.72 Product Overview: Planning Run Info Details 5 Production Planning 308

sections.title: Planning PP/DS Materials in MRP Live (One MRP Run)
sections.en: 5.6.4 Planning PP/DS Materials in MRP Live (One MRP Run) The advanced planning materials also can be planned in the MRP Live planning run. MRP Live will call the PP/DS planning tools for planning the advanced planning mate- rials. When the requirement is to execute the product heuristics as part of MRP Live, this can be achieved by including the advanced planning materials in the MRP Live run. However, if there is a need to execute multiple heuristics in sequence, including the product heuristics in one step, this isn’t possible from MRP Live planning. In such cases, a separate PP/DS planning run needs to be scheduled and executed. When planning advanced planning and nonadvanced planning materials together in MRP Live, you must ensure that all the materials above the BOM level structure of the material are also planned in advanced planning. This makes sure that the dependent demand generated in one level by PP/DS is passed all the way to the last-level material that is relevant for advanced planning. The MRP Live run executes the planning in sequence according to the low-level code set in SAP S/4HANA for the materials. So, if you have special planning situations where the PP/DS low-level code is critical for planning, such as usage of planning packages or interchangeability, they need to be planned in a PP/DS planning run. For the advanced planning materials, it’s recommended to have an MRP type similar to X0 (without MRP, with BOM explosion), so that if any older planning tools are used in SAP S/4HANA apart from MRP Live, the materials aren’t planned. MRP Live will always call the PP/DS product heuristics when the material has Advanced Planning selected. If the MRP type is set to No MRP, then the material also isn’t planned in PP/DS irrespec- tive of the Advanced Planning checkbox. MRP Live can be executed using Transaction MD01N or via SAP Easy Access menu path, Logistics  Production  MRP Planning  MRP Live. As shown in Figure 5.73, the MRP Live selection screen has fields for materials, plants, and so on. There are no specific settings required in the MRP Live run to plan the advanced planning materials. For advanced planning materials, the product heuristics are maintained in the Advanced Planning tab in the Product Heuristic field of the material master in Transac- tion MM02. The settings maintained in the heuristics customization for the assigned product heuristics of the material derive the planning parameters, including the han- dling of the lower-level components and scheduling parameters. MRP Live can be executed online in dialog mode or can be scheduled in the background job. The MRP Live log contains the level of materials planned and the number of PP/DS materials planned by the execution. Application logs are written for the PP/DS materi- als, which can be accessed from Transaction SLG1 (Application Logs). © 309

sections.title: Monitoring and Evaluating the Planning Runs
sections.en: 5.7 Monitoring and Evaluating the Planning Runs Figure 5.73 MRP Live Planning in SAP S/4HANA 5.7 Monitoring and Evaluating the Planning Runs It’s important to monitor the logs and the evaluations from the PP/DS planning runs, including the MRP Live run, to ensure that all materials are planned correctly and that there are no repeated errors or terminations that stop materials from getting planned correctly. In this section, we’ll cover some of the tools used to evaluate the planning logs.
sections.he: חשוב לנטר את הלוגים וההערכות מהריצות (כולל MRP Live) להבטחת תכנון נכון ושאין שגיאות/terminations חוזרים. בסעיף זה — כלים להערכת הלוגים.

sections.title: PP/DS Planning Log
sections.en: 5.7.1 PP/DS Planning Log When a planning-relevant action is executed via the interactive planning tools or from the online/background production planning run, the system generates application logs and records all the relevant information according to the PP/DS global settings. If the PP/DS global settings (Transaction /SAPAPO/RRPCUST1) are set for all messages, the application log will contain information, warning, error, and termination messages. 5 Production Planning 310 Tip The user parameter /SAPAPO/WHAT_PL can be set with value D in the user data for the user ID executing the planning runs to capture the detailed log to the level of information messages. This will override the log level set in /SAPAPO/RRPCUST1 for the specific users. The central transaction to monitor all the logs system-wide for PP/DS can be accessed via Transaction /SAPAPO/RRPLOG1 or from SAP Easy Access menu path, Logistics  Advanced Planning  Production Planning  Reporting  Logs  Display Logs. The selection screen of this transaction is shown in Figure 5.74. Figure 5.74 PP/DS Log Display: Selection Screen for Logs The logs can be filtered by the Application that was used for planning. All the various applications, such as the product view, planning run, and planning table, are available as selection options. The All Applications option is available to read all the logs for the defined selection criteria irrespective of the PP/DS application used for planning. The user name is also available as a selection option under the Log Context area. © 311 5.7 Monitoring and Evaluating the Planning Runs The log selection can be restricted by the date and time ranges in the From and To fields of the Time Restriction area. This transaction can list all PP/DS logs, including planning and scheduling logs. If you’re only interested in a specific type of log (scheduling or planning), choose the appropriate checkbox. The Problem Class can be used to select only error or termination messages. Especially if other selection options aren’t very restrictive, the log list will be huge, making finding a specific message by scrolling on the log results a tedious activity. Typically, you should set the filter for the error and termination messages. Then, after the context of the error or termination is known from the result, that information (time stamps, user, etc.) can be used to rerun the log display to understand the complete context of the error or termination messages. The Log Creation mode selection determines whether the system should read the logs generated by interactive tools or generated in the background mode, for example, in a background planning run, or both. The option for batch input isn’t relevant for PP/DS transactions. The log display transaction selection also has a Filter tab that provides further filter cri- teria specific to the PP/DS data, as shown in Figure 5.75. The active Planning Version 000 is entered by default; however, if you work with any nonactive PP/DS planning ver- sions for simulation reasons, you can set the planning version accordingly. Figure 5.75 Filter Options in the PP/DS Log Display 5 Production Planning 312 In PP/DS, the application log messages are grouped under exception groups. Some of these messages can also be customized. If you’re interested in certain groups of mes- sages in the logs, that can be done using the Exception Group in the filter. Tip The exception groups can be customized from the Customizing menu path: SAP IMG Menu  Advanced Planning  Application Logs for PP/DS  Maintain Exception Groups. Under the Message Context area, you can filter out the logs generated by specific heu- ristics or with the filter of the pegging area fields, such as the Product, Location, Produc- tion Planner, Account Assignment Object, and so on.

sections.title: Evaluate the MRP Live Execution
sections.en: 5.7.2 Evaluate the MRP Live Execution When MRP Live is executed in the background or in online mode, the system generates performance statistics apart from generating the application logs. While defining the variant for the MRP Live job in Transaction MD01N, you can enter a name for the perfor- mance log file so that it’s easy to identify and analyze after the MRP Live planning run. The MRP Live performance log can be accessed using Transaction MD_MRP_PERFLOG. The selection screen for this transaction allows you to select the performance logs by the name of the log, by the user name who executed the MRP Live planning, or by the MRP start date, as shown in Figure 5.76. Figure 5.76 MRP Live Performance Log: Selection Screen Click the Execute button in the screen to see the list of performance logs according to your selections. The key metrics, such as the MRP Live runtime (Tot.PlgTime), number of materials planned (Matls Plnd), how many of the materials were planned in PP/DS (PP/DS Matl), how many PP/DS materials failed during the planning run (PPDFailMat), and the time spent in the PP/DS planning tools (PP/DS Time), are listed as columns in this screen (see Figure 5.77). © 313 5.7 Monitoring and Evaluating the Planning Runs Figure 5.77 MRP Live: Performance Log Features for PP/DS Clicking on the menu path Go To  Advanced Planning Log will load the PP/DS applica- tion logs for the planning run 1. You can then navigate to a detailed screen where the individual planning steps are listed according to the low-level code and the planning tool (MRP Live on SAP HANA, classic MRP, or PP/DS) that planned the specific step. The time breakdown for the overall runtime (only for materials that aren’t in PP/DS) and the number of documents (e.g., planned orders, purchase requisitions, etc.) created, changed, and deleted by each step are also listed here. The PP/DS application logs can also be displayed for the MRP Live execution by select- ing the Advanced Planning Log button in the MRP Live Performance Log screen. Note The PP/DS application logs generated from the MRP Live executions also can be accessed from Transaction SLG1. In the selection screen, enter “APO” for the Object and “PPDS_MRPS4” (only in SAP S/4HANA 1909) for the Subobject.

sections.title: Evaluate the PP/DS Background Planning Run
sections.en: 5.7.3 Evaluate the PP/DS Background Planning Run The background PP/DS planning run can be monitored from the background planning transaction (Transaction /SAPAPO/CDPSB1) itself. But it’s also possible to only create a variant for the background planning transaction. You can use the variant and program /SAPAPO/BACKGROUND_SCHEDULING in the external job scheduling tools to sched- ule the background planning runs in embedded PP/DS. 5 Production Planning 314 The externally scheduled jobs can also be monitored in SAP background job monitor- ing Transaction SM37. You can use the job name or program name /SAPAPO/BACK- GROUND_SCHEDULING for filtering the PP/DS planning jobs. From the job screen, clicking on the job log shows all recorded messages raised during the background plan- ning job. If there are any terminations, those are also available in the job log, which can also be reviewed and analyzed from the application logs (Transaction SLG1). Depending on how the job is set up, there is a chance that the job is scheduled by a user name that isn’t the user name maintained in the job step. All the application logs are created under the user assigned in the step, so it’s really important that you identify the right user who executes the production planning step in the background job, as shown in Figure 5.78. After selecting the correct JobName, click the Step button in the menu bar to display the steps defined in the job. The User column in the Step List Over- view screen shows the user the system used to execute the job step. Figure 5.78 Background Planning Run Job: Job User versus Step User You can navigate to the job log from the Job Overview screen by clicking on the Job log button. The spool request has all the statistics of the PP/DS planning run and the results for the individual materials with top CPU consumption to indicate if there are any warnings, errors, or terminations. The main usage of the background planning job spool is to review the statistics and the top CPU-consuming materials to check if any specific master data or Customizing settings for these materials are causing bottle- necks. For performing the application-level analysis, the log display is a better tool because it has filtering capabilities, unlike the spool document. © 315 5.7 Monitoring and Evaluating the Planning Runs Some of the important statistics and information available in the planning job spool are shown in Figure 5.79. The materials planned in the planning run are listed in the sequence they are planned in 1. The number of records processed (e.g., the number of pegging areas selected and planned); the orders created, changed, and deleted; and the runtime statistics of the planning job (e.g., the runtime, the CPU time consumed by the heuristics, and the CPU time to update the data) are displayed 2. The materials that are the top CPU consumers are also listed in the spool 3. Figure 5.79 Information Available in the PP/DS Background Planning Job Spool

ניתן לנווט ל-job log מ-Job Overview (Job log button). ה-spool request מכיל את כל הסטטיסטיקות והתוצאות לחומרים בעלי צריכת CPU עליונה. השימוש העיקרי — סקירת הסטטיסטיקות והחומרים עתירי-ה-CPU. לניתוח ברמת היישום, ה-log display עדיף (יכולת סינון).
סטטיסטיקות חשובות ב-spool (Figure 5.79): החומרים בסדר התכנון; מספר הרשומות (pegging areas שנבחרו), ה-orders שנוצרו/שונו/נמחקו, וסטטיסטיקות runtime (הזמן, ‏CPU של ה-heuristics, ‏CPU לעדכון); החומרים עתירי-ה-CPU העליונים.

sections.title: Monitor Planning Results from MRP SAP Fiori Apps
sections.en: 5.7.4 Monitor Planning Results from MRP SAP Fiori Apps In the SAP S/4HANA system, the MRP cockpit is a set of SAP Fiori apps that can handle both the MRP planned and advanced planned materials. The apps can manage and monitor material shortages, receipts, and requirements. From the MRP apps, you can trigger a PP/DS planning run for individual materials to resolve a planning problem. The advanced planning-specific SAP Fiori apps—such as the SAP Fiori-based Advanced Planning Board and the Monitor Capacity app—are only relevant for advanced plan- ning resources and materials. For the MRP apps, the selection is based on the area of responsibility (AOR) assigned to the user in the app user settings. The AOR is the combination of the plant and the MRP controller. One user may be assigned to multiple plants and MRP controllers. For working with the MRP apps, authorization role SAP_BR_MATL_PLNR (Material Planner – External Procurement) and role SAP_BR_PRODN_PLNR (Production Planner) are delivered standard. After the roles are assigned and you open the SAP Fiori launchpad, you’ll see the MRP cockpit apps. 5 Production Planning 316 The first time you open an MRP app, it will prompt you to enter the Area of Responsi- bility. To change the AOR, launch the MRP app, and from the user menu in the upper- right corner of the SAP Fiori launchpad 1, go to the App Settings 2 to open the MRP Settings 3 popup, as shown in Figure 5.80. Click the Area of Responsibility arrow to access the My Area of Responsibility screen. In this screen, you can search for plants and MRP controllers using the filter bar 4. From the list displayed, set the AOR Status toggle button 5 to assign or unassign yourself from the MRP controllers. If the user doesn’t have authorization for the selected plant and MRP controller in the SAP S/4HANA sys- tem, no data will be loaded, and the message is logged. Figure 5.80 Assigning the AOR in MRP Cockpit Apps Tip In the SAP Gateway system, execute Transaction /N/UI2/FLP to open the SAP Fiori launchpad. The apps will be loaded per the authorization roles assigned to your user. The Monitor Material Coverage app and Display MRP Master Data Issues app can be used to monitor the results for the MRP Live planning runs, including advanced planned materials. Monitor Material Coverage The Monitor Material Coverage app is important because it shows the material cover- age per the shortage profile assigned in Customizing. To create and assign the shortage profile to users, follow the Customizing menu, SAP IMG Menu  Production  Material Requirements Planning  Apps for Material Requirements Planning  General Settings  Define Material Shortage Profiles  Assign Material Shortage Profile to Users. © 317 5.7 Monitoring and Evaluating the Planning Runs This app will list all the materials per the AOR defined and any additional filters set within the app. The stock availability will be shown with negative stock availability marked in red so you don’t have to scan through a huge list of materials and can focus on the materials with shortages. Filters can be applied by days till shortage, shortage quantity or day’s supply, and so on. You can select the materials and trigger an MRP Live run from the app itself by clicking the Start MRP Run button, which will start MRP Live for the selected materials in the SAP S/4HANA system. If the materials are advanced planned, the product heuristics also will be called by MRP Live. As shown in Figure 5.81, you also can launch the Manage Materials app for the selected material by clicking the Manage Materials button and then clicking the Start MRP Run button from the subsequent screen, as shown in Figure 5.82. Figure 5.81 Monitor Material Coverage App Figure 5.82 Manage Material Coverage App 5 Production Planning 318 In the Manage Material app, you can see all the demand supply and change supply ele- ments manually, and you can start an MRP Live run. Display MRP Master Data Issues Apart from monitoring the MRP Live planning run application logs from Transaction SLG1, the advanced planned materials that have failed in the MRP Live planning run also can be monitored from the Display MRP Master Data Issues app. This app lists all the materials with messages from the last MRP Live run for the AOR. You can set a filter on the category of the issues (information, warning, or error) or the source of the error (MRP Live, advanced planning). You can set the filter for the Source area as Advanced Planning to see a list of materials with errors in the MRP Live planning that are relevant to advanced planning, as shown in Figure 5.83. Figure 5.83 Advanced Planned Materials in the Display MRP Master Data Issues App One other efficient way of monitoring the planning results from the business point of view is from the Alert Monitor where alerts can be configured for delays, resources, shelf life, and so on. We’ll cover the Alert Monitor in Chapter 7.

sections.title: Leveraging the Production Planning Optimizer
sections.en: 5.8 Leveraging the Production Planning Optimizer The Production Planning Optimizer was introduced in SAP S/4HANA 2020 as part of the embedded PP/DS solution. In the earlier releases of SAP S/4HANA, only the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer was delivered, which will only optimize the schedule and resource utilization. But the procurement proposals, such as planned orders, purchase requisitions, and stock transfer requisitions, are created by the production © 319 5.8 Leveraging the Production Planning Optimizer planning heuristics in the PP/DS planning run, interactive planning or the MRP Live planning run. There was no option to generate an optimized plan. The possible option was to use the SAP IBP optimizer engine in the SAP IBP cloud solution. But as detailed planning information such as alternative sources of supply, detailed lot sizing proce- dures, and so on is available in PP/DS, it’s useful to have an optimizer engine within embedded PP/DS to arrive at an optimal plan before the plan is further optimized for the schedule and resource utilization. Planning using heuristics will execute the heuristics algorithm once and create the pro- duction plan. But optimizer engines such as the Production Planning Optimizer will iterate the planning results again and again to arrive at an optimal plan. The Production Planning Optimizer is a cost-based planning engine, which considers the following costs defined in the master data elements of embedded PP/DS:  Costs for production, procurement, and transportation  Costs for violation of safety stock levels  Costs for overloading the capacity of the resources (when overloading is allowed in the master data)  Penalty costs for late delivery and nondelivery Considering the constraints such as material flow through the BOM level of advanced planned materials, transfer of materials between plants and distribution centers, capacity constraints, lot sizes, and so on, the Production Planning Optimizer will opti- mize by minimizing the overall cost. Production Planning Optimizer works on a bucket-oriented planning basis. The hori- zon for the Production Planning Optimizer execution is divided into multiple small buckets, and the orders are proposed per bucket considering the demand and planning constraints in those buckets. Production Planning Optimizer supports linear optimiza- tion and discrete optimization where discrete constraints such as extended capacity usage and setup transitions can be considered by the optimizer. In this section, we’ll cover the details of the master data settings and Customizing set- tings required for leveraging Production Planning Optimizer. In addition, we’ll cover the steps to execute and monitor Production Planning Optimizer.
sections.he:
ה-Production Planning Optimizer הוצג ב-S/4HANA 2020 כחלק מ-embedded PP/DS. בגרסאות קודמות, רק ה-Detailed Scheduling Optimizer (ממטב schedule וניצול resource). ה-procurement proposals נוצרו ע"י ה-heuristics. לא הייתה אפשרות לתוכנית מותאמת (פרט ל-SAP IBP optimizer בענן). מכיוון שמידע תכנון מפורט (sources חלופיים, ‏lot sizing) זמין ב-PP/DS, שימושי optimizer engine פנימי.
תכנון ב-heuristics מבצע פעם אחת; ה-Production Planning Optimizer מאיטר שוב ושוב לתוכנית אופטימלית. הוא מנוע מבוסס-עלות המתחשב ב:
• עלויות production, ‏procurement, ו-transportation
• עלויות הפרת safety stock
• עלויות עומס-יתר על קיבולת ה-resources (כשמותר)
• penalty costs לאספקה מאוחרת ואי-אספקה
בהתחשב באילוצים (זרימת חומר דרך BOM, העברה בין plants, קיבולת, ‏lot sizes), ה-optimizer ממטב ע"י מזעור העלות הכוללת. עובד bucket-oriented — ה-horizon מחולק ל-buckets, וה-orders מוצעים לכל bucket. תומך ב-linear ו-discrete optimization (אילוצי discrete כגון extended capacity ו-setup transitions).

sections.title: Master Data Settings for Production Planning Optimizer
sections.en: 5.8.1 Master Data Settings for Production Planning Optimizer In this section, we’ll cover the master data objects and specific settings that are consid- ered by the Production Planning Optimizer. Material Master In the material master, the planning-relevant fields in MRP 1 and MRP 2 views, such as the Min Lot Size/Max Lot Size, Safety Stock, and Safety Time, are considered by Produc- tion Planning Optimizer. Apart from these fields, under the Advanced Planning tab, as 5 Production Planning 320 shown in Figure 5.84, the sections Penalties/Costs and Demand Penalties areas are con- sidered by Production Planning Optimizer for cost calculations for optimization. Figure 5.84 Production Planning Optimizer Costs and Penalties in the Material Master Procurement Costs refers to the costs incurred to procure the material in this specific location (plant). The Prod. Storage Cost is the cost incurred to store the material in the plant facility or in the warehouse. The value defined here corresponds to the cost of storing the material per its base unit of measurement for one day. Tip To use a time reference other than one day for the storage cost, the time reference can be changed (e.g., to one week or one month) using Transaction /SAPAPO/TMREF. The Safety Stock Pen. is the penalty applied for not meeting the safety stock levels defined in the material master and/or the time-dependent safety stocks maintained in Transaction /SAPAPO/TDS, depending on the safety stock method defined in the mate- rial master. Max Days’ Supply Pen. is the penalty cost applied if the max days’ supply is violated. The max day’s supply is defined in Transaction /SAPAPO/TDS, which is the maximum allowed earliness for a receipt allowed for a demand element. For example, if the maximum days’ supply is 10 days, and if the Production Planning Optimizer must create the order 11 days early due to capacity constraints, then for 1 day, the pen- alty defined here will be applied per unit of the material. © 321 5.8 Leveraging the Production Planning Optimizer Under the Demand Penalties section of the screen, the penalties for delay and nonde- livery are defined. Customer Demand, which is the demand originating from sales orders in general, and Demand Forecast originates from the PIR created in the SAP S/4HANA system. The Delay Penalty is the penalty cost applied per day of delay in ful- filling the demand per quantity of the material in its base unit of measure. For exam- ple, the penalty for customer demand is set as 10. If a sales order with a quantity of 100 and delivery date of 01.06.2023 can only be fulfilled on 02.06.2023, then the penalty is calculated as 100 (quantity) × 1 (day delay) × 10 (delay penalty) = 1,000. The Maximum Allowed Delay is the maximum allowed days after the demand date within which the demand can still be fulfilled. If the demand can’t be fulfilled before the maximum allow delay in days, Production Planning Optimizer will stop calculating the delay penalty and consider the Penalty for Non-Delivery. For example, let’s say the sales order with quantity 100 has a delivery date of 01.06.2023, and the maximum allowed delay is 5 days, along with a delay penalty of 100 and nondelivery penalty of 1,000. If the sales order demand can only be fulfilled on 07.06.2023 (1 day after the max- imum delay allowed), then the system will calculate the penalty as 100 (quantity) × 1000 (nondelivery penalty) = 100,000. The system calculates all the costs and penalties to determine whether to create an order on time or delayed or choose the demand not to be fulfilled if there are other constraints causing the order to be delayed. Resource Master In embedded PP/DS, the SAP S/4HANA work centers and resources (production planning for process industries) are transferred as resource master data. In the SAP S/4HANA work centers or resources, as shown in Figure 5.85, on the Change Work Center Capacity: Header screen, you can click on the APO Resource button to navigate to the PP/DS-related data. In the Header Data for APO Resource screen, navigate to the PPO Capacity Con- straints tab to enter the costs and constraints for Production Planning Optimizer. The Period Lot Size dropdown field has two options: Sequence-Dependent Lot Size and blank value. If you want this resource to be considered for setup time and setup costs for changeovers during optimization, select Sequence-Dependent Lot Size. When this field is set with blank value, the resource is not optimized for setup time and setup costs, by the production planning optimizer. Additional settings are required in the optimizer profile for this field to be considered during optimization, which we’ll cover in Section 8. For the consideration of setup costs and setup time by Production Plan- ning Optimizer, the recipe phase or routing operation should be assigned with a setup group, and only one resource with the setup group activated should be part of the PDS. In the Production Planning Optimizer Capacity Constraints area of the screen, you can maintain the Offset (in days) for the validity of the costs and other values maintained in the rows. The offset is calculated from the current date to the number of days in the future. In this example, till day 10 from today, the values maintained in the first row are valid, and from day 11 to day 365, the values maintained in the second row are valid. 5 Production Planning 322 Figure 5.85 Production Planning Optimizer Costs and Penalties in Resource Master Data The Normal Cap. Cost is the cost incurred to operate the resource under normal circum- stances per day. The Minimum Capacity(%) is the minimum capacity that should be con- sumed on the resource without which a penalty cost will be incurred, and the penalty is defined in the Min. Cap. Penalty (minimum capacity penalty) field. Cap. Extension(%) is the value of capacity that the system may extend if it needs to do so to avoid any other costs or penalties. For example, if the available capacity of a resource is 10 hours/day, defining 20% in this field will allow the optimizer to extend the available capacity to 12 hours, if there are high-priority demands to be delivered by this resource. This exten- sion isn’t updated in the resource master data, but the optimizer leverages the exten- sion value during the optimization run. The additional costs incurred for this extended capacity are defined in the Extd. Cap. Charges (extended capacity charges) field. Time-Dependent Master Data We’ve covered the time-dependent safety stock maintenance in Section 5.2.5. All the time-dependent master data is defined in Transaction /SAPAPO/TDS. Apart from the time-dependent safety stock, it’s also possible to define the Max. Stock (maximum stock levels/on-hand inventory), as shown in Figure 5.86 1, allowed for a material in a time-dependent way. The Max Days of Supply 2 (maximum days of supply) is also defined in this screen, which is the maximum earliness of a receipt element to cover a demand element. If the max days of supply is violated, the penalty defined in the material master is applied during the optimization. © 323 5.8 Leveraging the Production Planning Optimizer Figure 5.86 Time-Dependent Master Data Maintenance for Production Planning Optimizer You can also set time-dependent penalties for violation of safety stocks and maximum stocks. As shown in Figure 5.86, in the initial screen of Transaction /SAPAPO/TDS, select the Stock Penalties radio button 3 after entering the material and location selection details. In the next screen, you can enter the Safety Stock Penalty 4 and Max Stock Pen- alty 5 for different time periods. Production Data Structure and Transportation Lane In the PDSs, the cost and priority are considered by Production Planning Optimizer during optimization to choose the PDS, if there is more than one PDS available for a product location. In addition, the discrete PDS information is relevant for this PDS to be considered during the discrete optimization procedure. You can maintain the PDS cost, priority, and discretize flag via Transaction PDS_ MAINT. As shown in Figure 5.87, in the initial screen 1 of Transaction PDS_MAINT, enter the material and plant, and then enter “P” (PP/DS) in the PDS Usage in SCM field. In the next screen 2, enter the values for the PDS cost in the Var.Costs: Single-Level field and the PDS priority in the Priority field, and set the Discretiz. flag. Once you save the values in this transaction, the PDS needs to be retransferred to PP/DS using Trans- action CUTROADV_CREATE. After the retransfer, the corresponding fields are updated in the PDS header 3. 5 Production Planning 324 Figure 5.87 Cost and Priority in PDS for Production Planning Optimizer Tip Using Transaction /SAPAPO/CURTO_EDIT, the PDS cost, PDS priority, and Discretize flag can be updated, but a retransfer of PDS to PP/DS will overwrite these values with the values maintained in Transaction PDS_MAINT. In the transportation lane, you can maintain the transportation duration and the transpor- tation costs that will be considered by the optimizer to create stock transfer requisitions. For external procurement as of SAP S/4HANA 2022, the Production Planning Optimizer only creates anonymous purchase requisition with no vendor assigned because the loca- tion type of the vendor is still not supported by Production Planning Optimizer. Figure 5.88 Transportation Duration and Cost in Transportation Lanes © 325 5.8 Leveraging the Production Planning Optimizer As shown in Figure 5.88, in the Means of Transport area of the transportation lane, you can maintain the transportation cost along with the unit of measurement for the quan- tity and the transportation duration.
sections.he:
בסעיף זה — אובייקטי ה-master data וההגדרות שה-Production Planning Optimizer מתחשב בהם.

**Material Master:** שדות MRP 1 ו-MRP 2 (Min/Max Lot Size, ‏Safety Stock, ‏Safety Time) נחשבים. בלשונית Advanced Planning (Figure 5.84), ה-Penalties/Costs ו-Demand Penalties נחשבים. ‏Procurement Costs = עלות רכש ב-location זה. ‏Prod. Storage Cost = עלות אחסון ליחידת בסיס ליום.
**טיפ:** לשימוש בייחוס זמן אחר ליום (שבוע/חודש), ‏Transaction /SAPAPO/TMREF.
ה-Safety Stock Pen. = penalty לאי-עמידה ב-safety stock. ‏Max Days' Supply Pen. = penalty להפרת max days' supply (ב-/SAPAPO/TDS — ה-earliness המרבי המותר). תחת Demand Penalties, ‏Customer Demand (sales orders) ו-Demand Forecast (PIR). ה-Delay Penalty = penalty ליום עיכוב ליחידה. למשל, penalty 10, sales order של 100 ב-01.06.2023 הממולא ב-02.06.2023 → ‏100 × 1 × 10 = 1,000. ה-Maximum Allowed Delay = הימים המרביים שבהם ניתן עדיין למלא. מעבר לכך, ‏Penalty for Non-Delivery. למשל, ‏max delay 5 ימים, delay penalty 100, nondelivery 1,000; אם ממולא ב-07.06.2023 (יום אחרי המקסימום) → ‏100 × 1000 = 100,000.

**Resource Master:** ב-work centers/resources, במסך Change Work Center Capacity: Header, לחצו APO Resource (Figure 5.85). בלשונית PPO Capacity Constraints, העלויות והאילוצים. ה-Period Lot Size dropdown: ‏Sequence-Dependent Lot Size (להתחשבות ב-setup time/costs) או ריק. להתחשבות ב-setup, ה-recipe phase/routing operation צריך setup group, ורק resource אחד עם ה-group מופעל ב-PDS. ב-Production Planning Optimizer Capacity Constraints, ה-Offset (ימים) לתוקף. ‏Normal Cap. Cost = עלות הפעלה רגילה ליום. ‏Minimum Capacity(%) = הקיבולת המינימלית (אחרת Min. Cap. Penalty). ‏Cap. Extension(%) = הרחבת הקיבולת (למשל 20% → 12 שעות מ-10), עם Extd. Cap. Charges.

**Time-Dependent Master Data:** הכל ב-Transaction /SAPAPO/TDS. מעבר ל-safety stock, ניתן Max. Stock (Figure 5.86) ו-Max Days of Supply (earliness מרבי). ניתן גם penalties time-dependent — ב-/SAPAPO/TDS, בחרו Stock Penalties radio, והזינו Safety Stock Penalty ו-Max Stock Penalty לתקופות.

**Production Data Structure ו-Transportation Lane:** ב-PDSs, ה-cost וה-priority נחשבים לבחירת PDS (אם יותר מאחד). מידע ה-discrete PDS רלוונטי ל-discrete optimization. תחזוקה ב-Transaction PDS_MAINT (Figure 5.87) — הזינו "P" (PP/DS) ב-PDS Usage in SCM, ‏Var.Costs: Single-Level (cost), ‏Priority, וסמנו Discretiz. לאחר שמירה, יש להעביר-מחדש דרך Transaction CUTROADV_CREATE.
**טיפ:** ב-Transaction /SAPAPO/CURTO_EDIT ניתן לעדכן, אך retransfer ידרוס.
ב-transportation lane, ניתן transportation duration ו-costs (Figure 5.88). נכון ל-S/4HANA 2022, ה-Production Planning Optimizer יוצר רק purchase requisition אנונימי (ללא vendor) — סוג ה-location של vendor אינו נתמך עדיין.

sections.title: Profiles for Production Planning Optimizer
sections.en: 5.8.2 Profiles for Production Planning Optimizer For executing Production Planning Optimizer, there are profiles that need to be set up in the configuration. We’ll discuss them in the following sections. Time Bucket Profile The Production Planning Optimizer plans based on the bucket-oriented method, and once the receipt elements are proposed by the optimizer, they are scheduled by the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer in the same run. The time bucket profile breaks the total optimiza- tion horizon into smaller buckets. For example, for the initial seven days, you want the optimizer to plan in very granular subdaily buckets. Then, for the next four weeks, you want to plan in daily buckets, and the following 2 months, you want to plan in weekly buck- ets. The time bucket profile can be set up to consider the planning bucket requirements. Navigate to the configuration via SAP IMG Menu SPRO  Advanced Planning  Production Planning Optimization  Basic Settings  Define Time Bucket Profiles. In the initial screen of this configuration, as shown in Figure 5.89, click on the Sub Daily Bucket Definition ID for defining the subdaily buckets. If you want to create subdaily buckets of three shifts with eight hours each, then you can enter the Start Time of the first bucket within a day (in our example, 00:00:00) and the duration of the bucket (e.g., 8 hours) in the Subdaily Bucket Duration field. The Repetitions/Day field defines how many times within the day the bucket with the same duration is to be repeated (in our example, 3). This will create three buckets for each of the eight-hour segments in a day. Figure 5.89 Subdaily Bucket Definition for the Production Planning Optimizer Time Bucket Profile 5 Production Planning 326 To define the time bucket profile, double-click on the Time Bucket Profile Definition folder, and create a new entry. Enter a name and description for the profile. Then, select the newly created profile, and double-click on the Time Units folder. In the resulting screen, click on the New Entries button, and enter the Time Units and Time Unit Dura- tion. In this example, as shown in Figure 5.90, for the first 7 days, we’ll define the bucket using the subdaily buckets. When you select Subdaily Buckets as the time unit, you’ll have the option to also enter the subdaily bucket ID in the Sub Daily column. For the next 14 days, daily buckets are defined, and for the next 7 weeks, weekly buckets are defined. When you select week as the time unit, you’ll have the option to enter the start day of the week in the Week Starts On field. Next, 6 months are defined in monthly buckets and 4 quarters in quarterly buckets. Note During optimization using the Production Planning Optimizer, if no horizon for optimi- zation is entered, the time bucket profile will be used to calculate the end of the opti- mization horizon from the current date. Figure 5.90 Time Profile Definition for Production Planning Optimizer Category Profile The category profile is the setting where you can group the order categories such as CC (stocks), BM (sales orders), and so on for different elements such as customer demand, © 327 5.8 Leveraging the Production Planning Optimizer stocks, and firmed receipt elements, and assign them to the optimizer input categories. For example, if you don’t want to include blocked stocks in the available stock, you can exclude the order type for the blocked stocks (CI) from the category group for stocks and assign this group in the category profile for Production Planning Optimizer input data. The category group can be created from SAP IMG menu path SPRO  Advanced Planning  Production Planning Optimization  Basic Settings  Maintain Category Groups. In the ini- tial screen of this transaction, you’ll see the existing category groups. The category groups starting with the character “O” are the ones delivered in the standard system. You can create new category groups or copy existing groups and modify them. Select the cat- egory group, and double-click on the Categories folder option. In the resulting screen, you can enter new order categories or remove existing copied entries. In this example shown in Figure 5.91, we’re copying the existing group O03 for Stock to a custom category group Z03. In the copied group, the category CI was part of it, so we removed the entry for order category CI. Figure 5.91 Creating a Category Group for the Production Planning Optimizer Category Profile In the category profile, you can assign the category groups to different elements for the opti- mizer input data. To create the category profile, follow SAP IMG menu, SPRO  Advanced Planning  Production Planning Optimization  Basic Settings  Define Category Profiles. From the initial screen shown in Figure 5.92, you can create new entries or copy and modify existing entries. Profile SAP001 is delivered as a standard category profile. In this example, as we want to exclude the blocked stock from the optimizer input, we’re copying profile SAP001 into ZAP001 and assigning the Z03 category group we previ- ously created to the stock group for the optimizer input. The order categories included in the category groups are the only input PP/DS transac- tion data that will be read by the optimizer to perform the optimization calculations. 5 Production Planning 328 Figure 5.92 Category Profile for Production Planning Optimizer Input Data Production Planning Optimizer Profile The Production Planning Optimizer profile is the core of the Production Planning Opti- mizer where different settings are made that influence the way input data is deter- mined, and the calculations of costs during optimization. To set up the Production Planning Optimizer profile, follow SAP IMG menu path, SPRO  Advanced Planning  Production Planning Optimization  Basic Settings  Define PP Opti- mizer Profiles. In the initial screen of this transaction, you’ll see all the available opti- mizer profiles. You can create a new profile or copy the standard profile SAP_ALL to a custom profile and make changes to the settings. When you select and copy the stan- dard profile, you’ll see the next screen where you can enter a name and description to the profile. Click on the Maintain Profile button, which will take you to the Optimizer Profile Maintenance screen, as shown in Figure 5.93. At the top of the screen, you’ll see the optimization method. With the Linear Optimi- zation option, the constraints set in the General Constraints tab will only be consid- ered by the optimizer. With the Discrete Optimization method, the constraints listed in the Discrete Constraints tab, such as fixed resource consumption (which is usually the setup time and fixed material consumption in the PDS) will also be considered by the optimizer. As the discrete optimization process is performance intensive, it’s © 329 5.8 Leveraging the Production Planning Optimizer recommended to execute the discrete optimization for a shorter horizon. For the rest of the planning horizon, linear optimization can be executed. Figure 5.93 Production Planning Optimizer Profile: General Constraints In the General Constraints tab, the Production Capacity checkbox must be selected if you want the finite capacity of the production resources to be considered by the opti- mizer. Along with this checkbox, the resource should also be marked as a finite resource in the resource master for the optimizer to consider finite capacity. Maximum PDS Lot Size defines if the optimizer should consider the maximum lot size defined in the PDS as the production quantity per day and derive the quantities that can be pro- duced in one bucket based on the length of the bucket. The Optimizer Lot Formation dropdown field defines how quantities are split within a bucket to create planned orders. For example, with the Form Lots According to Settings value in this field, if the optimizer determines that a quantity of 100 is to be produced in a specific bucket, then this field drives how many planned orders needs to be created by the optimizer to meet the quantity of 100. The optimizer will check the material master fixed lot size first, then check the maximum lot size, and finally split the total 5 Production Planning 330 bucket quantity into different planned orders. Irrespective of the value in this field, the system will always consider the maximum and minimum lot sizes of the PDS and adjust the order quantities accordingly. If you want the system to consider the safety stock, select the Consider Safety Stock checkbox. The Consider Period Length for Safety Stock Penalty and Consider Period Length for Storage Costs checkboxes will calculate the penalty and costs based on the length of the bucket. For example, if the penalty is 100 per day and the bucket has 7 days, the total penalty for the quantity will be multiplied by 7 (days). The time-depen- dent maximum days of supply defined in Transaction /SAPAPO/TDS can be considered by the optimizer when the Time-Dependent Maximum Days of Supply checkbox is selected. Apart from this checkbox, the Time-Dependent DOS flag in the material mas- ter also needs to be selected in the Advanced Planning tab. The Bucket Offset fields define the availability of the receipt elements to meet the demand on time. A value between 0 and 1 can be defined in this field. Of these values, 1 is the most optimistic value, which means the receipt can be available at the end of the bucket and still the demand in the bucket is considered to be fulfilled on time. With 0, which is a conservative approach, and for demand in a bucket, the receipt should be available by end of the previous bucket for on-time fulfillment of the demand. For example, in a daily bucket scenario, with a 0.5 value for the offset, if the production duration is 15 hours, which is more than half a day—12 hours = Bucket duration (24 hours) × Offset (0.5)—the receipt should be available in the previous bucket for any demand within the current bucket to be considered as an on-time fulfilment. Finally, if there are supersession chains defined for product interchangeability, the optimizer will consider the interchangeability master data if the Supersession Chain checkbox is selected. In the Discrete Constraints tab, you’ll define the constraints that need to be respected with the Discrete Optimization method. As shown in Figure 5.94, the fields in this tab will only be editable when the Discrete Optimization method is selected. The values in the constraints are in terms of the duration in which the discrete constraint must be respected by the system. For example, the Discrete Production Capacity Increase field is set with value of 1 Y, which means the extended capacity defined in the resource master under the PPO Capacity Constraints tab will be leveraged by the optimizer for one year from the date of the optimizer execution. The Integral Production Lots field will ensure that the system creates orders with mul- tiples of the minimum lot size of the PDS. The Fixed Material and Resource Consump- tion field will consider the setup times and any other fixed consumption values defined in the PDS. The Sequence Dependent Lot Size field will enable the optimizer to consider the setup time and cost defined in the setup matrix. As of SAP S/4HANA 2022, only the setup matrix based on the setup groups is supported. © 331 5.8 Leveraging the Production Planning Optimizer Figure 5.94 Production Planning Optimizer Profile: Discrete Constraints Note The Production Planning Optimizer has limitations on the scenarios it can support. The elaborate list of such restrictions is provided in SAP Note 3226003 (SAP S/4HANA 2022). These restrictions will be relaxed in further releases of SAP S/4HANA. In the Solution Methods tab, you can define settings such as the maximum duration allowed for the optimizer to find the solution. For the optimization method, it’s recom- mended to use the Automatic Algorithm selection, so that the system can determine the correct algorithm for the optimization problem to be solved. In the Integration tab, you can define constraints for the demand generated by the existing firmed orders, for example, if there are firmed planned orders, and their com- ponents generate dependent demand. Incremental Optimization means that the opti- mization is being performed on top of a set of existing firmed orders. The following list shows the elements for which constraints can be defined for incremental optimization, as shown in Figure 5.95: 5 Production Planning 332  Dependent Demand for Fixed Orders Dependent demand from fixed planned orders.  Distribution Demand for Fixed Orders Demand generated in the source locations in stock transfer scenarios.  Substitution Demand for Fixed Orders Dependent demand generated by substitution planned orders that are created when product interchangeability (supersession chains) is defined for materials. Figure 5.95 Production Planning Optimizer Profile: Incremental Optimization Constraints For the preceding elements, you can select the following options to constrain the plan:  Regard as a hard constraint The dependent demand from fixed orders is considered a hard constraint. The sys- tem must fulfill such demands. If the plan becomes infeasible, the optimizer won’t find a solution.  Regard as a pseudo-hard constraint The optimizer may cause shortages for these dependent demands, but a high pen- alty cost is internally assigned by the optimizer to ensure that the shortages are only created when no other alternative plan is feasible.  Regard as a customer demand/Regard as demand forecast The dependent demands will be considered either as customer demand or forecast demand, and the penalties and nondelivery costs defined in the material master will be applied. © 333 5.8 Leveraging the Production Planning Optimizer The Stock of Non-Selected PDS Input Products field determines how the system should treat the stock of the materials that aren’t selected in the optimization run. For exam- ple, to produce P1, if C1, C2, and C3 components are required, and you’ve only selected P1, C1, and C2 in the optimization run, then this setting will determine whether the plan should be constrained with the availability of component C3 (which isn’t part of the selection) or the optimizer can assume infinite supply of C3 and plan P1. Similarly, in stock transfers, if the source locations aren’t selected in the optimization run, the Stock of Non-Selected Source Location Products field determines how the optimizer should treat the material availability in the source location. The Automatic Cost Generation tab enables the optimizer to determine the costs auto- matically based on the settings made in this tab. In the Automatic Cost Generation area at the top-right of the screen, the Enabled checkbox should be selected for this tab to be editable. When selected, the system doesn’t consider the costs defined in the master data and generates the costs automatically based on the settings maintained in the optimizer profile. This won’t change or update the costs defined in the master data during optimization using the automatic cost generation. Under the Consideration of Priorities area, you can define the priority for different demand classes such as customer demand, forecast demand, and safety stocks. The higher the priority, the more costs will be assigned for delay and nondelivery of the demand classes. In this example shown in Figure 5.96, the Priority Customer Requirement is set as 1, which means higher costs will be assigned by the optimizer automatically to the cus- tomer demands compared to the next priority item, which is the forecast demand. The priority defined in the material master Advanced Planning view also can be consid- ered by the system to generate higher costs for higher priority products by selecting the Priority of Location Products checkbox. The product priority is subdivided into three categories. In this example, products having priorities 1–100 will have a higher cost compared to the products having priority of 101–200. Costs based on the procure- ment priority defined in the PDS or in the transportation lane can also be generated by the optimizer by selecting the corresponding checkboxes. For products that don’t have any input components, such as raw materials, if you want to consider the actual stor- age cost defined in the material master, you can select the Costs of Products without Input Products checkbox. Note For the parallel reading of the PP/DS data and parallel updates of the results of the optimizer back to PP/DS, the parallel processing profile can be defined using IMG menu path SPRO  Advanced Planning  Production Planning Optimization  Define Parallel Processing Profile. To enable parallel processing of the optimizer execution itself, the number of parallel processes can be defined in the Production Planning Optimizer profile under the Extended Settings tab. The number of CPUs available in the optimizer server must be more than the number of parallel processes defined in the optimizer profile. 5 Production Planning 334 Figure 5.96 Production Planning Optimizer Profile: Automatic Cost Generation

לביצוע ה-Production Planning Optimizer, יש profiles בתצורה.

**Time Bucket Profile:** ה-optimizer מתכנן bucket-oriented, וה-receipts מתוזמנים ע"י ה-Detailed Scheduling Optimizer באותה ריצה. ה-profile מחלק את ה-horizon ל-buckets. למשל, 7 ימים ב-subdaily, 4 שבועות ב-daily, 2 חודשים ב-weekly. דרך menu path: ‏SPRO • Advanced Planning • Production Planning Optimization • Basic Settings • Define Time Bucket Profiles. לחצו Sub Daily Bucket Definition ID (Figure 5.89) — הזינו Start Time, ‏Subdaily Bucket Duration (8 שעות), ו-Repetitions/Day (3). להגדרת ה-profile, לחיצה כפולה על Time Bucket Profile Definition, צרו entry, ולחיצה כפולה על Time Units. הזינו Time Units ו-Time Unit Duration (Figure 5.90). ל-Subdaily Buckets, הזינו את ה-Sub Daily ID. ל-week, ‏Week Starts On.
**הערה:** אם לא הוזן horizon, ה-time bucket profile מחשב את הסוף מהתאריך הנוכחי.

**Category Profile:** מקבץ order categories (CC – stocks, ‏BM – sales orders) לאלמנטים (customer demand, ‏stocks, ‏firmed receipts) ומקצה ל-optimizer input categories. למשל, להחרגת blocked stocks (CI). דרך menu path: ‏... • Maintain Category Groups. ה-groups עם "O" תקניים. בחרו group, לחיצה כפולה על Categories. בדוגמה (Figure 5.91), העתקת O03 (Stock) ל-Z03 והסרת CI.
ב-category profile, מקצים את ה-groups לאלמנטים. דרך menu path: ‏... • Define Category Profiles (Figure 5.92). ‏SAP001 תקני. בדוגמה, העתקת SAP001 ל-ZAP001 והקצאת Z03 ל-stock group. רק ה-categories ב-groups נקראים ע"י ה-optimizer.

**Production Planning Optimizer Profile:** הליבה. דרך menu path: ‏... • Define PP Optimizer Profiles. צרו או העתיקו את SAP_ALL. לחצו Maintain Profile (Figure 5.93). למעלה, שיטת ה-optimization: ‏Linear Optimization (רק אילוצי General Constraints) או Discrete Optimization (גם Discrete Constraints, כגון fixed resource consumption). ‏discrete עתיר-ביצועים — מומלץ לאופק קצר.
בלשונית General Constraints, ה-Production Capacity checkbox (להתחשבות בקיבולת finite; ה-resource גם מסומן finite). ‏Maximum PDS Lot Size. ה-Optimizer Lot Formation dropdown קובע פיצול ל-planned orders (Form Lots According to Settings — בודק fixed lot size, אז max, ואז מפצל; תמיד מתחשב ב-max/min של ה-PDS). ‏Consider Safety Stock. ‏Consider Period Length for Safety Stock Penalty/Storage Costs (לפי אורך ה-bucket). ‏Time-Dependent Maximum Days of Supply (גם Time-Dependent DOS ב-material master). ה-Bucket Offset (0–1; ‏1 אופטימי = receipt בסוף ה-bucket עדיין on time; ‏0 שמרני). ‏Supersession Chain (interchangeability).
בלשונית Discrete Constraints (Figure 5.94), עורכים רק עם Discrete Optimization. הערכים במשך. ‏Discrete Production Capacity Increase (1 Y → extended capacity לשנה). ‏Integral Production Lots (מכפילים של min lot size). ‏Fixed Material and Resource Consumption (setup times). ‏Sequence Dependent Lot Size (setup time/cost מ-setup matrix; נכון ל-S/4HANA 2022, רק setup matrix מבוסס setup groups).
**הערה:** ל-Production Planning Optimizer מגבלות (SAP Note 3226003, S/4HANA 2022).
בלשונית Solution Methods, המשך המרבי לפתרון. מומלץ Automatic Algorithm. בלשונית Integration, אילוצים לביקוש מ-firmed orders. ‏Incremental Optimization = מיטוב על orders קיימים (Figure 5.95):
• **Dependent Demand for Fixed Orders**
• **Distribution Demand for Fixed Orders** — במיקומי source ב-stock transfer.
• **Substitution Demand for Fixed Orders** — מ-substitution planned orders (supersession chains).
אפשרויות לאילוץ:
• **Regard as a hard constraint** — חובה למלא. אם בלתי-ישים, אין פתרון.
• **Regard as a pseudo-hard constraint** — עלול למחסור, אך penalty גבוה.
• **Regard as a customer demand/Regard as demand forecast** — לפי ה-penalties וה-nondelivery costs.
ה-Stock of Non-Selected PDS Input Products קובע את הטיפול במלאי חומרים שלא נבחרו (למשל C3 שלא נבחר — האם להגביל או להניח אספקה אינסופית). בדומה ל-Stock of Non-Selected Source Location Products.
לשונית Automatic Cost Generation — קביעת עלויות אוטומטית. ה-Enabled checkbox. כשמסומן, המערכת אינה מתחשבת בעלויות ה-master data ומחוללת אוטומטית (ללא שינוי ה-master data). תחת Consideration of Priorities, עדיפות לכל demand class (גבוהה = יותר עלויות לעיכוב/אי-אספקה; Figure 5.96, ‏Priority Customer Requirement = 1). ה-Priority of Location Products checkbox (3 קטגוריות: 1–100 יקר יותר מ-101–200). עלויות לפי procurement priority ב-PDS/transportation lane. ‏Costs of Products without Input Products לחומרי גלם.
**הערה:** ל-parallel reading/updates, ‏parallel processing profile דרך menu path: ‏... • Define Parallel Processing Profile. להפעלת parallel processing של ה-optimizer עצמו, מספר התהליכים בלשונית Extended Settings (מספר ה-CPUs בשרת חייב להיות גבוה יותר).

sections.title: Executing the Production Planning Optimizer
sections.en: 5.8.3 Executing the Production Planning Optimizer The Production Planning Optimizer can be executed using Transaction /SAPAPO/PPO_ OPT or following SAP Easy Access menu path, Logistics  Advanced Planning  Produc- tion Planning  Automated Production Planning and Optimization  Production Planning Optimizer Run. The initial screen of this transaction is shown in Figure 5.97. Under Global Settings, you can enter the Planning Version and Propagation Range. Propagation Range restricts the system to include further products and resources that can be included in the optimization run based on the dependencies of products and resources defined in the selection for the optimization. In Planning Horizon, you can enter the Planning Start Date and Planning End Date within which the optimizer should select the demand and receipt elements and opti- mize the plan. If no planning horizon is entered, the planning horizon is derived from the time bucket profile. The Selection of Products area allows you to enter specific selection criteria of Product Number and Location, along with additional selection options such as Production Plan- ner and Planning Group set in the material master. © 335 5.8 Leveraging the Production Planning Optimizer Figure 5.97 Executing the Production Planning Optimizer The Settings for Optimizer area defines the various profiles that the optimizer should consider for the optimizer run. Enter the Optimizer Profile, Time Bucket Profile, and Category Profile. In addition, if parallel processing is to be leveraged for reading for the optimizer engine and writing back the data by the optimizer engine to PP/DS, enter the parallel processing profile in the Parallel Proc. Profi field. In the Production Planning Optimizer execution, it’s also possible to execute the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer immediately once the receipts are proposed by the Pro- duction Planning Optimizer. When these two optimizer engines are executed sepa- rately by scheduling two different optimization runs (one for Production Planning Optimizer and another for Detailed Scheduling Optimizer), it’s possible that Detailed Scheduling Optimizer will move orders beyond the buckets within which Production Planning Optimizer proposed these receipts by optimizing the cost. To avoid that, it’s 5 Production Planning 336 recommended to execute Detailed Scheduling Optimizer as part of the Production Planning Optimizer execution for the products which are planned using Production Planning Optimizer. With this option, Production Planning Optimizer will virtually modify the order validity dates of the receipts it generated with the start and end time stamp of the bucket within which the receipts were generated by the Production Plan- ning Optimizer. This will be passed to the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer, so the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer will try to schedule these orders within the bucket respecting the order validity dates. We’ll cover the details of the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer in Chapter 6 where we cover detailed scheduling topics. To leverage this option of combined Production Planning Optimizer and Detailed Scheduling Optimizer runs, under the Settings for DS Optimizer area of the screen, as shown in Figure 5.97, select the Execute DS Optimizer checkbox. Next, enter the DS Optimizer Profile, which must be used by the system to execute Detailed Scheduling Optimizer. If you want to allow Detailed Scheduling Optimizer to start the optimized schedule earlier than the set optimization start date, you can enter an offset in the number of minutes in the Scheduling Offset field. There can be a mix of finite, bottleneck, and infinite resources as part of the same order, belonging to different operations of the order. Respecting the bucket start for infinite resources may cause the finite operations to breach the bucket start and end. To relax this constraint, you can select which resources are expected to respect the bucket start in the Respect Bucket Start for field. In this example shown in Figure 5.97, only the bot- tleneck and finite resources are required to respect the bucket start. You can save the selection options in the Production Planning Optimizer selection screen in Transaction /SAPAPO/PPO_OPT and schedule a job in the background to exe- cute the optimizer.
