The scheduling mode used by this heuristic is Insert Operation, so the system will try to schedule the backlog operations as soon as possible closer to the current date by push- ing the already existing operations in the future direction and placing the backlog operations there. The remove backlog heuristic will only select the operations that are in backlog and then schedule them in the future, as shown in Figure 6.29. Here, you can see a working example of the remove backlog heuristic, both before execution 1 and after execution 2. The current date is represented by the dashed vertical line 3. Note the backlog oper- ations 4 and the operations scheduled in the future that are closer to the current date 5. In addition, the operations that are moved by this heuristic to place the backlog operations are also finitely sequenced on the resource. Other operations on the resource that aren’t impacted by the backlog operation rescheduling aren’t changed, so resource overload situations could still occur in periods that are far from the current date. 6 Detailed Scheduling 380 Figure 6.29 Remove Backlog Working Example The schedule sequence and/or remove backlog heuristics can be used just after the pro- duction planning run or when planned orders are sent from an external planning sys- tem (e.g., SAP IBP) to sequence the order and resolve backlogs and capacity overload for the selected resources. The run can be fine-tuned by a Detailed Scheduling Optimizer run or another detailed scheduling heuristic later.

sections.title: Schedule Operations
sections.en: 6.3.3 Schedule Operations The schedule operations (SAP005) heuristic can be used to schedule the deallocated operations (see Figure 6.30). Only the deallocated operations within the planning period defined are selected and then rescheduled according to the strategy profile assigned to the heuristic. Figure 6.30 Schedule Operations Heuristic Settings © 381 6.3 Leveraging Detailed Scheduling Heuristics The schedule sequence (SAP001) heuristic doesn’t schedule any deallocated operations on the selected resources; it only schedules operations with the Scheduled status. If there are business process scenarios where the production orders are created in SAP S/4HANA (e.g., via interfaces), then the production orders will be created with deallocated status in PP/DS by default. In such cases, the schedule operations (SAP005) can be executed as a first scheduling step to allocate resources to the orders and then do further finite sched- uling, as shown in our working example in Figure 6.31. Here, in the initial scheduling sit- uation in the top portion, you can see the scheduled operations 1 and the deallocated operations 2. After the schedule operations heuristic is executed, shown in the middle portion, only the deallocated operations are scheduled 3. Conversely, after the sequence operations heuristic is executed, shown in the bottom portion, all operations are sched- uled 4. Figure 6.31 Schedule Operations Working Example

sections.title: Minimize Runtime
sections.en: 6.3.4 Minimize Runtime Minimize runtime (SAP004) is another basic detailed scheduling heuristic that reduces the lead time of the orders. This heuristic can be executed for a resource. The opera- tions on the resources will be fixed by the system during the execution of the heuristic. So that the operations that are selected for this heuristic stay where they are, only the dependent operations are moved to reduce the lead time. 6 Detailed Scheduling 382 If the operations on the selected resource are scheduled infinitely before the start of this heuristic, they remain in the same state after the execution too. Therefore, it’s important that the schedule sequence heuristic or another finite scheduling heuristic is executed before the execution of the minimize runtime heuristic. From there, the system will move all other operations dependent on the fixed operation within the propagation range and will try to minimize any unnecessary gaps between these oper- ations. After the best possible lead time reduction is achieved for all the orders, then the operations that were fixed initially are unfixed. All the operations must be in the planning period for this heuristic to schedule them closer to each other. If there are backlogs, those aren’t rescheduled by this heuristic. The scheduling mode used by this heuristic is Find Slot. Figure 6.32 shows the operations with gaps in the past 1, followed by the current date 2. The gaps between operations in the past are shown as GP, and the gaps between the operations in the future are shown as GF. In addition, there are resource overloads in the past 3 and in the future 4. Figure 6.32 Minimize Runtime Heuristic: Initial Scheduling State Example Figure 6.33 shows the screen after the heuristic is executed. The heuristics was exe- cuted by selecting resource WS4_FIN1_PPS1_001. So the operations in this resource will remain wherever they are, and the dependent operations (on resource WS4_FIN2_ PPS2_001) are moved to close the gaps. Figure 6.33 Minimize Runtime Heuristic: After Heuristics Execution Example © 383 6.3 Leveraging Detailed Scheduling Heuristics The operations with gaps in the past remain as they are 1. However, on the right side, you can see that the order lead time has been reduced by removing the gaps between operations of the same orders 2 (the operations with resource overload remain the same, but the gaps are closed 3). In the heuristic settings, in the strategy parameters for the dependent objects, you can set the Sched. Submode to Schedule Dependent Operations According to Scheduling Mode. This will schedule the dependent opera- tions using a finite scheduling strategy. But the resource that was selected to execute this heuristic will remain as it is, even if there are capacity overloads.

sections.title: Multilevel Scheduling Framework Heuristics
sections.en: 6.3.5 Multilevel Scheduling Framework Heuristics The detailed scheduling heuristics we’ve seen so far can be used for scheduling back- logs, scheduling deallocated orders, and sequencing the operation on the finite resources. After the production planning run and one or more heuristics from the schedule sequence, schedule operations, and remove backlog, the schedule can be fine- tuned further, for example, by Detailed Scheduling Optimizer (Section 6.5). These steps can be executed every week as background jobs to ensure the demands are fulfilled on time with optimized resource utilization. The multilevel scheduling framework offers heuristics that can navigate through the pegging structure and schedule the orders from the lowest level to the highest level. The following heuristics are available in the multilevel scheduling framework:  Stable forward scheduling  Enhanced backward scheduling  Change fixing/planning intervals We’ll discuss each in the following sections. Stable Forward Scheduling The stable forward scheduling (SAP_DS_01) heuristic is used to perform multilevel finite scheduling. Manufacturing schedule disruptions such as backlogs, capacity over- loads, and violations of the minimum intervals for the orders can be corrected in sev- eral levels of production by this heuristic. This heuristic and the enhanced backward scheduling heuristic can be executed in short-term horizons after a finite schedule has arrived using another scheduling tool such as Detailed Scheduling Optimizer. These heuristics aim to resolve short-term problems that arise after an initial finite schedul- ing such as a backlog of orders, backward pegging (e.g., the order for the semifinished product is scheduled after the finished product order), or any resource breakdowns (downtimes) impacting the order schedule. The heuristics parameters for the stable forward scheduling heuristic are shown in Figure 6.34. 6 Detailed Scheduling 384 Figure 6.34 Stable Forwarding Heuristic Settings The Start Date for Scheduling is the earliest date and time from which the system can start scheduling orders on the resource. This option, along with the Scheduling Offset option in the heuristic settings, has different behavior based on which dates and times are set in the heuristic settings. If the start date time is entered for the Start Date for Scheduling field, and if a Schedul- ing Offset is entered, then the system ignores the scheduling offset. The start date for scheduling is set as the start date/time for scheduling. Following is the behavior for other combinations of scheduling start date/time and off- set time:  With only start time Schedule start = Current date at the scheduling start time set.  With only start date Schedule start = Start date at 00:00:00 hours.  With start time and offset Offset is applied first to calculate the schedule start date, and the entered start time in the Customizing is set as the start time for the scheduled start. If you select the value for the Handling of Deallocated Operations option as No Selec- tion or Scheduling of Deallocated Operations, the deallocated operations aren’t © 385 6.3 Leveraging Detailed Scheduling Heuristics selected and therefore not scheduled. However, if operations on which these deallo- cated operations are dependent are rescheduled, then the deallocated operations will be updated with the date and time so that they stay closer to the operations being rescheduled. The Use Earliest Dates setting has two options:  All Operations Use Earliest Dates Irrespective of the start date/time of the operations, all operations are scheduled one after another on the resource starting the scheduling start date/time. There will be no gaps left on the resource after the heuristic execution with this setting. If your planning period has a longer horizon, this setting will reschedule all orders to start at the earliest possible date on the resource from which this heuristic is executed. You should use this setting only with a limited planning period (very short-term horizon).  Operations in the Past Use Earliest Dates The operations that are backlogged (start date older than current date) will be rescheduled to start from the scheduling start date/time, and other operations on the resource won’t be pulled toward the earliest date. The backlog operations when rescheduled may cause resource overloads due to the already existing operations on the resource; in that case, the existing operations (which aren’t backlogged) are also rescheduled. Finiteness Lvl can be entered to decide which resources are finitely scheduled during this heuristic’s execution. This heuristic reads the whole pegging structure from the selected operation (and all operations of the same order) or the operations and all the orders of these operations when the heuristic is executed with resource selection. Then, forward scheduling is executed starting with the lower-level manufacturing orders (orders for the semifinished products first and then the higher-level orders). For the externally procured materials, this heuristic executes a postprocessing step to set the procurement order dates as close as possible to the manufacturing requirements. The propagation range must allow the heuristics to work across the pegging hierarchy. If orders/operations are outside the pegging hierarchy, an error message is raised during the execution of the heuristics. The stable forward scheduling heuristic resolves the following issues in the schedule:  Backlogs Resolve backlogs by scheduling forward from the current date.  Capacity overloads Finite scheduling on all levels of the pegging structure ensures that capacity over- loads are resolved.  Violation of minimum spacing between orders/operations Violations of the minimum intervals between operations are handled. 6 Detailed Scheduling 386 An example of the heuristic resolving the scheduling issues across the pegging struc- ture is shown in Figure 6.35 and Figure 6.36. In Figure 6.35, the order number ending with 370 is the finished product order, the order ending with 371 is the next level semi- finished product, and the order ending with 372 is the last level in the bill of materials (BOM) structure. You can see the operations in the backlog (with a start date in the past) 1. Then, there is a backward pegging with lower-level order (372) scheduled after higher-level orders (371) 2. Finally, you can see that more gaps exist between opera- tions of the same order on the right side 3. The nonworking times (weekend of January 14 and 15) are hidden to demonstrate this example. Figure 6.35 Stable Forward Scheduling Heuristic: Initial Scheduling State Example Figure 6.36 shows the situation after the stable forward scheduling heuristic has been executed. The resource WS4_MLTB3 (the lowest level resource in the pegging structure) was selected, and the stable forward heuristics was executed. Then, the gap between the operations 10 and 20 of the order ending with 370 is removed 1. The backlog order 371 is rescheduled to the future 2. The backward pegging between the orders 372 and 371 is also resolved 3. As the heuristic only has the start time entered as 00:00:00 (refer to Figure 6.34), the heuristic started scheduling the order from the current date (16.0.2023) start of the working time (08:00:00). Figure 6.36 Stable Forward Scheduling Heuristic: After Heuristic Execution Example © 387 6.3 Leveraging Detailed Scheduling Heuristics Enhanced Backward Scheduling The enhanced backward scheduling heuristic (SAP_DS_02) also finitely schedules the operations across the pegging structure. This heuristic is delivered with the standard algorithm /SAPAPO/SFW_HEUR_BW_EXT. This heuristic schedules the operations in a backward direction. The current date’s available capacity isn’t considered as available by this heuristic, so during backward scheduling, the current date’s operations may result in getting scheduled in the past. Therefore, it’s important that after the enhanced backward scheduling heuristic, the stable forward heuristic is also executed. The enhanced backward scheduling heuristic offers additional settings compared to the stable forward heuristics. The available Enhanced Backward Scheduling heuristic settings are shown in Figure 6.37. If there is no available capacity on the resource, which is the cur- rent mode of the operation (activity) chosen in the Mode Selection setting, the alternative modes (if available for the operation) can be evaluated by the heuristic, and the mode with highest priority and available capacity for the desired date/time is selected. Figure 6.37 Enhanced Backward Scheduling Heuristic Settings 6 Detailed Scheduling 388 The setup time (changeover) required by the operations on the resources can be reduced by choosing Take Set-Up Sequences into Account in the Setup Sequence field in the heuristic. Additional filters are available to filter the order available-to-promise (ATP) categories and order priorities, so that only the important orders can be scheduled using this heu- ristic. During manufacturing, there could be unplanned changes to the schedule due to scraps, machine breakdowns, or the last-minute need for a high-priority order to be executed. During such situations, a robust scheduling tool is required that can aid the production scheduler with rescheduling operations on resources that went to backlog, caused resource overloads, or violated the minimum interval requirements between the operations. In such cases, the enhanced backward scheduling and stable forward scheduling heuristics can be used to reschedule the orders (resource) impacted and propagate the scheduling change across the pegging network up to the finished mate- rial level. By doing so, this heuristic may violate delivery dates and planned indepen- dent requirements (PIR) dates. Create Planning/Fixing Intervals The create planning/fixing intervals heuristics (SAP_DS_03) is provided to set, change, and delete the planning and fixing intervals on resources. This heuristic uses the stan- dard algorithm /SAPAPO/HEUR_REL_FIXINT_MAINT. This heuristic takes the current date as a base and sets the planning and fixing intervals based on the heuristic settings. Let’s walk through the settings for both fixing and planning intervals, as follows:  Fixing Interval A fixing interval is created to lock the resource capacity for the defined duration and fix all the orders and operations that are scheduled within the fixing interval. This is to protect the capacity for the scheduled operations in the very short-term horizon and not allow any other operations to get scheduled in the fixing interval, which may disturb the existing schedule. Sequence-dependent setup activities can also be deactivated within the fixing inter- val. When there are setup activities that have setup groups, and the sequence of the operations are changed, the setup time required also changes based on the setup times defined for changeovers. Such setup activities are called sequence-dependent setup activities. Within the very short-term horizon, if operations are moved to han- dle shop floor uncertainties, redetermination of the setup times may lead to a major change in the schedule. When fixing intervals are created using the create planning/ fixing intervals heuristic, you can deactivate the sequence-dependent setup activi- ties, meaning that when sequence-dependent activities are moved, the setup time isn’t redetermined. © 389 6.3 Leveraging Detailed Scheduling Heuristics  Planning Interval Planning interval is the duration within which the system can carry out scheduling. Outside the planning interval, the system considers the resource to be fixed, so it won’t select or perform any scheduling actions for the objects outside the planning interval. The heuristics settings provide the Relative Interval Dates/Times option for the heuris- tic execution (see Figure 6.38). This relative duration is used to calculate the planning or fixing interval from the current date. Figure 6.38 Create Planning/Fixing Intervals Heuristic Settings The Interval Type options determine if the heuristic execution should create a planning or fixing interval. The Function options determine whether to replace an existing interval 6 Detailed Scheduling 390 (Replace Intervals), add a new interval to an existing interval or create a new interval (Add Interval), or delete the intervals (Delete All Intervals). When a fixing interval is used, the options for deactivating the sequence-dependent setup activity are provided, and the operation can be fixed within the fixing interval. When the setup activities are deactivated, the start date of the fixing interval will be deactivated, and it will fix the resource from the past to the fixing interval end date. Figure 6.39 shows a working example of the fixed and planned intervals when the heu- ristics are executed per the settings maintained in Figure 6.38. For the fixing interval heuristics, note the current date 1, and the resource is fixed from the past to one day in the future from the current date (until 00:00:00 time) 2. For the planning interval heuristic execution in the bottom portion, you can see that the fixing interval is applied from the past to one day in the future (from current date 1) 2, and the fixing interval is also applied after three days 3 from the start of the planning interval (17.01.2023 00:00:00). This results in the three days of the planning interval 4. Figure 6.39 Working Model of the Create Fixing and Planning Interval Heuristic

sections.title: Multiresource Scheduling Heuristic
sections.en: 6.3.6 Multiresource Scheduling Heuristic The multiresource scheduling heuristic can be used in scenarios where alternative modes (resources) are available for manufacturing materials. Many of the detailed scheduling heuristics and scheduling functions offer switching modes (resources) if there are alternative modes available in the PDS and the primary mode doesn’t have enough capacity. Apart from switching alternative modes of the same PDS activity, with the multire- source scheduling heuristic, it’s also possible to switch to resources that are alternative PDSs. Example The PDS for material A has an operation (resource R1) with one alternative mode (resource R2). In addition, there are two more PDSs available for the same material A, and the other two PDSs use two different resources (PDS2/resource R3, PDS3/resource © 391 6.3 Leveraging Detailed Scheduling Heuristics R4) other than the original PDS. In case of a resource overload, the multiresource sched- uling heuristic can schedule the operations on R2, R3, or R4, based on the mode priori- ties (alternative modes and alternative sources of supply are considered). The multiresource scheduling heuristic is delivered with the name SAP_MULT_SCH and algorithm /SAPAPO/HEU_MULTIRES_SCHED. This can be copied to another cus- tom heuristic to adjust per the requirements. The settings are shown in Figure 6.40. Figure 6.40 Multiresource Scheduling Heuristic Settings The Planning mode can be bucket capacity–oriented (1) or time-continuous finite capacity-based scheduling (2). With the Planning direction of forward (F), the order start dates are considered for scheduling the order; with backward (B), the order end date is set, and then the order is backward scheduled. The Period definition is a critical field for this heuristic with options of days (D) or weeks (W). The Max. number of periods backwards defines the number of days/weeks in the backward direction during which the system should perform finite scheduling. The 6 Detailed Scheduling 392 PPM/PDS switch periods option refers to the number of days/weeks in which the sys- tem can schedule the impacted orders (due to resource overload) in the past before it tries to switch the PDS to schedule the orders on alternative resources. If all the modes of the current PDS of the order and the modes from the alternative PDS have the same priority, the alternative mode of the current PDS will be given the first priority before switching to alternative PDSs. For longer horizons in which this heuristic is executed, the system might only schedule the high-priority orders first without scheduling any other orders. To avoid this, the period block can be used. The planning period will be divided into a number of period blocks, and orders within the blocks are scheduled independently. A working example of the multiresource scheduling heuristic is shown in Figure 6.41. In this example, the heuristic was executed from the detailed scheduling planning board, but it can also be executed from the production planning run as a step. The heuristic settings from Figure 6.40 are used for executing this example. Figure 6.41 Multiresource Scheduling Heuristic Example © 393 6.3 Leveraging Detailed Scheduling Heuristics You can see in Figure 6.41 that there are multiple PDSs for the same material 1, which have the following modes/resource:  PDS 1, mode 1 WS4PP_WS3_PPS2_001  PDS 2, mode 1 WS4PP_WS4_PPS2_001  PDS 3, mode 1 WS4PP_WS1_PPS2_001 (all the orders in the example use this PDS/mode 2)  PDS 3, mode 2 WS4PP_WS5_PPS2_001 Then, the current scheduling situation shows an overload on the WS1 resource 2. After the heuristic is executed, you can see the overload is resolved 3. The system scheduled the orders from the overload date (23.01.2023) until 19.01.2023 (five days from 23.01.2023) as the scheduling direction in this example is backward scheduling. After it finitely scheduled the orders on the original mode where the orders were placed before for the five-day periods, then it scheduled the orders by switching the mode belonging to other PDSs of the same product and alternative modes of the PDSs. Note To get proper results from this heuristic, when using the period definition of D, the order length should be less than one day, and with weekly period definition, the order length should be less than a week. This heuristic is designed for process industries, but it can be also used for other scenarios, keeping this restriction in mind.

sections.title: Demand-Driven Scheduling (DDMRP Schedule Sequence)
sections.en: 6.3.7 Demand-Driven Scheduling (DDMRP Schedule Sequence) Demand-driven MRP (DDMRP) is a planning methodology based on the actual usage of the materials and setting-up buffer levels at strategic positions in a multilevel BOM structure or stock transfer location. The DDMRP solution is part of SAP S/4HANA. We won’t cover the detailed setup of DDMRP in SAP S/4HANA, which is out of scope of this book, but we will cover the concept of DDMRP briefly and how the DDMRP calculated buffer levels are leveraged by PP/DS for scheduling the orders on bottleneck resources, which produces DDMRP and non-DDMRP materials. The DDMRP process comprises the following steps:  Buffer positioning Buffer positioning is identifying the strategic positions across BOM levels or stock transfer locations. For example, if a product has five levels of BOM till the last raw material level, a change in the demand for the finished product will have an impact in the plan and schedule for all semifinished products in the BOM level and the raw material. If the third-level semifinished material is used by multiple other products 6 Detailed Scheduling 394 and has a long manufacturing lead time, any change in the plan or schedule will have a bigger impact in the production of this third-level semifinished material. So, if this semifinished material is activated for advanced planning, the manufacturing of this material isn’t driven by the demand of the finished product but based on the buffer levels calculated by the DDMRP process using its historical daily usage and lead time among other factors considered by DDMRP. In the buffer positioning step, the DDMRP process identifies such critical positions in the supply chain and classi- fies such materials for DDMRP buffer calculation.  Buffer sizing The materials identified for the strategic positioning of buffers in the preceding step will go through the buffer sizing process. These buffer sizes are calculated by the DDMRP process considering the parameters such as daily average usage, decoupled lead time (the lead time to manufacture the buffered material, including the lead time of any externally procured materials needed for the manufacturing), and other formula parameters set in the DDMRP configuration. The buffers are calculated in red, yellow, and green zones. The top of the red buffer level is the safety stock, the top of the yellow zone is the reorder point, and the top of the green zone is the maximum stock level. For example, if the DDMRP processes calculate 100 as top of red, 200 as top of yellow, and 400 as top of green, as soon as the stock goes below the top of yellow (200), a replenishment order is triggered to procure materials to reach the top of green (400). The buffer sizing step will calculate the size of buffers for these three zones.  Replenishment planning and replenishment execution Replenishment planning is executed to calculate the quantity of the materials to be produced or externally procured based on the buffer sizing and the current inven- tory, demand, and supply situation. In PP/DS, the heuristic named SAP_DD_SCHED with the algorithm /SAPAPO/DD_ SCHEDULE_HEURISTIC is delivered in the standard system. This heuristic will con- sider the buffer levels calculated by DDMRP in the finite scheduling process. We’ll walk through an example in Figure 6.42 in which it makes sense to use the DDMRP schedule sequence heuristics and how the scheduling is performed by the sys- tem. Product S4DD_FERT1 is a buffered material, and it has semifinished product S4NDD_HALB1. Product S4NDD_FERT1 is a nonbuffered material, and it has semifin- ished product S4DD_HALB1, which is a buffered material. And another finished prod- uct S4NDD_FERT3 and its semifinished material S4NDD_HALB2 are both nonbuffered materials. As you see in Figure 6.42, all of these semifinished products are manufac- tured using work center S4_DDR_W. Work center S4_DDR is a bottleneck resource that controls the pace in which all the finished goods are manufactured. When there are orders for all these semifinished products to be scheduled on the same work center (PP/DS resource), the DDMRP schedule sequence heuristics can be helpful to prioritize the orders based on the buffer levels calculated by DDMRP, and for the nonbuffered materials a slack time–based priority calculation will derive the priority percentage. © 395 6.3 Leveraging Detailed Scheduling Heuristics Figure 6.42 Demand-Driven PP/DS Scheduling Heuristics: Example Scenario The PP/DS scheduling priority is calculated as a percentage number, and the lowest percentage value calculated as the priority has the first priority on the resource and will be scheduled on the resource. The priority is calculated at the start of the scheduling time stamp as the reference for the calculation of the total receipts, demands, and on- hand stock. The priority is calculated for the operations of orders that are part of the selection. Based on the priority calculated, the system prioritizes one operation and schedules it. Then, the end of this scheduled operation becomes the reference time stamp for calculating the priority for the rest of the operations, and the next operation is scheduled. This iteration will be performed till all the relevant operations are sched- uled on the resource. For the DDMRP buffered products, the following formula is applied to calculate the priority: Priority in percent = (Projected stock/Safety stock) × 100 The projected stock is calculated as: Projected stock = Sum of receipts – Actual demands + On-hand stock The receipts in the preceding formula are from orders and operations that aren’t part of operations selected to be scheduled using this heuristic, for example, fixed opera- tions that can’t be rescheduled by this heuristic. If an order with at least one operation on the resource being scheduled uses this heuristic, the receipt quantity from this order will be considered only if the receipt time is before the reference time stamp for scheduling. Similarly, for orders for the product using a different source of supply that doesn’t consist of the resource on which this heuristic is being executed, the receipt quantity will only be considered if the receipt time is before the reference time stamp. All the actual demands that are placed before the reference time stamp will be consid- ered by this heuristic to calculate the projected stock. The configuration of the DDMRP S4DD_FERT1 S4NDD_FERT1 S4NDD_FERT3 S4NDD_HALB1 S4DD_HALB1 S4NDD_HALB2 S4HANA_PPDS_RAW001 Work Center S4_DDR_W Buffered DDMRP Material Legend: Materials Not Relevant for DDMRP 6 Detailed Scheduling 396 MRP type in SAP S/4HANA determines which demands (among demand elements such as stock transfer requirements, dependent requirements, etc.) are considered as actual demands. For the order operations from nonbuffered materials, which are scheduled along with the operations of the DDMRP buffered materials, we’ll now discuss the options avail- able to calculate the priority percentage. In the heuristic settings, as shown in Figure 6.43, the General Strategy Parameters and the Strategy Parameters f. Dependent Objects contain the settings such as the scheduling mode, scheduling direction, and so on, similar to other scheduling heuristics. In the Scheduling Parameters tab, there are special settings that influence the way the orders (operations) are scheduled consider- ing a calculated priority. Figure 6.43 Heuristic Settings: DDMRP Schedule Sequence Heuristics Under the Priority of Non-Buffered Product, the following options are available for the nonbuffered materials:  Dynamic(1.Downstream Buffer/2.Slack Time) With this option, when a nonbuffered product’s order operation is encountered by this heuristic, it checks the pegging structure to check if the pegged order to the order being scheduled has DDMRP buffering enabled. If there are any orders in the pegging structure toward the final order at the top of the pegging structure, the © 397 6.3 Leveraging Detailed Scheduling Heuristics priority for the pegged order is calculated and propagated to the operation being scheduled by this heuristic. If there are no materials in the pegging structure, then the following formula is applied to calculate the priority percentage. Priority in percent = ([{Priority adjustment factor × (Due date – Reference time stamp)} ÷ Order duration] – 1) × 100 The priority adjustment factor can help in situations where the difference between the due date and the reference time stamp is equal to the order duration. If the adjustment factor is 1, the calculated priority will be 0%. But if the adjustment factor is set as 1.4, the priority will be 40%. This denotes that a delay of 40% of the order’s duration is acceptable during scheduling. The due date is the earliest requirement date of all the pegged requirements to the order being scheduled by the heuristic. As shown in Figure 6.44, the heuristic is scheduling operations from orders 1, 2, and 3. The system calculates the priority based 01/01/2023 as the reference time stamp and determined the operation of the order 1 to be scheduled first. Based on the length (2 days) of order 1, now the refer- ence time stamp shifts to 01/03/2023. Now the system calculates the priority for orders 2 and 3. If order 2 is from a nonbuffered product and the adjustment factor is set as 1, the priority will be calculated for order 2, using the following formula factors: – Due date = 01/07/2023 (the date of the earliest demand pegged) – Reference time stamp = 01/03/2023 – (Due date – Reference time stamp) = 96 hours – Order duration = 24 hours (1 day) – {Priority adjustment factor × (Due date – Reference time stamp)} = {1× (96)} = 96 – ([{Priority adjustment factor × (Due date – Ref time stamp)} ÷ Order duration] – 1) = [96/24] – 1 = 3 So, priority in percentage = 3 × 100 = 300%. Figure 6.44 Example for Priority Calculation Using Slack Time Order 1 01/01/ 2023 01/02/ 2023 01/03/ 2023 01/04/ 2023 01/05/ 2023 01/06/ 2023 01/07/ 2023 Order 2 Demand 2 Reference Time Stamp 01/08/ 2023 Demand 3 Order 3 6 Detailed Scheduling 398  Slack Time only With this option for the nonbuffered materials, the priority percentage is calculated as explained previously using the slack time, irrespective of any DDMRP buffered materials being part of the pegging chain toward the top-level order. This heuristic can be executed interactively from scheduling tools such as the detailed scheduling planning board or the resource planning table. The Detailed Log checkbox under the Miscellaneous section of the heuristic settings (refer to Figure 6.43) can be switched on to display the detailed calculation of priorities in the appli- cation log of the heuristic execution, as shown in Figure 6.45. Figure 6.45 Detailed Log for Priority Calculation in DDMRP Schedule Sequence Heuristics

sections.title: Triggering PP/DS Scheduling
sections.en: 6.4 Triggering PP/DS Scheduling The PP/DS detailed scheduling heuristics and functions can be executed as part of the production planning job and interactively from the detailed scheduling planning board, the resource planning table, and the product planning table. Apart from executing the heuristics in the background and in online mode to schedule the operations on the resources, another important aspect of detailed scheduling is to monitor the scheduling results from the scheduling tools and to adjust them to resolve any issues found even after the scheduling runs. During the heuristic execution, depending on the strategy settings, there could be operations scheduled infinitely for dependent operations due to the error tolerance set © 399 6.4 Triggering PP/DS Scheduling in the strategy profile of the heuristics, or operations may be deallocated as part of the heuristics. Such exceptions can be displayed from the detailed scheduling planning board, and the production scheduler needs to schedule those operations. With embedded PP/DS, new SAP Fiori apps are available to monitor the resource utili- zation and change the shift schedule from the app itself to manage the resource capac- ity. In addition, you can dispatch and deallocate operations on the resources and simulate the results before the changes are saved in the system. The Advanced Sched- uling Board SAP Fiori app is delivered in embedded PP/DS to perform detailed schedul- ing activities. The Advanced Scheduling Board app has limited functionality compared to the SAP GUI–based detailed scheduling planning board. However, the app contains the functionalities required to execute and monitor basic scheduling. We’ll discuss each of these execution options and apps in the following sections.

sections.title: Detailed Scheduling Planning Board
sections.en: 6.4.1 Detailed Scheduling Planning Board The detailed scheduling planning board is one of the important tools production schedulers use to visualize the schedule and adjust it by dragging and dropping opera- tions onto the required resources on the timeline. Objects such as operations and orders are color-coded to make it easy for schedulers to identify different objects based on their status (e.g., scheduled operations vs. deallocated operations are displayed with different colors and patterns). Graphical representation of the scheduling situation and interactively simulating the resolution for the scheduling problems identified are the main objectives when using the detailed scheduling planning board. Multiple charts can be loaded onto the detailed scheduling planning board to display the current scheduling satiation of the resources, the orders against the materials loaded on the detailed scheduling planning board, stocks over time, and so on. These charts can be switched on and off per the requirements from the detailed scheduling planning board profiles and can be interactively changed in the detailed scheduling planning board transaction itself. The settings and the constraints maintained in the strategy profile are the core driving the behavior of the interactive scheduling changes made on the detailed scheduling planning board. You can save the adjusted schedule into a simulation version, which later can be merged back into the active version by loading the simulation version onto the detailed scheduling planning board and adopting it to the active version. Planning Board Selection Screen The detailed scheduling planning board can be launched via Transaction /SAPAPO/ CSPS0 or from SAP Easy Access menu, Logistics  Advanced Planning  Production Plan- ning  Interactive Production Planning  Detailed Scheduling  Detailed Scheduling Plan- ning Board – Variable View. The selection screen of the detailed scheduling planning board is displayed in Figure 6.46. 6 Detailed Scheduling 400 Figure 6.46 Detailed Scheduling Planning Board: Selection Screen The various profiles used in the detailed scheduling planning board, such as the detailed scheduling strategy profile, heuristics profile, planning board profile, work area, and propagation range, are assigned to the overall profile. (We’ve covered the overall profile customization in Chapter 3, Section 3.6.1.) By assigning the Overall Pro- file to the detailed scheduling planning board selection screen, all other relevant pro- files are loaded per the customization. The detailed scheduling planning board can be used for active planning version 000 or for inactive planning versions. To use the detailed scheduling planning board to work with the active planning version data, enter “000” in the Plng Version field. The Time Profile assigned to the overall profile prefills the planning and display periods in the selection screen, which can be manually overwritten. The display period is the period for the duration used by the objects loaded onto the detailed scheduling plan- ning board. But making changes to the schedule either by manually rescheduling or © 401 6.4 Triggering PP/DS Scheduling using a function or heuristics within the detailed scheduling planning board can only be performed for the planning period defined in the selection screen. Work Area is like a selection variant where the selection criteria for the resources, prod- ucts, and orders are already entered and saved. Therefore, you, as a production sched- uler, can create your own work area with the resources and products you’re responsible for scheduling. The selection criteria filled in by the work area also can be overwritten manually. Tip After changing the selection criteria for the resources, products, and orders, you can save it to a new work area by clicking the Save button to the right of the Work Area field on the selection screen. In the Resource tab, set the Selected Resources checkbox to load only the resources you’ve entered explicitly in the selection criteria, manually, or from the Work Area definition. If you don’t set this indicator, the system will load additional resources derived as follows:  The selected resources and corresponding operations on the resource are loaded.  From the operations, the orders are loaded, and from the orders, the system deter- mines the other resources used by the orders (operations).  From the operations and orders, the system loads the products in the product chart, and the resources corresponding to other orders (operations) of the loaded products are also displayed in the resource chart. You should select the Selected Resources checkbox to ensure that the volume of data loaded onto the detailed scheduling planning board is predictable and doesn’t lead to poor performance of loading and subsequent processing of the detailed scheduling planning board. The same is applicable for the selection of materials entered in the Product tab of the selection screen. Select the Selected Products checkbox to restrict the selection of prod- ucts by the explicitly entered materials in the selection. If the order/operation network display (pegging and order-internal relationship links) is activated in the detailed scheduling planning board profile by not setting the check- box in the No Display column for the Network View: Operations and Network View: Orders, as shown in Figure 6.47, the selected resource or selected product setting is ignored by the system, and the order network and corresponding resources and mate- rials are loaded. The detailed scheduling planning board performance is impacted by the volume of data loaded and the number of charts loaded during start-up. To improve performance, use time segments in the time profile definition so that the data is loaded in segments 6 Detailed Scheduling 402 as you work in the detailed scheduling planning board and navigate through the resource time stream (scroll through the time scale). (Refer to Chapter 3, Section 3.6.2, for more information on time segments.) The reading of the SAP liveCache data for the display of the detailed scheduling planning board can be improved by selecting the Perf.Func. checkbox. To select this checkbox, click on the Profiles button in the selec- tion screen menu bar (refer to the top of Figure 6.46), and in the Plng Board Profile tab of the popup screen, select the Perf.Func. checkbox on the bottom-left part of the screen (see Figure 6.47). You can hide the charts in the detailed scheduling planning board by setting the No Display checkbox on the detailed scheduling planning board profile, as shown in Figure 6.47. After the right selection settings are made, click on the Execute button to load the planning board. Figure 6.47 Detailed Scheduling Planning Board Selection of Charts to Be Displayed, and Setting the Performance Function Planning Board Navigation The detailed scheduling planning board, as shown in Figure 6.48, opens with the shuf- fler on the left side of the screen, which has the list of resources under the Resource Pool and a list of products under the Product Pool. You can display or hide resources and products from the corresponding charts by selecting the resource and clicking on the show or hide buttons in the shuffler 1. The shuffler can be hidden by clicking on the Display/Hide Shuffler button on the menu bar 2. © 403 6.4 Triggering PP/DS Scheduling From the menu bar, you can navigate to the settings and perform actions such as reschedule or deallocate selected operations. Manually performed scheduling changes within the detailed scheduling planning board can be undone by using the Undo Last Scheduling Function button in the menu bar. You can navigate to the menu bar path More settings to manage all the settings for the display and function of the detailed scheduling planning board, as shown in Figure 6.48. Figure 6.48 Detailed Scheduling Planning Board: Navigation Tip If you want to change the detailed scheduling strategy profile, click on the DS Strategy button in the menu bar. In the dialog popup for the strategy settings, click on the Expert View on the bottom-right corner of the screen to display all available strategy settings. Depending of the average duration of the orders, you can set the granularity for the timelines on the chart. If your orders are smaller (less than a day), you may set the time scale as days; for working with resources with bigger orders, the time scale can be set to weekly or monthly display. This can be changed from the menu bar settings, as well as by right-clicking (context menu) on the time bar on the individual charts, as shown in Figure 6.48 3. The toolbar 4 can be customized, which is covered in Chapter 3, Section 3.6.4. Further additional settings for the detailed scheduling planning board display and functions can be accessed by clicking on the More button in the menu bar and clicking on the Settings option. 6 Detailed Scheduling 404 Context Menu In the detailed scheduling planning board, many of the available functions for the objects (resources, products, and operations/orders) are provided in the context menu (right-click on the objects to access these menus). You can click on the context menu of Resource to expand the display, as shown in Fig- ure 6.49, if there is more than one order scheduled at the same time on the resource via the Expand Multiple Loading option. You can also Define Downtimes on the resources and create/change/delete fixing intervals with the Define Fixing Intervals option. Figure 6.49 Resource Context Menu On the product chart, the context menu provides options to navigate to production planning transactions such as the product or pegging overview of the product. You can load additional charts for displaying the product stock, and so on from the context menu. The context menu of the orders and operation objects provides most of the pos- sible actions for an order/operation. Planning Board Features The color and shape of the objects displayed in the detailed scheduling planning board are configurable as covered in Chapter 3, Chapter 3.6.4. If you want to know what the © 405 6.4 Triggering PP/DS Scheduling object symbols represent, you can choose More  Extras  Legend. The legend lists the charts and individual graphical objects, including the object and status they represent. To manually move orders in the product chart or the operations in the resource chart, you can click the operation/order, drag it to the desired position on the graphical rep- resentation of the resource capacity, and drop it in position. If the detailed scheduling strategy allows the operation/order to be placed in the desired position, it will be placed there and scheduled according to the strategy profile (scheduling mode, direc- tion, treatment of dependent operations, etc.). To move multiple operations, as shown on the left side in Figure 6.50, you can press the (Ctrl) key, select all the required operations, and drag them while the (Ctrl) key is still pressed. Then release the dragged objects in the required position on the detailed scheduling planning board. The current time stamp will be displayed on the bottom of the screen. In addition, you can drag a box around the objects 1 by clicking to select multiple objects, as shown in the left side of Figure 6.50. When there are alternative modes present for the activities (alternative modes from the same PDS), while selecting and dragging the operations manually, the system will highlight the resource rows belonging to alternative modes in green 2, as shown on the right side of Figure 6.50. This way, if there are capacity constraints in the primary mode, you can place the operation on one of the highlighted alternative modes. If there are alternative resources available from alternative PDSs, those aren’t highlighted. Figure 6.50 Moving Operations and Alternative Modes The pegging relationships between orders and inter-order relationships can be displayed by choosing Extras  Activity/Pegging Relationships  Show. For individual objects, this 6 Detailed Scheduling 406 can be done from the context menu of the object. In Figure 6.51, you can see the fixed pegging lines (dark red lines) 1, the dynamic pegging lines (green lines) 2, and the oper- ation relationships lines (blue lines) 3. By double-clicking on the pegging links, you can navigate to the pegging overview screen of the product view, where you can change the type of pegging relationships if necessary. Figure 6.51 Display of Pegging and Operations Relationships The Alert Monitor can be invoked by clicking on the Alert Monitor button in the menu bar or displaying the alerts by choosing More  Extras  Alerts  Display. This will high- light the objects in the detailed scheduling planning board by making the object blink. In the same menu path, the Hide option can be used to stop the display of alerts in the chart objects. However, such graphics-intensive functions are performance intensive, and they can be switched on and off only on a need basis and not set as default for reg- ular usage of the detailed scheduling planning board. Tip To scroll on the timelines within the charts, you can use the arrow keys. If, after you’ve selected objects and started scrolling, you want to cancel the action and place the objects back in the original position, release the dragged objects on the time axis on top of the chart. This will cancel the drag action. You can use the Find button on the menu bar to search for objects with order number, product, and so on. If you enter an order number and search, the system will highlight all the operations of the order present in the resource chart and the order in the prod- uct chart. Execution of Functions You can select one or multiple operations, orders, or resources to execute functions such as rescheduling (according to the set strategy) or deallocating the objects. To exe- cute a heuristic on the selected objects, select the objects (e.g., relevant resources), and choose Functions  Heuristics, as shown in Figure 6.52. The heuristic you want to exe- cute must be part of the heuristics profile you’ve assigned to the overall profile. © 407 6.4 Triggering PP/DS Scheduling Figure 6.52 Executing Heuristics from the Detailed Scheduling Planning Board Unlike the interactive execution of production planning heuristics, most of the detailed scheduling heuristics don’t have a dialog popup to change any heuristic set- tings already saved in the heuristics. Only with the schedule sequence manually heu- ristic (SAP003) is a new screen launched to list all the operations from the selected resources for this heuristic, as shown in Figure 6.53. Here, you can move the operations to the clipboard and sequence them manually (drag and drop between the Clipboard side and Sequence to be planned side). After you set the sequence for the operations, click on the Schedule button. The operations will be scheduled based on the strategy profile set in the heuristic. Figure 6.53 Schedule Sequence Manually Heuristic To check the logs of the actions performed in the detailed scheduling planning board, you can click on the Logs button in the menu bar. This will display all the planning and scheduling logs generated from manual actions as well as the heuristics executions. 6 Detailed Scheduling 408 Simulation Session All the schedule changes and the heuristics you executed in the detailed scheduling planning board are always performed in a simulation session (sim session) by the sys- tem, until you adopt the changes to the active version while saving. When you navigate back from the detailed scheduling planning board screen, the system prompts for you to Adopt the current scheduling data from the detailed scheduling planning board into the active planning version or to Save the data to a simulation version, which can be worked on later before merging back to the active version, as shown in Figure 6.54. Figure 6.54 Detailed Scheduling Planning Board: Option to Save the Data in a Simulation Version Note The simulation version saved from the detailed scheduling planning board scheduling data shouldn’t be confused with the inactive planning versions, which can be created by copying the active planning version 000. These are two different objects. The simu- lation version from the detailed scheduling planning board only has the data loaded onto the planning board. Inactive planning versions (copy of 000) are created and maintained from the version copy report and Transaction /SAPAPO/MVM (Model Ver- sion Management). When merging the simulation version data or the data from the detailed scheduling planning board session (sim session) back with the active version, the merge will take place depending on the status of the objects. For example, if you’ve rescheduled an operation of a production order in the detailed scheduling planning board, and the order has been confirmed in SAP S/4HANA in the meantime, then while merging the sim session (rescheduled operation) to the active version (operation confirmed), the status in the active version takes higher priority, and the rescheduling change from the detailed scheduling planning board will be ignored during the merge. While working in the detailed scheduling planning board, you can perform a refresh to load the current © 409 6.4 Triggering PP/DS Scheduling active version data onto the planning board; this overwrites any changes you’ve made so far in the detailed scheduling planning board. The simulation versions can be accessed from Transaction /SAPAPO/CDPSS0, as shown in Figure 6.55. The saved simulation sessions can be loaded onto the detailed schedul- ing planning board (graphical processing 1) or to the resource planning table (tabular processing 2). In addition, from this transaction, the simulation version can be adopted to the active version 3. Figure 6.55 Accessing Simulation Versions Multilevel Time Buffers A multilevel time buffer (MLTB) calculates the buffer for rescheduling orders without impacting the schedule of the upstream or downstream orders in the pegging struc- ture. This is useful in situations where a finished product is produced in a constrained resource with many products scheduled on it. If a change is required in the semifin- ished product’s order schedule, it would eventually impact the finished product’s man- ufacturing resources, which has far more impact due to the line manufacturer’s multiple other products. In this case, if there is a time gap between the finished product and semifinished product orders, the MLTB calculates this exact time gap and displays it as a key figure in the planning board. This will help the schedulers with a time thresh- old within which the semifinished order can be rescheduled without impacting the schedule of the finished product order scheduled on the constrained resource. There are three types of time buffers that can be calculated and displayed in the plan- ning board:  Time buffer relative to successor This is the time difference between the operation being rescheduled and the imme- diate next operation of the same order or the next order that is pegged to the opera- tion/order being rescheduled.  Time buffer relative to predecessor This is the time difference between the operation being rescheduled and the imme- diate previous operation of the same order or the next order that is pegged to the operation/order being rescheduled. 6 Detailed Scheduling 410  Time buffer relative to primary demand The primary demand is the top level of the pegging structure, which can be a forecast requirement, sales order requirement, and so on. If there are gaps between the oper- ations of the orders and gaps between the orders, the time buffer relative to primary demand for any level of the order/operation in the pegging structure is the total time that becomes available if all these gaps are closed. The primary demand date is a constant. The orders/operations will be simulated with an infinite backward sched- uling starting at the demand due date till the operation/order for which this key fig- ure is being calculated and that value is displayed. In the example shown in Figure 6.56, the top portion A is the original schedule of the orders on their resources. Here, we’ll take the order 1 for product S4PPDS_MLTB_ HALB1, which is pegged to the higher level and pegged by a lower-level material, as an example and see how the buffers are calculated. For calculating the time buffer relative to the successor, the system calculates the difference 2 between the end time stamp of this order and the start time stamp of the higher-level pegged order (for product S4PPDS_MLTB_FERT1). Figure 6.56 Example for Calculation of Time Buffers Relative to Predecessor and Successor Orders As shown in the middle part of the screen B, if the order is manually rescheduled within this calculated threshold, this doesn’t impact the schedule of the higher-level order. Similarly, the difference 3 between the start time stamp of the order 1 and the end time stamp of the lower-level order pegged (for product S4PPDS_MLTB_HALB2) provides the time buffer relative to predecessor. As you can see in the bottom part of Figure 6.56 C, moving the order in the backward direction within the buffer threshold won’t impact the schedule of the order for product S4PPDS_MLTB_HALB2. © 411 6.4 Triggering PP/DS Scheduling An example of the time buffer relative to the primary demand is shown in Figure 6.57. The original schedule is shown in the top portion A. Here the time buffer relative to pri- mary demand is being calculated for the order in the lowest level of the pegging struc- ture. The primary demand is a forecast element 2. For this order 1, the system calculates the difference 3 of the end time of the order (for which the buffer is being calculated) and the end time of the same order, if it’s rescheduled along with all orders in the higher pegging levels (with no gaps) and without impacting the due date for the primary demand 2, as shown in the bottom part B. Figure 6.57 Example of Calculation of Time Buffer Relative to Primary Demand The time buffer can be calculated as a gross duration or as net duration. For example, if an operation is disturbed by a nonworking day or shift break, the gross duration is the difference of the start and end time stamps of the operation. The net duration is the actual operation duration, which doesn’t include the nonworking times. The MLTB Pro- file determines whether the duration calculated in the gross or net duration. The MLTB profile can be configured using SAP IMG menu path, SPRO  Advanced Planning  Detailed Scheduling  Maintain MLTB Profiles. In the MLTB profile settings, under the Time Buffer Calculation Method field, you can set if the duration needs to be calculated in net time or gross time, as shown in Figure 6.58. In the detailed scheduling planning board, you can set the overall profile SAP_MLTB to display the MLTB-related key figures such as the buffer relative to successor/predeces- sor in the order and operation charts in the detailed scheduling planning board. After entering this overall profile and the selection criteria for the detailed scheduling plan- ning board, execute the transaction, and you’ll be in the detailed scheduling planning board. Within the detailed scheduling planning board, select the resources (see Figure 6.59 1) for which you want to calculate the time buffers for the corresponding orders and operations. Then navigate to Functions  Multi-Level Time Buffer  Calculate Time Buffer 2. This will calculate the time buffer key figures, and in the order chart 3 and operations chart 4, you can see the values for the buffers updated. When there are changes made to the schedule of the orders, you can use the Refresh Time Buffer 5 to recalculate the buffers based on the new scheduling situation. 6 Detailed Scheduling 412 Figure 6.58 MLTB Profile Settings Figure 6.59 Calculation and Display of Multilevel Time Buffer in Detailed Scheduling Planning Board © 413 6.4 Triggering PP/DS Scheduling

sections.title: Advanced Scheduling Board
sections.en: 6.4.2 Advanced Scheduling Board In embedded PP/DS, Advanced Scheduling Board is delivered as a standard SAP Fiori app. This app can be used to perform order-scheduling functions such as schedule, deallocate, fix, interrupt, creation/deletion of orders, setting conversion indicator for planned orders, and so on. The Alert Monitor is integrated to this app. In addition, exe- cution of detailed scheduling heuristics is also possible through the Advanced Schedul- ing Board app. Note The Advanced Scheduling Board is a new SAP Fiori app. The old Production Scheduling Board app is still available as of SAP S/4HANA 2022, but all the new features and func- tionalities are delivered in the new Advanced Scheduling Board app. Activation of advanced planning (PP/DS) is mandatory for using the Advanced Sched- uling Board app, and only the resources activated for advanced planning can be sched- uled via the app. This SAP Fiori app is delivered with the authorization business role SAP_BR_PRODN_PLNR. After your user is assigned a role, the Advanced Scheduling Board app appears under the Advanced Planning tab in the SAP Fiori launchpad, as shown in Figure 6.60. Figure 6.60 Advanced Scheduling Board App in the SAP Fiori Launchpad To activate the Advanced Scheduling Board app, the backend OData service needs to be registered and maintained in the SAP S/4HANA system. To register the service, use Transaction /IWBEP/CONF_SERVICE. As shown in Figure 6.61, in this transaction, enter the value “UI_SCM_ADVNCD_SCHEDG_BOARD” for the Service and enter “1” in the Service Version field. Execute the transaction, and in the next screen, select the Deacti- vate Parallelization of Batch Requests checkbox and save the transaction. This is a tech- nical setting required for certain types of SAP Fiori apps. 6 Detailed Scheduling 414 Figure 6.61 Registration of OData Service for the Advanced Scheduling Board App Like the MRP apps, the Advanced Scheduling Board app also works based on the area of responsibility (AOR). For the Advanced Scheduling Board app, the AOR is the combina- tion of the plant and the planner assigned to the resource master data. When you launch the app for the first time, you’ll see a popup to set up the AOR. Subsequent to changing the AOR, click on the user profile button within the Advanced Scheduling Board app, and select the App Settings option, as shown in Figure 6.62. In the App Set- tings popup screen, click on the Area of Responsibility. In the resulting screen, click on the Add Plant and Planner 1 button to assign new planners and plant combinations to the AOR. Use the Delete 2 button to remove existing assignments. Once you launch the app, you’ll see the default filter options such as the display hori- zon and the resource name. To add additional filters, click on Adapt Filters, and you’ll see a list of all available filter options, as shown in Figure 6.63. Select the required filter options, and you can save the added filters and values you’ve entered for the filter val- ues as a variant. © 415 6.4 Triggering PP/DS Scheduling Figure 6.62 Setting Up Area of Responsibility in the Advanced Scheduling Board App Figure 6.63 Filter Options in the Advanced Scheduling Board App In the charts selection dropdown 1, you can select the charts to be loaded on the Advanced Scheduling Board app. A maximum of four different charts can be selected and loaded at one time, as shown in Figure 6.64. 6 Detailed Scheduling 416 Figure 6.64 Chart Selection Options in Advanced Scheduling Board Display Horizon is a mandatory filter field where you can choose from options such as current year, quarter, month, or a date range. After the filter options are entered and the charts to be displayed are selected, click on the Go button to load the charts with the corresponding graphical objects. In the top of the screen shown in Figure 6.65 is the selection filter bar 1 and the toolbar 2 with various options to execute detailed sched- uling steps in the Advanced Scheduling Board app. All the displayed charts have a table area 3 where you can set additional details for the corresponding object such as resources, products, or orders, depending on the chart. Figure 6.65 Advanced Scheduling Board App Details © 417 6.4 Triggering PP/DS Scheduling Click on the Settings button 4 within the chart table area to select the columns to be displayed in the table. In the graphical chart area 5, the graphical elements such as operations and orders are displayed, depending on the charts loaded. In the toolbar shown in Figure 6.66, click on the Settings button 1, and in the Profile Settings tab in the Settings popup, you can enter the Alert Profile. Once the alert profile is entered, click on the Alerts button 2 to display the list of alerts generated per the alert profile settings. In the Alerts popup, use the dropdown 3 to select the alert type to display the alert list. In the list of alerts, click on the Go To 4 button to highlight the cor- responding object 5 in the graphical chart area. Figure 6.66 Alert Monitor in the Advanced Scheduling Board App In the resource chart to display overlapped operations on the resources, as shown in Figure 6.67, click on the Expand Overlap button 1 to display operations that are loaded in parallel on the resources. You can select multiple objects by holding down the (Ctrl) button or by dragging a box around the objects to be selected. With the objects selected, click on the Show Relationships/Pegging Relationships button in the toolbar 2 to display the operation relationships and the order pegging relationships 3 in the corresponding charts. The Scheduling button in the toolbar helps to execute simple scheduling functions 4 such as Fix, Undo Fix, Deallocate, and Reschedule operations. Click on the Go to Date button 5 to select a specific date from a calendar popup to nav- igate to a specific date in the graphical chart area. The Zoom In, Zoom Out, and the Zoom Slider 6 buttons can be used to control the gran- ularity of the time periods such as days, weeks, months, and so on, displayed in the graphical chart area. Click on the Find button 7, which will open a popup 8 to search and highlight objects within the graphical chart areas. 6 Detailed Scheduling 418 Figure 6.67 Features within the Advanced Scheduling Board App As shown in Figure 6.68, there are context menu options available both on the objects in the table area and on the graphical objects. For options in context menus such as order processing or resource master data, the corresponding GUI transaction is ren- dered in an HTML screen. The context menu options in the resources 1 and the opera- tions 2 are also shown. To display the details of the selected graphical object, click on the Information button 3, which will open the details of the selected object in the side panel 4. Figure 6.68 Context Menu Options and Detailed Information of Objects in the Advanced Scheduling Board App © 419 6.4 Triggering PP/DS Scheduling Click on the Strategy button in the toolbar to launch the Detailed Scheduling Strategy Settings popup, as shown in Figure 6.69. Here, you can select the detailed scheduling strategy profiles 1 you’ve defined in the PP/DS configuration. In addition, you can change the Scheduling Mode 2 and Planning Direction 3 within the strategy settings. Only the listed scheduling modes 4 are supported in the Advanced Scheduling Board app. The strategy profile settings that can’t be edited are shown in display-only mode. To display all the settings of the strategy profile, click on the Next button 5, and in the Review step 6, you can check all the settings in the strategy profile. Figure 6.69 Detailed Scheduling Strategy Profile Settings in the Advanced Scheduling Board App 6 Detailed Scheduling 420 You can also execute detailed scheduling heuristics using the Heuristics button in the toolbar. This will launch a new HTML screen, as shown in Figure 6.70. Within this new screen, you can select the heuristics 1 you want to execute from the list of available heuristics. All detailed scheduling heuristics are listed there. The current selection of Resource in the Advanced Scheduling Board app is selected for the heuristic execution. Click on the Execute button 2 to run the heuristics. Upon completion of the heuristic execution, the application logs 3 are also displayed. Click on the Back button 4 to nav- igate back to the Advanced Scheduling Board main screen. Figure 6.70 Execution of Detailed Scheduling Heuristics from Advanced Scheduling Board After making the required scheduling changes and heuristics execution within the Advanced Scheduling Board app, as shown in Figure 6.71, select the Adopt button at the bottom of the screen to save the data back to the active version. To refresh the screen without saving the data and refresh the data, click on the Reset button. For saving the scheduling changes in a simulation version, click on the Save As button, and enter a name for the simulation version in the popup. You can add the Simulation Version 1 as a filter criterion to load back the simulation version in the Advanced Scheduling Board © 421 6.4 Triggering PP/DS Scheduling app. The simulation version saved from the Advanced Scheduling Board app can be accessed and changed using the GUI Transaction /SAPAPO/CDPSS0. Figure 6.71 Saving and Accessing Simulation Versions within Advanced Scheduling Board App

sections.title: Monitor Capacity Utilization App
sections.en: 6.4.3 Monitor Capacity Utilization App Monitor Capacity Utilization is an SAP Fiori app to monitor the resource usage in an interactive graphical format to identify any resource overloads and take action to mit- igate the scheduling issues by changing the operations or by updating the capacity of the resources. This SAP Fiori app works based on the AOR assigned to the app just like the Advanced Scheduling Board app. If you have the AOR already assigned in the Advanced Schedul- ing Board app, the same will be considered for the Monitor Capacity Utilization app as well. All the resources activated for advanced planning and within the AOR (plant and resource responsible) are displayed in a list with a graphical representation of the capacity utilization over the time horizon set in the filter criteria, as shown in Figure 6.72 (if you click a resource, you can see the utilization percentage per period 1). You can add more filter criteria to narrow down the list of resources displayed as well 2. Columns with details on the minimum and maximum loads on the resource for the period of analysis are listed, and the average utilization of the resource is also provided. The dates of first underload and first overload are also displayed as default columns. There are more than 30 columns available for you to manage and display in the set- tings of the app, which you can access via the Settings button 3. You can also configure the chart display to a period other than the evaluation period by clicking on the chart settings on the app 4. You can select the resources and launch 6 Detailed Scheduling 422 other detailed scheduling tools such as the Resource Planning Table and the Production Scheduling Board tools 5. Figure 6.72 Monitor Capacity Utilization App: UI Features The Evaluation Profile is created in the Customizing of embedded PP/DS via menu path SAP IMG Menu  Advanced Planning  Apps for Material Requirements Planning  Gen- eral Settings  Define Evaluation Profile for Capacity Utilization. The objects relevant for calculating the capacity utilization are defined here. Options are available to include or exclude manufacturing orders (production and process orders), scheduled operations on the resource, and deallocated operations on the resource, as shown in Figure 6.73. Figure 6.73 Customization of the Evaluation Profile for the Monitor Capacity Utilization App © 423 6.4 Triggering PP/DS Scheduling The definition for the percentage utilization to determine if the capacity is underuti- lized or overutilized is also made in this Customizing setting. The evaluation profile is then assigned to the user names under Customizing menu path, SAP IMG Menu  Advanced Planning  Apps for Material Requirements Planning  General Settings  Assign Evaluation Profile to User. To navigate to the detailed screen for the individual resources, click on the Resource row in the list (refer to Figure 6.72). This will open a new screen (see Figure 6.74) with a bar chart for the resource utilization and the shift details, along with the operations scheduled on the resource for the evaluation period. The capacity situation is displayed in a bar chart with colored legends displaying overutilization, underutilization, and normal utilization of the resource. The chart can be changed to analyze the capacity consumption by Material, Activity, and Order Type, as shown in Figure 6.74. Figure 6.74 Resource Utilization Details and UI Options In the detailed screen, you can change the resource availability data in Edit mode, as shown in Figure 6.74. On the SHIFT TABLE, you see the list of shifts per the shift sequence definition in the resource master data maintained through SAP S/4HANA Transactions CR02 or CRC2. Shift definitions can only be managed from one source (PP/DS resource master or Monitor Capacity Utilization app) to ensure data consistency. For this reason, only the resources marked with external capacities (can be marked from the SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization resource view of the SAP S/4HANA work center master data) in the resource master data are allowed for editing the shift data in the SAP Fiori app. Apart from switching on the external capacity, as shown in Figure 6.75, assign the Active Version with value 1 1, assign a valid Grouping 2 for the assignment of shift sequences, and assign a Factory Calendar 3 in the work center master data in SAP S/4HANA for editing the shifts in this app. 6 Detailed Scheduling 424 Figure 6.75 Prerequisites for Editing Shifts from the Monitor Capacity Utilization App When the prerequisites are met, you can see the list of shifts per the shift sequence defi- nition in the SHIFT TABLE, as shown in Figure 6.76. You can switch the shift from the currently assigned shift to another shift from the list of shifts defined using the drop- down option in the Shift Definition column 1. You can delete a shift by selecting the corresponding shift 2 and clicking on the Delete button 3. You can change the resource utilization of a specific shift to accommodate overload situations by changing the utilization value 4. In addition, you can add a new shift, which is present in the shift definition, add a new interval (assigning a specific shift sequence to a new period), or add resource downtimes using the corresponding options in the Add button 5. To navigate to a specific date on the list of shifts, click on the Shift Calendar button 6, and select the date. © 425 6.4 Triggering PP/DS Scheduling Figure 6.76 Shift Edit Options in the Shift Table The operations scheduled on the resource are also listed under LIST OF OPERATIONS, and you can change the operation dates in the list. When dates are changed, the new scheduling of the order is performed according to the scheduling mode 1 selected. The field end date will be editable with backward scheduling, and the start date becomes editable if the scheduling direction 2 is set as forward scheduling. You can fix or deal- locate the operation using the Planning Status dropdown options 3, as shown in Figure 6.77. To save the changes made to the shifts and operations, click on the Save button 4. Figure 6.77 Working with Operations List in the Capacity Utilization App 6 Detailed Scheduling 426

sections.title: Resource Planning Table
sections.en: 6.4.4 Resource Planning Table So far, we’ve covered the graphical scheduling tools such as the detailed scheduling planning board and the Advanced Scheduling Board app. In PP/DS, a tabular-based scheduling tool is also available, which is called the resource planning table. This detailed scheduling tool can be launched by using Transaction /SAPAPO/RPT or the SAP Easy Access Menu path, Logistics  Advanced Planning  Production Planning  Inter- active Production  Planning Detailed Scheduling  Resource Planning Table. In the selection screen, you can enter the selection options such as Time Profile, Resource, Product or Order selection options under the corresponding tabs 1. The overall profile can be changed by clicking on the User Settings button 2, as shown in Figure 6.78. Figure 6.78 Selection Screen for the Resource Planning Table After entering the required selection options, click on the Execute button on the screen to load the resource planning table. In the next screen shown in Figure 6.79, on the right side, you’ll see the navigation area 1, which has the tools that can be leveraged for scheduling using the resource planning table. On the right side of the screen, the top © 427 6.4 Triggering PP/DS Scheduling portion has the resource utilization table 2, which shows resource-related data such as the available capacity, capacity consumption, alerts, downtimes, and so on. You can navigate to different resources by double-clicking on the resource name in the resource list 3 in the navigation area. When you double-click on the resource utiliza- tion percentage 4 cell in the resource utilization table, this will open the list of opera- tions in the bottom part of the screen in the operations table 5. Figure 6.79 Details of the Resource Planning Table To change the scheduling of the operations on the resources, as shown in Figure 6.80, select the operations A from the operations table, right-click and select Pick Operations 1 (or select the Pick button 2 from the toolbar), and then navigate to the date in which you want to reschedule the selected operations. You can navigate to the preferred date B in the resource utilization table, and on the required date, right-click and select Drop Operations 3 to reschedule the operation from the picked date to the new dropped date. In addition, you can use the Drop Operations 4 button in the toolbar. The opera- tions will be scheduled based on the detailed scheduling strategy settings maintained. To pick all the operations from a specific date, use the Pick option by selecting the date in the resource utilization table, and use the Drop option on a different date to resched- ule all operations from one date to another. 6 Detailed Scheduling 428 Figure 6.80 Rescheduling Operations in the Resource Planning Table Using Pick and Drop In the navigation area, the following tools are available:  Resource Pool The Resource Pool area has the list of resources selected per the selection conditions defined in the initial selection screen.
