In this example 1, if the remaining shelf life is less than 15 days (360 hours), an info alert is raised; if the remaining shelf life is less than 10 days (240 hours), a warning alert is raised; and if the remaining shelf life is less 8 Advanced PP/DS Features 484 than 5 days (120 hours), an error alert is raised. There are supply elements such as the planned orders and the batch stock 2, which aren’t pegged to any requirement ele- ment, as they can’t fulfill minimum shelf-life conditions for the requirement element. Therefore, depending on the leftover shelf life of these elements, the alerts are raised 3. Figure 8.13 Alerts for Expiring and Unconsumed Receipt Elements

sections.title: Product Interchangeability
sections.en: 8.2 Product Interchangeability During the life of a product in product lifecycle management, there will be changes required to the components of the materials due to a supplier stopping a specific com- ponent; for safety, quality, or product improvement issues; or for a regulatory man- date. These changes require components or products to be discontinued and substituted with a successor product or component. In SAP S/4HANA, the discontinuation of a material and assigning a follow-up material can be done from the MRP 4 view of the material master. However, this method has restrictions, such as the inability to create multilevel discontinuations (material B replaces material A, and then material C replaces material B) and that control for the use of existing stock for discontinued material may also require updating the discontinua- tion information in the bill of material (BOM) master data for material requirements planning (MRP) to consider the discontinuation. But SAP S/4HANA discontinuation supports certain functionalities such as parallel discontinuation, where a group of com- ponents can be replaced by another group of components with the discontinuation group assigned in the BOM master data. This isn’t supported in PP/DS product inter- changeability. © 485 8.2 Product Interchangeability The interchangeability in PP/DS should only be considered for planning purposes during the transition period from the discontinued component to the replacement component. The existence of an interchangeability group won’t eliminate the require- ment to update the BOM master data, which is used by other areas, such as product costing, in SAP S/4HANA. Embedded PP/DS supports the discontinuation and substitution via the product inter- changeability functionality; detailed scheduling supports the discontinuation via the linear supersession chain where only one product in the chain is valid at any given point in time. Procurement planning (both in-house and external procurement) and order processing are supported in PP/DS interchangeability. You can also use the use- up strategy in PP/DS product interchangeability to control whether the existing stock can be used to cover requirements until the stock completely depletes for the discon- tinued material or whether the discontinuation is in effect without consideration of the existing stock. Following are some of the restrictions applicable to PP/DS product interchangeability:  Embedded PP/DS only supports simple interchangeability (1:1). Configurable prod- ucts can’t participate in interchangeability.  For integrating manufacturing orders with product substitutions, the interchangeabil- ity should not have multiple substitutions within one chain (e.g., product A – B – C).  If shelf-life planning is in use, all the products in the interchangeability chain should have the same shelf-life conditions. Now, let’s go through the relevant master data to see how interchangeability works in the planning process.

sections.title: Master Data
sections.en: 8.2.1 Master Data PP/DS product interchangeability works based on the following master data objects, which we’ll discuss in this section:  Interchangeability group (supersession chain)  Assignment of the interchangeability group to the supply chain model  Automatic generation and assignment of planning packages Interchangeability Group You create the interchangeability group of type supersession chain using Transaction /INCMD/UI or using SAP Easy Access menu path, Logistics  Advanced Planning  Master Data  Product and Location Interchangeability  Interchangeability Group. As shown in Figure 8.14, in the interchangeability transaction, the screen has four main sections: 8 Advanced PP/DS Features 486  Quick Search This can be used for searching the existing interchangeability groups in the system; the search results are displayed at the bottom of the screen.  Header The interchangeability group header has the Group Type (only supersession chain is supported in PP/DS), Group name, Group Description, and Relevant for fields. In the SAP S/4HANA system, advanced available-to-promise (aATP) and PP/DS aren’t directly integrated, so select Planning in the Relevant for field. The Status is set to In Process when the group is created and saved without releasing the same. You can use the Release button on the menu bar to set the Status to Released. Figure 8.14 Interchangeability Group in PP/DS  Location In the Location tab, assign the locations for which the interchangeability group is rel- evant. The materials being maintained in the interchangeability group should be available in the locations defined in the Location tab of the header data.  Details The Details tab of the interchangeability transaction screen contains the details of the materials that are assigned as the preceding and succeeding materials in the interchangeability group and the attributes of the interchangeability relationship. After the header data is entered, navigate to the Location-Independent Attributes sec- tion under Details, and click on the Append Row button (new document symbol icon) on the toolbar to add a new row. You can enter the details of the preceding and succeed- ing materials and the attributes in the row by clicking the number in the Item No. col- umn and arriving at the Basic Data tab, as shown in Figure 8.15. You also can click the © 487 8.2 Product Interchangeability row in the Attributes tab, and the row will be expanded into a new screen, as shown in Figure 8.16. Figure 8.15 Maintenance of Interchangeability Group Details: Basic Data Figure 8.16 Maintenance of the Interchangeability Group: Attributes As shown in Figure 8.16, the group details can be maintained at a Cross-Location level or Location-Specific level in the Location dropdown. The cross-location details maintained are applicable for all locations assigned to the interchangeability header, and the prod- ucts participate in interchangeability maintained in the details. If there is a require- ment to maintain different values for specific plants, then select the location from the Location dropdown menu, and maintain the details. For example, material A is replaced by material B in plant 1, 2, and 3 from 01.Jan.2023. However, in plant 2, if the interchangeability is valid only from 01.Feb.2023, the same can be maintained as a location-specific Valid-from Date in the attributes. PP/DS only supports linear supersession chains, which means that the chain can have only one preceding and succeeding material. Multiple interchangeability (nonlinear 8 Advanced PP/DS Features 488 supersession chain) isn’t supported in PP/DS, where a product has several successor products (1:N), or several products have one successor product (N:1). The materials par- ticipating in the supersession chain should follow these prerequisites:  The materials in the supersession chain have to be different. Material A-B-A isn’t supported.  The supersession chain may not contain any assemblies.  A material can only be contained in one supersession chain. When a material that is part of another interchangeability group is assigned to a supersession chain, the sys- tem will raise an error message.  The base unit of measure must be the same for all materials in a supersession chain.  A supersession chain may not contain any configurable products.  The shelf-life data must be the same for all products in a supersession chain. In the Basic Data tab (refer to Figure 8.15), enter the material to be discontinued in the Material Number field under Preceding Member Details, and enter the material that will replace the discontinued material in the Material Number field under Succeeding Member Details. In the Attributes tab (refer to Figure 8.16), enter the date in the Valid-from Date from which the system should consider the interchangeability to switch the requirements of the discontinued material to the follow-up material. The interchangeability Direction field has two options:  Full The preceding and succeeding materials can interchange each other.  Forward The succeeding material will replace the preceding material from the valid-from date. The value defined in the Use-up Strategy field is used to determine how the existing stock for the preceding material is treated. The options are as follows:  Yes Use the existing stock first; only when the stock is depleted, switch over the demand for the preceding material to the succeeding material.  No Irrespective of the existing stock for the preceding material, switch over the demand from the preceding material to the succeeding material on the valid-from date.  Restricted With a restricted use-up strategy, a Use-up Date can be defined, and the existing stock of the preceding material is used up only until the use-up date. The Succeeding Quantity Factor and Preceding Quantity Factor are used in scenarios where the replacement quantity factors between the preceding and succeeding material © 489 8.2 Product Interchangeability aren’t equal. For example, material A replaces material B, but two quantities of material B are required to replace one quantity of material A. In this case, the Preceding Quantity Factor is defined as 1, and the Succeeding Quantity Factor is defined as 2. Set the status of the interchangeability group to Released by clicking on the Release button in the menu bar of the screen, and click the Save button to save the interchange- ability group data. Assign the Interchangeability Group to a Model For a released interchangeability group to be considered for planning, it must be assigned to the supply chain model. In embedded PP/DS, 000 is the active model. You can assign the group to the 000 model by executing Transaction /SAPAPO/INCMD_ MODEL or navigating to the transaction via SAP Easy Access menu path, Logistics  Advanced Planning  Master Data  Product and Location Interchangeability  Assign Interchangeability Group to a Model. Enter the Interchangeability Group in the initial screen, and click on the Execute but- ton, as shown in the upper-left screen of Figure 8.17. On the Assignment of interchange- ability group model popup screen, all the available models defined in the system are listed. Select Model Name 000, and click on the Assign Objects to Model button (to the right of the green checkmark) to assign the interchangeability group to the model 000. Figure 8.17 Assigning the Interchangeability Group to Model 000 Planning Packages When materials are assigned to supersession chains, these materials must be planned together. When executing MRP in PP/DS or executing product heuristics, it’s essential that all the materials in the chain are planned together to avoid any excess supply being created for the materials. When the interchangeability groups are assigned with 8 Advanced PP/DS Features 490 a location in the interchangeability master data, the system automatically creates a planning package and assigns it to all the materials in the material master Advanced Planning view. Note Planning packages can also be used in regular planning scenarios if there is a require- ment to plan certain materials together irrespective of their position in the BOMs (low- level codes). For interchangeability, a special planning package type 001 is delivered in the standard system. For the automatic generation of the planning packages, several Customizing entries are delivered in standard embedded PP/DS. The planning package type can be verified from Customizing menu path, SAP IMG Menu  Advanced Planning  MRP Planning Run  Maintain Planning Package Types. As shown in Figure 8.18, the Heuristic SAP_PP_I001 is assigned to Package Type 001. This heuristic calls the product heuristics assigned to the material in the material master for all the materials in the supersession chain in the correct order, and the product heuris- tics will decide which requirements are to be passed on to the successor product from the discontinued product. The heuristics will also consider settings such as the Use-up Strategy maintained in the interchangeability group master data. Figure 8.18 Planning Package Type: Customizing Setting the Automat. Maintenance checkbox in Customizing for the 001 package type enables the system to generate and update the material master with the planning pack- age automatically. In addition, the number range for the automatically generated planning packages must be maintained via Customizing menu path, SAP IMG Menu  Advanced Planning  MRP Planning Run  Maintain Number Ranges for Automatically Generated Planning Packages. The planning packages that are automatically created by the system via the superses- sion chains can’t be edited manually. When the materials are removed from the super- session chain, the materials are also removed from the planning package. The planning packages can be displayed from Transaction /SAPAPO/HEUR2 or from SAP Easy Access menu path, Logistics  Advanced Planning  Master Data  Product and Location © 491 8.2 Product Interchangeability Interchangeability  Define Planning Package. As shown on the upper screen in Figure 8.19, the materials that are part of the supersession chain are listed in the product selec- tion (ProdSelection) for the planning package. Note the Plan. package field at the top of the screen with the interchangeability group number as its description. In addition, in the material master, the planning package values are updated, as shown in Figure 8.19 on the lower screen. Figure 8.19 Automatic Creation and Assignment of Planning Packages for Interchangeability Group

sections.title: Interchangeability in the Planning Process
sections.en: 8.2.2 Interchangeability in the Planning Process Materials involved in interchangeability can be planned via MRP runs in the produc- tion planning run, interactive planning by executing the product heuristics in the plan- ning tools, or automatic planning triggered by the planning procedure definition. In all these cases, the system considers the planning package and always executes the super- session chain heuristic (SAP_PP_I001), which in turn will call the product heuristics assigned to the material master. 8 Advanced PP/DS Features 492 In the planning package created by the interchangeability group, the sequence of materi- als is also maintained according to the interchangeable direction (predecessor material first and successor material next). When MRP is executed for one material in the plan- ning package, it automatically reads the package and executes planning for all the mate- rials in the package according to the sequence of materials within the planning package. In the PP/DS planning run, for the interchangeable products to the planned correctly, one prerequisite is that the MRP heuristics should have the setting to execute the prod- uct heuristics in the heuristics customization. In addition, while defining the planning steps in the production planning run, you must ensure that none of the interchange- able materials are part of a planning step that executed a procurement planning heu- ristic (e.g., planning of standard lots [SAP_PP_002]) other than MRP heuristics. By executing a procurement heuristic other than the MRP heuristics, the planning pack- age sequence of materials can’t be ensured, and the planning results may be incorrect. During the planning, the requirement of the predecessor product may need to be cov- ered by the successor product based on the validity of the supersession chain and the use-up strategy maintained in the interchangeability group. In this case, the system will generate an order of type substitution order (Subst.ord) to transfer the demand from the predecessor (RAW1) to the successor material to cover the DepDmd, as shown in the Elements tab in Figure 8.20 1. The substitution order will have the predecessor material as an input (RAW2 under Requirements) and the successor material as an out- put component (RAW1 under Receipts) in the order 2. The substitution orders can’t be manually changed, and these are considered unfirmed orders for the purpose of plan- ning, so that the planning run can adjust them per the demand and supply situation. A pegging relationship is established between the original requirement element (in Figure 8.20, the DepDmd) and the substitution order. So, during detailed scheduling activities, if the strategy profile is set to respect dynamic pegging, then the substitution orders can also be rescheduled along with the requirement element. Note MRP Live (Transaction MD01N) can’t plan products with interchangeability, so a PP/DS planning run with MRP heuristics must be executed for such materials. Because the substitution orders aren’t transferred to SAP S/4HANA, the demand and supply situation in transactions such as the stock requirements list (Transaction MD04) may state excess supply for the predecessor product and supply deficiency for the successor product. Therefore, it’s essential that only PP/DS planning tools are used to monitor and plan these materials. For in-house production orders with interchangeable components, it’s mandatory that the planned orders are set with the conversion checkbox in embedded PP/DS so that the interchangeability is taken into account in the manufacturing order (production order or process order). © 493 8.2 Product Interchangeability Figure 8.20 Planning with Interchangeability As shown in Figure 8.21, if there is an interchangeable component, the original compo- nent (predecessor) 1 (RAW1 and RAW3) are listed in the production order (Transaction CO03) Component Overview screen with 0 quantity. The interchanged component (successor component) 2 (RAW2 and RAW4) will be listed in the Component Overview screen with the original component requirement quantity of the corresponding prede- cessor materials, respectively. Figure 8.21 Production Order Created with Interchanged Components 8 Advanced PP/DS Features 494

sections.title: Characteristics-Dependent Planning
sections.en: 8.3 Characteristics-Dependent Planning As discussed in Chapter 2, Section 2.6, and Chapter 3, Section 3.2.4, embedded PP/DS supports variant configuration (VC) or characteristics-dependent planning (CDP). CDP can also be used in make-to-stock (MTS) scenarios. All the supply and demand ele- ments, such as forecast elements, planned orders, production orders, and stocks/ batches, have their own classification (assignment of characteristics values), and PP/DS supports planning that considers these characteristics value assignments. When deter- mining the net requirement calculation, the system checks the compatibility of the characteristics values and creates receipts if there are no matching receipt elements available to fulfill demand elements with specific characteristics values. In addition, the characteristics value compatibility is considered while creating pegging relation- ships. Along with the material master classification, the classification master data—such as the object dependencies that are created in SAP S/4HANA to control the material and operation selections in BOMs and routings—can also be sent to the corresponding pro- duction data structure (PDS) master data in PP/DS. Note Conversion from VC to CDP or vice versa can be performed in embedded PP/DS using ABAP program /SAPAPO/CONFR_CFGREL_MAINTAIN. Caution should be exercised, however, when doing the conversion after master data and/or transaction data has already been created in the system because the conversion may lead to inconsistencies and/or data loss. The report performs a where-used list for finding the materials that will be impacted; if no inconsistencies are detected, it will complete the conversion. Adjustment of the materials to reassign the correct classification (classes of the correct type) must be done manually as a post step. In addition, the transaction data must be retransferred to PP/DS from SAP S/4HANA. In the next sections, we’ll cover how PP/DS planning and pegging processes consider the characteristics and also the steps to set up block planning.

sections.title: Planning and Pegging
sections.en: 8.3.1 Planning and Pegging When embedded PP/DS is set with the CDP configuration schema, the system consid- ers the characteristics value for the calculation of the net requirement for a product location to determine the deficit in supply quantity. In the SAP S/4HANA material master, as shown in Figure 8.22 1, the material is assigned with Class Type 300 (variant class). Upon integration (see Chapter 2, Section 2.6), this will create Class type 400 (CDP classification) in PP/DS 2. The material is also set as a configurable material in the SAP S/4HANA material master (Transaction © 495 8.3 Characteristics-Dependent Planning MM02) by setting the Material is Configurable checkbox under the Client Specific Con- figuration section in the Basic Data 2 tab. The configuration relevance and classifica- tion of the material in PP/DS can be displayed from the PP/DS product master (Transaction /SAPAPO/MAT1) 3. Figure 8.22 CDP Classification in SAP S/4HANA and in PP/DS Master Data Heuristics such as the planning of standard lots can consider the characteristics value during planning. Any demand or supply element created for the CDP materials in PP/DS contains the classification (characteristics values), which is represented by a small tri- angle symbol in PP/DS transactions such as the product view, as shown in Figure 8.23. Clicking on the icon shows the characteristics values assigned to the demand element or the supply element. Figure 8.23 Pegging in a CDP Scenario Considering Characteristics Values 8 Advanced PP/DS Features 496 The pegging links dynamically generated by the system also consider the characteris- tics value, and no pegging link will be established between demand and supply ele- ments that don’t have the same characteristics values. As shown in Figure 8.24, in the Pegging Overview tab, although there are more supply elements present for this exam- ple material, no pegging is created because there is no supply element with the match- ing characteristics value of the demand elements. In our example, the demand elements have the characteristics value of 100 G, and all the supply elements have the characteristics value of 200 G. Figure 8.24 Pegging in CDP: No Pegging Created without Compatible Elements With the previous demand and supply situation, if a planning heuristic such as the planning of standard lots is executed, it will create additional supply elements to fulfill the forecast demands. Like the shelf-life planning heuristic, this may result in excess supply being created for the material in question. But if the configuration (characteris- tics value – 100 G packaging) is different for the customer order or forecast, and it can’t be fulfilled with the receipt elements (planned orders – 200 G packaging), the system will create additional supply elements to satisfy the sales order demand, as shown in Figure 8.25. Figure 8.25 Planning Heuristics Considering Characteristics for Creating New Receipt Elements In our example, the demand elements (forecasts) have the characteristics value of 100 G, so the planning heuristic has created two receipt elements (the planned orders © 497 8.3 Characteristics-Dependent Planning 47026 and 47027) with the same characteristics value (100), although there are other receipt elements present (the planned orders 47024 and 47025) that don’t have a matching characteristics value to fulfill the sales order demand elements. Now, if you go to the Pegging Overview tab, you can see that the forecasts and planned orders that have the same characteristics values are pegged to each other, as shown in Figure 8.26. Figure 8.26 CDP: Pegging Considering Characteristics Values

sections.title: Block Planning
sections.en: 8.3.2 Block Planning One of the commonly used features of PP/DS in CDP is block planning. Block planning is the preassignment of capacities to produce materials belonging to certain character- istics. This is widely used in mill production (paper, metal, etc.). In process-oriented manufacturing, when the manufacturing process for a product has started, it can’t be interrupted or stopped due to the nature of manufacturing pro- cesses. In such cases, a preassigned capacity for the manufacturing resource is created via a campaign. This process is called campaign planning. A campaign is created for the resource in PP/DS, and a group of orders is assigned to the campaign. In addition, the setup and cleanup orders can be created at the start or end of the production campaign. The orders in the campaigns can be determined via the setup groups assigned to the operations of the orders, which in turn results in similar products and their orders being assigned to the campaign. In discrete manufacturing, however, materials must be grouped based on the opera- tion and resource in which the material is being produced. For example, a product may go through multiple operations, and if there is a bottleneck resource that requires con- siderable setup for switching the products, the schedule of that work center must be frozen to preassign its capacity to perform operations with certain characteristics. In PP/DS, this can be achieved via block planning. In block planning, blocks are created in the resources with specific characteristics, and operations with the same characteris- tics values will be scheduled in those blocks. 8 Advanced PP/DS Features 498 For campaign planning in process industries, the campaigns can also be integrated to SAP S/4HANA. However, in block planning, the blocks are only relevant in PP/DS, and only the schedule of the operation and the order are integrated back to SAP S/4HANA. Master Data The materials for which block planning is to be executed are assigned with class type 300 (variant class), which will generate class type 400 (CDP classification) in embedded PP/DS. The blocks are created in the resource master data in PP/DS. You create the work center master data in SAP S/4HANA and activate the Advanced Planning checkbox in the Basic Data view of the work center master data (see Chapter 2, Section 2.4). This will integrate the work center into the resource master data on the PP/DS side. When resources are created in PP/DS, they are assigned to the 000 model and the 000 ver- sion, which are the active model and version in PP/DS. In addition, model-independent resource master data is generated. Maintain Blocks To create blocks for resources, the first step is to create the basic definition and reference cycle, which we’ll discuss in this section. You can maintain blocks of the resource master data in PP/DS using the resource master Transaction /SAPAPO/RES01. The block basis definition is maintained at the model-independent resource. On the initial screen of the resource master data, select the Model-Independent Selection checkbox, as shown on the upper screen of Figure 8.27, and press (Enter). In the next screen, you’ll see the resource master data that is assigned to the 000 version as well as the model-independent (no ver- sion assigned) resource data, as shown on the lower screen in Figure 8.27. Figure 8.27 Model-Independent Resource Master Data © 499 8.3 Characteristics-Dependent Planning Now, in the model-independent resource master data, navigate to the Block Plng (block planning) tab, and assign the CDP Class (class type 400), in which the character- istics required to create the blocks are assigned (see upper area of Figure 8.28). Click on the Create Blocks button to launch the Maintain Blocks screen (see lower area of Figure 8.28). Figure 8.28 Block Planning: Maintain Block Basis Definition In this screen, navigate to the Block Basis Definit. tab. List the block definitions by entering a number (No.) for the block and a Description; for example, in Figure 8.28, there are three block definitions maintained as 100 G, 200 G, and 500 G. You also can set a color representation for these blocks in the Displayed I (displayed in color) col- umn, which will be displayed in the detailed scheduling planning board to visually dif- ferentiate one block from another. You can assign the characteristics value associated with the block definition by select- ing a block that is maintained and navigating to the Requirements tab, as shown in Fig- ure 8.29. Assign a characteristics value for the defined block and assign the characteristics values to all the blocks that are defined in the block basis definition, as shown in Figure 8.29. You can only assign values for the characteristics that are already defined in the classification master data, as shown in Figure 8.30. 8 Advanced PP/DS Features 500 Figure 8.29 Assigning Characteristics Values to Defined Blocks Figure 8.30 Example: Characteristics Values Defined in the Master Data After the block basic definition is defined, the next step is to create reference cycles to define in what sequence the blocks are to be created on the resource capacity and the length (duration) of the individual blocks. Navigate to the Ref.Cycle tab (see Figure 8.31), and enter a Sequence number for the blocks to be created on the resource capacity. Enter the duration of the block in Days (Length), Time (Length), or Equivalent [Seconds]. If the blocks can be consumed by operations over its regular operating capacity, you can also define by what percentage overloads are allowed by maintaining the overload © 501 8.3 Characteristics-Dependent Planning percentage in the Rel. O column. Then, in the Number column, enter the block number that was defined in the block basis definition, as shown in Figure 8.31. Click the Save button to save the block and reference cycle definition. Figure 8.31 Block Maintenance: Create Reference Cycle This completes the block master data maintenance. Assign Block Intervals The next step is to assign the block definition to the model-dependent resource master data. To do so, navigate to the resource master data by double-clicking on the resource assigned to the 000 version in the list of resources displayed in the Change Resource: Header Data screen (from Transaction /SAPAPO/RES01). Navigate to the Block Planning tab, and click on the Maintain Blocks button. In the Maintain Blocks screen, navigate to the Intervals tab, as shown on the left in Figure 8.32. You can add individual blocks (no reference to the reference cycle) by clicking on the Insert Block button 1. In the New Date (Valid To) popup screen, fill in the Preceding To (Date) field and the time stamp in the To (Time) field, with the date and time until which you want the blocks to be gener- ated on the resource. If the Observe Productive Time checkbox is selected, the blocks will be created by respecting the productive working times of the resource. Click on the Execute button to generate the corresponding block as shown in Figure 8.33 1. You can insert the reference cycle by clicking on the Insert Reference Cycle button as shown in Figure 8.32 2. This will take you to the Insert Reference Cycle as of popup screen, where you can select the reference cycle from the Reference Cycle dropdown. Enter the date and time for which you want to insert the reference cycle in the Preced- ing To (Date) and the To (Time) fields, respectively. In the Insert field, enter the number of 8 Advanced PP/DS Features 502 times you want to insert the reference cycle into the resource. If you select the Overwrite, if Necessary checkbox, the existing block definition on the resource will be overwritten by the reference cycle being inserted. Click on the Execute button, and you’ll see that the blocks are inserted per the reference cycle definition, as shown in Figure 8.33 2. Figure 8.32 Block Planning: Maintain Block Intervals Figure 8.33 Block Planning: Display of Blocks in Block Maintenance After the block intervals are maintained in the resource master, you can transfer the PDS master data from SAP S/4HANA to embedded PP/DS using Transaction CUR- TOADV_CREATE. If the resource assigned to the operation/activity of the PDS has block planning, the same is also assigned to the activity of the PDS, as shown in Figure 8.34. © 503 8.3 Characteristics-Dependent Planning This enables the scheduling of the activities with characteristics on the blocks set with the same characteristics values. Figure 8.34 Block Planning Class in the PDS Activities Tip If the PDS master data is transferred before the resource classification is maintained for block planning, the PDS must be retransferred (absolute transfer) after the resource classification. In SAP S/4HANA, object dependencies are defined to select the relevant components and operations depending on the classification of the receipt element being created. If there are object dependencies assigned to the BOM and routing master data, the same is transferred to the PDS in PP/DS. In PDS, the object dependencies can be evaluated at the operation level or at the activity level. The prerequisite for integrating the object dependency data is that the object dependency master data in SAP S/4HANA is assigned to the correct dependency groups. The object dependency is only evaluated at the operation in PP/DS if you’ve assigned the dependency group SAPAPOOPR. The object dependency is only evaluated at the activity in PP/DS if you’ve assigned the dependency group SAPAPOACT. Blocks in Planning and in Scheduling When orders are created by planning heuristics or manually, the operations for which block planning-relevant resources are assigned will be scheduled on the corresponding block on the resource. In the strategy profile (refer to Chapter 6, Section 6.2.1), select Take Into Account in the Block Planning field, as shown in Figure 8.35. Blocks can also be set with fixing indicators; in this case, no new activities can be automatically scheduled in those blocks. To ignore the block fixings, choose 2 Take Into Account, Ignore Block Fixings from the Block Planning field in the strategy profile. The blocks can be displayed from the detailed scheduling planning board (Transaction /SAPAPO/CDPS0; see Chapter 6, Section 6.4.1). Although the demand elements are on the same date/time, when the production planning heuristic is creating the receipt 8 Advanced PP/DS Features 504 elements as mandated by the strategy profile, the blocks are considered, and orders are scheduled to place them on the correct blocks (with matching characteristics values). Figure 8.35 Block Planning: Strategy Profile Settings In the detailed scheduling planning board, the blocks are visually represented by the color set for the block definition in the master data. The orders are placed within the blocks as displayed in Figure 8.36. You can right-click on the graphical element of the blocks in the planning board to navigate to the block maintenance. From the block maintenance, the blocks can be created, changed (extend/shrink duration), or deleted. In this example, you can see the characteristic values 100 G 1, 200 G 2, and 500 G 3 that we’ve used throughout this chapter. From the detailed scheduling planning board, the following heuristics are supported for the maintenance of blocks:  SAP_CDPBP_01 (reschedule blocks) This heuristic can be used in situations where the block definitions or the schedule has changed, and the operations on the impacted blocks need to be rescheduled.  SAP_CDPBP_02 (adjust and reschedule block limits) When there are overload or underload situations, the adjust and reschedule block limits heuristic can be executed to extend or to shrink the blocks and schedule the operations within these blocks accordingly.  SAP_CDPBP_03 (enhanced block maintenance) This heuristic calls up the block maintenance screen for adjustment (creation, change) of the existing blocks on the resource. © 505

sections.title: Push Production
sections.en: 8.4 Push Production Figure 8.36 Blocks in the Detailed Scheduling Planning Board and Assignment of Orders to the Blocks 8.4 Push Production Push production is the process of creating a production plan to consume excess supply of a material. Push production is a purely manual process to create a production plan to consume excess supply of materials with no requirements. The push production tool helps in making decisions to consume such products. In a typical production planning scenario, the requirements of the lower-level materi- als in the BOM levels are determined by the demand of the materials in the higher lev- els of the BOM structure. Push production works in the opposite way by finding the higher-level materials that can be produced using the lower-level materials. In industries such as dairy, food processing, and so on, raw materials are procured based on long-term contracts, and a slight reduction in the demand for certain finished products or a production scheduling problem such as machine breakdown to produce a specific product can result in an oversupply of raw materials. In addition, the shelf life of such raw materials plays a major role in determining if there is a push problem for a material. For products with excess coverage, a low shelf life is required to consume the material or to convert it into another material with a higher shelf life. In this section, we’ll cover the details on how to identify a push problem in the supply chain and how the push production tool can help in resolving the same. 8 Advanced PP/DS Features 506

sections.title: Identify the Push Problem
sections.en: 8.4.1 Identify the Push Problem The primary tool for identifying the push problem is the Alert Monitor (refer to Chap- ter 7). In the Alert Monitor, you activate the alert Order creates surplus under the Order Alerts – Product-Dependent alert type. Enter the threshold for the Variance in % of the required versus excess receipts, as shown in Figure 8.37. Planners can also monitor such materials from the product view (Transaction /SAPAPO/ RRP3) or from the product overview (Transaction /SAPAPO/POV1) to identify materials causing excess supply and trigger push production. Figure 8.37 Setting Up Alert Monitor for Identifying Excess Supply

sections.title: Launch the Push Production View
sections.en: 8.4.2 Launch the Push Production View After the excess supply elements are identified for the products from the Alert Monitor or from the product overview, you can navigate to the product view (Transaction /SAPAPO/RRP3) and choose Menu  Go To  Push Production. The product view must be in edit mode (by clicking the Change button in the product view) to launch the push production. For the push production scenario to be executed, following are the prerequisites:  Excess supply is available for the material.  The material is part of at least one PDS. This will launch a new Push Production screen, as shown in Figure 8.38. The push pro- duction tool has the following four panels in the screen:  Sources of Supply In this panel, the system executes a where-used list for the material for which push production is being planned and lists all the PDSs that have the material as part of their components. © 507 8.4 Push Production  Surplus for Material In this panel, which is at the top panel on the screen, all the supply elements (orders, stock elements) causing the excess stock for the material are listed.  Sources of Supply for Consuming Products All the sources of supply are listed here. Quantities can be calculated by the system, or you can enter the quantities for the products that can consume the excess material.  Product View At the bottom of the screen, this view shows the products for which a new order is being created to consume the excess supply of the material. In addition, the alerts are generated accordingly based on the new orders being created, which can help you determine how much additional supply you can create for the product without resulting in too much supply considering the shelf life or other demand elements of the product being produced. Figure 8.38 Push Production: User Interface To consume the excess stock of the elements listed in the Surplus for Material panel (the top panel on the screen), select the supply element, and then click on the Adopt button in the Sources of Supply for Consuming Products section. This will calculate the quantity of the products/PDSs that can consume the quantity of the selected excess supply element for the excess material. Click on the create order button above the Sources of Supply for Consuming Products to create a new planned order using the selected PDS, and it will load the product view, 8 Advanced PP/DS Features 508 including the newly created planned order for the product. Although this is a manual process, it helps planners make decisions regarding consuming the excess supplies for critical materials in the production plan. As the planners have to make decisions as to what products to produce consuming the excess stock, this process is delivered as a manual process.

sections.title: Tank Planning
sections.en: 8.5 Tank Planning Tank planning is an interactive planning process where raw materials, intermediates, or finished products need to be stored in tanks, and the tanks have minimum/maxi- mum storage requirements. Products can be filled into the tank for inbound external receipts such as purchase requisitions, stock transfer receipts, and receipts from planned or process orders. The draining from the tanks is represented by consumption from the tanks by demand elements as dependent demands for in-house manufactur- ing orders (planned/process orders), sales order demands, and stock transfer demands. The maintenance of the storage characteristics for the storage resources (tanks) was already covered in Chapter 2 for master data. In this section, we’ll look into the example shown in Figure 8.39. Raw material is procured externally and filled into a tank, and the raw material is drained from the tank for the consumption of producing a finished product. The finished product is stored/filled in a tank, which has an option of storing in alternative tanks, and the finished product tank is drained by a stock transfer demand. We’ll look into the configuration, the master data settings, and the process of interactive planning using tanks (storage resources). Figure 8.39 Example of a Tank Planning Scenario Note As of SAP S/4HANA release 2022, the tank planning process is supported for interactive planning, where the tank fill levels can be visualized in the planning tools, manual rescheduling is required to resolve fill level violations, and alerts can be set up for viola- tions. Future road map items for embedded PP/DS includes consideration of tank con- straints in automatic planning and scheduling including Production Planning Optimizer and Detailed Scheduler Optimizer engines. Plant PPS2 Plant PPS3 Manufacturing (REACTOR) of S4PPDS_LIQUID_FERT1 TANK2 TANK3 Supplier delivering raw material (S4PPDS_LIQUID_RAW2) Stock transfer of S4PPDS_LIQUID_FERT1 from plant PPS2 TANK1 © 509 8.5 Tank Planning

sections.title: Configuration
sections.en: 8.5.1 Configuration There are two main Customizing settings required to set up the tank planning scenario in PP/DS. The product storage definition (PSD) configuration defines default values and settings for the creation of the PSDs, and the visualization settings enable the graphical visualization of the stock levels in the storage resources in tools such as the detailed scheduling planning board. We’ll cover the details of these customizations next. Product Storage Definitions Apart from setting up the storage characteristics such as the min/max stock levels and the threshold for setting the fill levels to 0, another master data object called product storage definition (PSD) is required. The storage definitions can be automatically gener- ated when integrating the master recipes from SAP S/4HANA to embedded PP/DS. For setting the default values and activation of PSD creation, navigate to SAP IMG menu path SPRO  Advanced Planning  Tank Planning with Container Resources  Maintain Settings for Tank Planning with Container Resources. In this Customizing transaction, there are two main screen areas, as shown in Figure 8.40. Figure 8.40 Configuration of Default Values for Product Storage Definitions Under the Defaults for PSD for Inhouse Production (Source Type PDS) area of the config- uration, you can configure the default values for the PSDs for the product data struc- tures (PDSs). When the master recipes are integrated to PP/DS via Transaction CURTOADV_CREATE, based on the settings maintained here, the default values are set in the PSDs. Consumption Type for Draining Activities refers to how the draining from the tank is defined. The following options are available: 8 Advanced PP/DS Features 510  Start of Activity The draining is defined as an operation in the master recipe, and the tank from which the material to be drained is assigned to the operation/phase. A duration will be assigned in the draining step phase. With the Start of Activity setting, the draining is performed at the start time stamp of the activity of the planned/process order.  End of Activity The draining of the tank that stores the material is performed at the time stamp of the end of the activity.  Continual Consumption In scenarios where the draining is continuous, this setting can be used. For example, if 1,000 liters of liquid needs to be consumed from the storage tank to the processing unit over a duration of 10 hours, every 1 hour, 100 liters of liquid are drained from the tank into the processing unit.  Undefined No default value is set during the automatic creation of the PSD during PDS integra- tion, and the consumption type needs to be manually maintained in the product PSD master data. Similarly, for the filling of the tanks, the default value for the way the tanks are filled is set in the Consumption Type for Filling Activities. Select the Generate Product Storage Definition During PDS Generation checkbox to automatically generate the PSD during PDS integration of master recipes. Note You can automate the PSD generation during PDS integration using business add-in (BAdI) /SAPAPO/CURTO_CREATE method CREATE_STORAGE_DEF. If this BAdI is implemented, irrespective of the PSD generation Customizing setting, the PSD will be generated. In master recipes, you can assign the materials to the phases. This is called the material flow in the PDSs. If you only want to generate the PSDs when only the material flow is defined in the master recipe, select the Product Flow Data Required checkbox. For external procurement, including stock transfer orders, if the tank filling or draining needs to be modeled using PSDs, these PSDs needs to be created manually. While creat- ing such PSDs manually, the default values are defined under the Defaults for PSD for External Procurement (Source Type MATLOC) section in this Customizing transaction. The Input/Output Indicator is defined if the material is an input or output as the result of external procurement. For example, for external procurement from a supplier, the material is an output for the PSD. For stock transfers, in the receiving plant, the mate- rial is an output; in the sending plant, the material is an input node of the stock transfer request/order. The default can be defined as output for this field if you always work © 511 8.5 Tank Planning with external procurement from suppliers. If both supplier procurement and stock transfers are used, you can set the value as Undefined and set the correct value in the PSD master data manually. In PDSs, the durations for the filling and draining activities are defined for the in-house manufacturing in the PDSs. But for external procurement, these durations need to be defined in the PSD master data. To default the filling and draining durations for exter- nal procurement and stock transfer scenarios, define the durations in the Duration for Filling Activities and Duration for Draining Activities fields. When the Goods Receipt or Goods Issue Time Applied checkbox is selected, the filling and draining durations are derived from the goods receipt and goods issue processing times defined in the exter- nal procurement relationships. Visualization Settings The tank fill levels can be visualized from the detailed scheduling planning board in the resource chart and the fill level chart. To configure the visualization of the tank fill lev- els in the detailed scheduling planning board, proceed to SAP IMG Customizing menu path SPRO  Advanced Planning  Detailed Scheduling  Settings for the Detailed Sched- uling  Planning Board  Maintain Planning Board Profiles. Here, copy any of the standard delivered profiles such as SAP001 into a new planning board profile. In the Chart area, ensure that the full level chart is included in the list of available charts, as shown in Figure 8.41. Figure 8.41 Availability of the Fill Level Chart in the Detailed Scheduling Planning Board Profile In the resource chart, you can represent the fill levels on the container resources with color coding. To configure this, in the planning board profile shown in Figure 8.41, nav- igate to the Resources Chart by double-clicking on the Chart 1. Here, navigate to the His- togram Data tab shown in Figure 8.42. 8 Advanced PP/DS Features 512 Under the Fill Level Color Settings, you can choose the colors that represent the follow- ing fill level situations:  Below 0 The fill level in the tank is a negative value (a drain activity on an empty tank).  Btw. 0 and Threshold The fill level of the tank is between 0 and the threshold defined for setting the fill level to 0 in the resource master data.  Btw Threshold/MaxSt The fill level is more than the threshold value but under the max stock allowed in the tank.  Above Max. Stock The fill level of the tank is more than the max allowed stock for the tank. Figure 8.42 Configuration of Tank Fill Level Visualization in the Detailed Scheduling Planning Board Resources Assign this detailed scheduling planning profile to an overall profile, which can be used to load the profiles in the detailed scheduling planning board (Transaction /SAPAPO/ CDPS0). In addition, in the product planning table (Transaction /SAPAPO/PPT1), you can have the fill level details as key figures in the periodic fill level periodic chart. To default the © 513 8.5 Tank Planning key figures displayed in the fill level periodic chart in the product planning table, create a fill level periodic profile. Navigate to SAP IMG menu path SPRO  Advanced Planning  Product Planning Table  Create Periodic Planning. Here, navigate to the Maintain Fill Level View Periodic folder in the navigation area 1. As shown in Figure 8.43, a standard profile SAP001 is delivered with all possible key figures for the fill levels. To remove any key figures, copy the SAP001 profile into another profile (in this example, the Fill Level Profile of ZTANK is created), and navigate to the Row Selection folder 2. Then, uncheck the selected flag 3 to suppress the corresponding key figure to be hidden in the pro- duct planning table. Figure 8.43 Product Planning Table: Fill Level Key Figures Configuration Once the fill level profile is created, assign this profile to the overall product planning table profile. Navigate to SAP IMG menu path SPRO  Advanced Planning  Product Plan- ning Table  Define Overall Settings for the Product Planning Table. In this transaction, enter the Fill Level View Periodic profile, as shown in Figure 8.44. 8 Advanced PP/DS Features 514 Figure 8.44 Assigning the Fill Level View Periodic Profile to the Product Planning Table Master Profile

sections.title: Master Data
sections.en: 8.5.2 Master Data As discussed in the configuration section, the PSD is an important master data element for tank planning. To create or maintain the PSD master data, navigate to SAP Easy Access menu path, Logistics  Advanced Planning  Master Data  Product Storage Defi- nition  Product Storage Definition or use Transaction /SAPAPO/STORDEF. For in-house production, the PDSs are generated, and resources with storage characteristics are part of the master recipe. You can use this transaction to edit the automatically created PSDs and to create new PSDs. For in-house manufacturing PDSs, you may not add the storage resources in the master recipe; in this case, you can use this transaction to manually create PSDs to define any filling or draining requirements. In the initial selection screen shown in Figure 8.45, enter the selection conditions. The Source Type indicates the type of the PSD. If the PSD is linked to a PDS, then select the PDS as the source type. When you select the PDS as the source type, the Source of Sup- ply will become ready for input, where you can enter the PDS to further filter the selec- tion. PSDs are created for external procurement and stock transfers are created at the location product level, so select the source type Location/Product for such PSDs. You can also block PSDs from being used in orders and in planning; to filter on the status of the PSD, you can use the Blocked for Planning field. © 515 8.5 Tank Planning Figure 8.45 Create/Maintain Product Storage Definition: Initial Screen Click on Execute to maintain the existing PSDs, or click on the Create button to create new PSDs manually. In the next screen, you’ll see the list of existing PSDs, as shown in Figure 8.46. The list of already created PSDs are displayed in the next screen, which has three main screen areas:  Product Storage Definition Details This area contains the header information of the PSD. The Source Type 1 is the type of PSD. The PDS types refer to the PSDs created with reference to a PDS. The MATLOC types are the ones created manually for external procurement or stock transfers. When the configuration is active for generation for PSDs during PDS transfer, then the PSD is automatically created by the system, and Created by System 2 is set. You can also create a PSD with reference to a PDS manually. You can block the PSD at the header by setting the Blocked for Planning 3 checkbox.  Input/Output In this area, the details of the type of the activity are defined. To display this selec- tion, select a row 4 from the Product Storage Definition Details area just described, and click on the Display PSD 5 button. This will load the activity details. The I/O indi- cator (I/O. Ind 6) is set according to the direction of the PSD. For example, in a stock transfer scenario, value I is set for input, which is consumption of the material from the supplying plant. So, in the supplying plant, this indicator should be set as I. For the receiving plant, it’s the output of the stock transfer order, so in the receiving plant, this indicator should be set as O. Value I denotes that the tank will be drained, and value O denotes that the tank will be filled, which is displayed in the Activity Type 7 field. The Cons. Type 8 determines if the draining or filling activity is performed at the start time stamp of the activity or at the end time stamp of the order activity, or the consumption is continuous throughout the activity duration. Select a row from this section, and click on the Display Alternative Resources button 9 to load the section of the screen. 8 Advanced PP/DS Features 516  Alternative Resources In this area, all the possible tanks into which the material can be filled or from where the material can be drained can be maintained. The priority for the tank selection (this is similar to the mode priorities in the PDS) can be maintained in the Priority A field. To add an alternative tank, use the Assign Alternative Resource button B. Figure 8.46 Product Storage Definition Master Data In our example scenario (refer to Figure 8.39), the following PSDs are created:  For material S4PPDS_LIQUID_RAW2, the PSD is created manually with source type MATLOC and with activity type of filling in location PPS2 (as the PPS2 plant is receiv- ing the material from a supplier).  For material S4PPDS_LIQUID_FERT1, the PSD is automatically generated during the PDS transfer using Transaction CURTOADV_CREATE. In the master recipe, a drain- ing operation is defined with the resource TANK1 (where the raw material is stored), as shown in Figure 8.47 1. To this operation, material S4PPDS_LIQUID_RAW2 is assigned and has a processing 2 operation in a non-tank resource and a filling oper- ation to the receiving tank TANK2. The resource classification 3 is leveraged to add the TANK3 as an alternative tank to TANK2. In the master recipe, the drain and pro- cessing phases are set with a start-start relationship, so that when the processing operation starts, TANK1 will be drained at the start of the activity. When the opera- tions are classified in the master recipe, you can see that the Cla (classification) flag 4 is activated by the system. © 517 8.5 Tank Planning Figure 8.47 Master Recipe Structure in SAP S/4HANA This creates the elements in the PSD, as shown in Figure 8.48. In the Components area of the PSD, raw material S4PPDS_LIQUID_RAW2 is set with Draining 1 activity type. The finished product S4PPDS_LIQUID_FERT1 is set with Filling 2 activity type. The duration of the filling and draining will refer to the activity durations in the PDS. For the drain- ing activity, TANK1 3 is assigned, and the tanks TANK2 and TANK3 4 are assigned to the filling activity. Figure 8.48 PSD Based on Master Recipe (PDS) Master Data In addition, a manual PSD is created for the finished product in plant PPS2 with a draining activity, as the material is sent from plant PPS2 to PPS3 plant via the stock transfer process. 8 Advanced PP/DS Features 518

sections.title: Interactive Tank Planning
sections.en: 8.5.3 Interactive Tank Planning With the preceding data setup, we have the following transaction data elements, as shown in Figure 8.49: 1 A purchase requisition is created to procure the raw material from a supplier. You can see the Purch. Requisition element as a filling activity assigned based on the PSD. 2 A planned order is created for manufacturing the finished material. The filling and draining activities are derived from the PDS master data. 3 A stock transfer request is created for transfer of the finished material from plant PPS2 to PPS3. Here, you can see a draining activity in plant PPS2. Figure 8.49 Tank Filling and Draining Activities in PP/DS Transaction Data Objects In the detailed scheduling planning board, use an appropriate overall profile, as dis- cussed in the configuration section, and load all these container (tank) resources. In the detailed scheduling planning board in the resource chart, you can see the filling and draining activities from the manually created PSDs for external procurement, and the stock transfers along with the activities from the PDS for in-house production are dis- played. In the fill level chart, the bars show the fill level of the tanks. As shown in Figure 8.50, the inbound purchase requisition 1 is scheduled from 24.04.2023 to 29.04.2023 (five days of fill time set in the PSD). The fill level 2 is set to the full purchase requisition quantity at the start of the activity (consumption type in PSD). On 02.05.2023, when the planned order is draining 3 part of the quantity from TANK1, you can see the fill level reduction 4 in the fill level chart. The filling activity 5 of the planned order to TANK2 is set with Continuous, so the fill level of TANK2 starts at the start of the fill activity and is continuously filled 5 throughout the duration of the fill activity. © 519 8.5 Tank Planning On 06.05.2023, the stock transfer request is draining 6 TANK2, and the fill level reduc- tion is shown in the fill level chart 7. Figure 8.50 Fill Levels in the Detailed Scheduling Planning Board When there are alternative tanks available (in this example, TANK3 is an alternative to TANK2), you can drag and drop the orders between the alternatives in case one tank is completely filled. In the fill level chart, you can invoke the context menu (right-click) and select the Fill Level Detail List 1 to see the details of the activities that are filling and draining the tank, as shown in Figure 8.51. Figure 8.51 Interactive Scheduling of Tanks In the Fill Level Detail List popup window 2, you can click on the ChngStRes 3 (change storage resource) to switch the storage resources (when alternative tanks are defined in 8 Advanced PP/DS Features 520 the PSD). Once you click the change button 3, a new popup appears with the list of all available tanks (storage resources), where you can use the allocate and deallocate but- tons 4 to assign or unassign the tanks. In the tabular planning tool, which is the product planning table (Transaction /SAPAPO/ PPT1), you can evaluate the fill levels as shown in Figure 8.52. Load the fill level chart 1, and in the fill level key figure 2, double-click on the fill level cells to load the detailed activity list of filling and draining. In the detailed list 3, you can also change the storage resource by clicking on the change storage resource (ChngStRes) button 4. In the product planning table selection screen, you can set the Evaluate PSD flag to include the storage resources that aren’t part of the product’s PDS, but are the storage resources defined in the PSD master data for PDSs and MATLOC combinations. Figure 8.52 Interactive Tank Planning in the Product Planning Table Tip In the product view, when storage resources are assigned to orders, you can right-click on the orders to switch the storage resource when alternative storage resources are defined in the PSD master data. In the Alert Monitor, there are specific alert types delivered for the container resources (tanks), as shown in Figure 8.53. From the PP/DS planning and scheduling tools, you can invoke the Alert Monitor to display the alerts for various exceptions in the tank plan- ning scenario. © 521

sections.title: Production Campaign Planning
sections.en: 8.6 Production Campaign Planning Figure 8.53 Alerts for Container Resources 8.6 Production Campaign Planning Production campaign planning is a process of grouping orders with similar characteris- tics to be produced on the same bottleneck production line. For example, if a manufac- turing line manufactures various colors of paints, it makes sense to keep the same- colored paint orders together before switching to another color. In such production lines, to switch between products with different characteristics, there is a setup or clea- nout time involved. So, in the production campaign planning processes in PP/DS, objects called production campaigns are created, and orders with the same setup group are assigned to the campaigns. Apart from the setup and cleanout times and the associated costs, the storage of the products may also incur costs. For example, if an intermediate material is produced and stored in a container that incurs high costs to maintain the container when prod- ucts are stored, it needs to be consumed by the subsequent production of the finished product to keep the storage cost minimal. In PP/DS production campaign planning, there are various tools available to create and manage such campaigns:  Transaction /SAPAPO/PCMT (Production Campaign) This transaction is available in the PP/DS system to manually create and manage the production campaigns in a tabular form. 8 Advanced PP/DS Features 522  Detailed scheduling planning board This allows you to graphically visualize the production campaigns and leverage dedi- cated heuristics that are available for creating and managing production campaigns.  Detailed Scheduling Optimizer Detailed Scheduling Optimizer is used to evaluate the setup matrix to reduce the setup times and costs, as well as optimize the storage costs associated with changes in the sequencing of the orders. Detailed Scheduling Optimizer optimizes the setup times/costs and storage costs, and it also creates the production campaigns. The production campaigns are also objects in the SAP S/4HANA system. So, the embed- ded PP/DS campaigns are also integrated via the core interface to SAP S/4HANA. In the SAP S/4HANA side, there are processes to handle the campaigns with respect to prod- uct costing. The functionality of block planning isn’t to be confused with campaign planning. Block planning focuses on predefining blocks at the resource level of certain durations with preassigned characteristics for the block, so that the orders with characteristics can only be scheduled in those blocks. The blocks are PP/DS master data objects and have no relevance in SAP S/4HANA. Next, we’ll cover the required configuration settings, master data objects, and various tools that can be leveraged in PP/DS to perform the production campaign planning.

sections.title: Configuration
sections.en: 8.6.1 Configuration The configuration settings required for campaign planning consists of setting up the number ranges for the campaigns in PP/DS, the campaign profiles that define the color of the campaigns, and the visualization settings to graphically represent the campaigns in the detailed scheduling planning board. Number Ranges The production campaigns created in PP/DS are assigned with PP/DS campaign num- bers. When they are integrated to SAP S/4HANA, the campaigns will get assigned an external campaign number (i.e., the campaign number assigned in SAP S/4HANA). But the PP/DS campaign number is retained throughout the campaign’s lifecycle. Figure 8.54 Number Range Assignment for PP/DS Production Campaigns © 523 8.6 Production Campaign Planning To manage the number range of the PP/DS production campaigns, navigate to SAP IMG menu path SPRO  Advanced Planning  Global Settings  Maintain Number Ranges for Production Campaigns. In this transaction, if no default entry is available, create a new number range for the default object PCM. You can also change the existing number range assignments from this transaction, as shown in Figure 8.54. Campaign Profile The campaign profile is an object used by the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer when creat- ing optimized campaigns. To create the campaign profile, navigate to SAP IMG menu path SPRO  Advanced Planning  Production Campaign Planning  Maintain Campaign Profile. The campaign profile is based on the setup groups that are assigned to the master recipe operations. The characteristics-based generated setup groups aren’t available for selection while creating the campaign profile. So, these setup groups should exist in the SAP S/4HANA side and are integrated over to embedded PP/DS via an integration model. The initial screen of this configuration transaction, as shown in Figure 8.55, has a client- wide setting 1 for the placement of the setup clean-out order. For example, if the cam- paign is created for orders with a setup group for color white and transitioning to another campaign for orders for color black, this setting will determine if a cleanout time needs to be planned at the end of the white color orders’ campaign or a setup time needs to be planned in the black colored orders’ campaign. Figure 8.55 Campaign Profile in PP/DS 8 Advanced PP/DS Features 524 To create a new campaign profile, click on the New Entries button 2. In the New Entries screen, enter a name and description for the campaign profile. Enter the plant in which the profile is relevant in the Location field. In the Setup Group field, select the setup group for which this campaign profile is relevant. Only the static setup groups, which are core interfaced over from SAP S/4HANA, are available for selection in this field. In the Max. no. of charges field, enter the maximum number of orders that the optimizer can cover under one campaign. For example, if there are 50 orders in the optimization horizon with the same setup group, and if the maximum number of charges is 25, the optimizer would create 2 campaigns with 25 orders each. The Campaign Color field determines the graphical representation of the campaigns in the detailed scheduling planning board. Visualization When campaign planning is leveraged, it’s required to display the campaigns as graph- ical objects to enable production schedulers to manage the campaigns to add orders, remove orders, or split the campaigns in the detailed scheduling planning board. To make the campaign object to be displayed an overarching graphical object covering the orders contained in the campaign, the detailed scheduling planning board profile needs to be enabled to display the campaigns. The detailed scheduling planning board profile can be configured from SAP IMG menu path SPRO  Advanced Planning  Detailed Scheduling  Settings for the Detailed Scheduling Planning Board  Maintain Planning Board Profiles. In the standard system, a detailed scheduling planning board profile SAP_PCM is delivered that has the specific setting in the resource chart settings, as shown in Figure 8.56. If you want to combine other requirements for the resource chart along with the cam- paign planning requirements, enable the Campaigns checkbox in your specific plan- ning board profile. The color of the campaign bar in the detailed scheduling planning board is determined from the campaign profile, when the campaigns are created by a campaign heuristic, or from the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer. When you create the campaigns manually from the detailed scheduling planning board, you can select the color of the campaign for the display in the planning board. Assign the planning board profile to an overall profile. In the standard system, an over- all profile “SAP_PCM” is delivered with the required settings for campaign planning in the detailed scheduling planning board. © 525 8.6 Production Campaign Planning Figure 8.56 Activation of Campaign Visualization in the Detailed Scheduling Planning Board: Resource Chart

sections.title: Master Data
sections.en: 8.6.2 Master Data For campaign planning, especially for the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer to create opti- mized campaigns, there are specific master data requirements. The storage cost of the products is defined in the material master, which will be evaluated by the Detailed Sched- uling Optimizer during campaign optimization to calculate the storage costs if the out- put of the product isn’t consumed immediately. As shown in Figure 8.57, in the material master under the Advanced Planning view, maintain the storage cost in the Prod. Storage Cost field. This cost is to store the material in its base unit of measure for one day. Figure 8.57 Storage Cost for Products in the Material Master 8 Advanced PP/DS Features 526 For leveraging the campaign planning functionalities, the resource master should be activated for campaign planning. As shown in Figure 8.58, in the resource master data under the capacity header, navigate to the Header Data for APO Resource view, and select the Campaign Relevant 1 checkbox. When this is activated, during scheduling, the system will ensure that when campaigns are available on the resource, no new orders that can’t belong to the campaign (having a different setup group) are scheduled within the campaign. For the optimizer to select the resources relevant for campaigns, the resources must be set with the Bottleneck Resource 2 indicator in the resource master data. Figure 8.58 Resource Master Data Settings for Campaign Planning To create the setup groups, follow SAP IMG menu path, SPRO  Production Planning for Process Industries  Master Data  Master Recipe  Data for Operations and Phases  Define Setup Groups and Setup Group Categories. In this example shown in Figure 8.59, we’ve created two setup groups—BLACK and WHITE—in plant PPS2. Figure 8.59 Creation of Setup Groups in SAP S/4HANA © 527 8.6 Production Campaign Planning Create an integration model for the setup groups using Transaction CFM1, and activate the integration model via Transaction CFM2. During the campaign planning process, the system evaluates the setup group assigned to the setup activity of the PDS, and the campaigns are created for the orders with the same setup group. To have the setup groups in the PDS, the setup phases in the master recipe should be assigned with the setup groups, as shown in Figure 8.60. The phase that has the setup group assigned and the next phase of the same operation should have a finish-start relationship, and the resource in PP/DS should also be assigned with the setup matrix for the correct integration of the setup activity to the PP/DS PDS. Figure 8.60 Setup Group Assignment to the Master Recipe and the Setup Activity in PP/DS PDS To define the setup matrix in PP/DS, use Transaction /SAPAPO/CDPSC7 or follow SAP Easy Access menu path, Logistics  Advanced Planning  Master Data  Setup Group/ Setup Matrix. In this simple example, the setup matrix is defined to changeover from BLACK to WHITE and WHITE to BLACK (see Figure 8.61 1). In campaign planning, when campaigns are created, there is an option to create setup and cleanout orders, which will replace the setup activity of the first order in the campaign. These setup/cleanout 8 Advanced PP/DS Features 528 orders are also integrated to SAP S/4HANA so that the cost of the setup or cleanout can be distributed to the orders within the same campaign. When defining the setup matrix, you can assign a PDS to the changeovers so that the setup or cleanout orders are created based on this PDS 2. You can use the campaign heu- ristics or Detailed Scheduling Optimizer to create the setup/cleanout orders, which will replace the setup time of the first order in the campaign with a separate planned order based on the PDS assigned in the setup matrix. In our example, dummy material S4PP_ DS_SETUP_CLEANOUT is created, and a produce operation is defined with the equal dura- tion of the changeover transition in its master recipe/PDS. In this example, WHITE to BLACK and BLACK to WHITE has 5 hours of changeover duration, so only one PDS is gen- erated with 5 hours (18,000 sec) of produce time 3. It’s important to create these setup/ cleanout PDSs with an assigned duration that is equal to the setup time defined in the setup matrix. For example, if WHITE to BLACK is 5 hours, you need to have a PDS for the dummy material with 5 hours of operation time; likewise, for BLACK to WHITE, if the dura- tion is 7 hours, you’ll have another PDS for the dummy material with 7 hours of produce time, which is assigned to the corresponding transition in the setup matrix. Figure 8.61 Setup Matrix Creation in PP/DS and Assignment of PDS for Setup/Cleanout Orders

sections.title: Campaign Planning Tools
sections.en: 8.6.3 Campaign Planning Tools There are various tools in PP/DS that can be used to create and manage the production campaigns. We’ll cover the details of those tools in this section. © 529 8.6 Production Campaign Planning Production Campaign Transaction The production campaign transaction is a completely manual process to create produc- tion campaigns and assign orders to them. No graphical support is available within the transaction, but the campaigns created in the campaign transactions can be visualized in the detailed scheduling planning board. To launch the campaign transaction, follow Sap Easy Access menu path Logistics  Advanced Planning  Production Planning  Interactive Production Planning  Production Campaign. You can also use Transaction /SAPAPO/PCMT. In the initial screen of the transaction shown in Figure 8.62, you can enter the selection criteria for the existing campaigns and click on the Change or Display 1 button to manage existing campaigns. To create a new campaign, click on the New Campaign button 2. Figure 8.62 Campaign Transaction: Selection Screen In the next screen, shown in Figure 8.63, you’ll see a list of existing campaigns per the selection options entered in the initial screen. Even with the Create Campaigns option, the existing campaigns per the selection are displayed in the left side of the screen 1. To create a new campaign, enter a description and select a color for the campaign. The color is used for the display of the campaign bar in the detailed scheduling planning board. To create new planned orders and assign them to the campaign being created, click on the Create and Add Orders button 2 at the bottom of the screen. This will open the Create and Add Orders to Production Campaign popup screen. Enter the product, location, quantity, and dates for the new planned orders, and click on the Create and Add Orders button 3. The orders will be added to the campaign, but you’ll have to close 4 the popup window to see the added orders. If you want to add existing orders to the new campaign, you can use the Add Existing Orders button 5. 8 Advanced PP/DS Features 530 Figure 8.63 Manual Creation of Production Campaigns Once the new campaign is saved, you can see the Ext. Camp. No. field (see Figure 8.64) 1 is updated with the corresponding SAP S/4HANA campaign number. In addition, you can load the resource in the detailed scheduling planning board with a campaign-rele- vant overall profile (SAP_PCM is the standard delivered overall profile), and you can visualize the new campaign 2 in the detailed scheduling planning board. Figure 8.64 Update of SAP S/4HANA Campaign Number and Campaign Visualization in the Detailed Scheduling Planning Board © 531 8.6 Production Campaign Planning As this campaign is created manually and doesn’t use the Detailed Scheduling Opti- mizer, you can see that the finite resource is overloaded with multiple orders in parallel within the campaign 3. Heuristics for Campaign Planning In the standard PP/DS system, there are various heuristics delivered to create and man- age the production campaigns. We’ll cover the details of these heuristics next. All the campaign heuristics can be executed interactively in the detailed scheduling planning board or in the background using the PP/DS planning run (Transaction /SAPAPO/ CDPSB0).  Create production campaigns This heuristic with name SAP_PCM_CRT and algorithm /SAPAPO/HEUR_PCM_CRE- ATE creates new production campaigns based on the existing sequence of the orders. When there are orders that aren’t sequenced correctly—that is, when orders with different setup groups are sequenced without considering the reduction in setup time—the campaigns will be created for every setup group transition. As shown in Figure 8.65, based on the existing sequence, this heuristic creates cam- paigns for every setup group transition. In this example, the setup groups are BLACK and WHITE. The campaign colors green 1 and orange 2 are assigned for these setup groups, and the campaigns are created accordingly. This heuristic can result in over- loads 3 on resources if there are existing overloads before execution of this heuris- tic. So, it’s essential that the resource is scheduled finitely using a heuristic or the orders are scheduled finitely and optimized for setup times using Detailed Schedul- ing Optimizer before this heuristic is executed.
