You can interactively drag and drop orders between the campaigns, and the campaign dates will be adjusted accordingly. In addition, you can see that the setup times are still attached to the orders in which the setup time is attached 4 (no standalone setup/cleanout orders are created). This heuristic can also be executed in a background planning run (Transaction /SAPAPO/ CDPSB0). Figure 8.65 Result of the Create Production Campaign Heuristic 8 Advanced PP/DS Features 532  Dissolve production campaigns This heuristic delivered with the name SAP_PCM_DIS and the algorithm /SAPAPO/ HEUR_PCM_DISSOLVE dissolves (deletes) the existing production campaigns on the resource. All the campaigns, including the manually created campaigns, will be dis- solved when this heuristic is executed. As shown in Figure 8.66, all the campaigns, including ones created via the heuristics and created manually, are dissolved. Figure 8.66 Results of the Dissolve Production Campaign Heuristics  Create setup/cleanout orders This heuristic (SAP_PCM_SRVA) with algorithm /SAPAPO/HEUR_PCM_SERVICE_ ADAPT deletes and re-creates the setup/cleanout orders. In the production cam- paign, the sequence-dependent (based on the setup matrix) setup time of the first order in the campaign will be replaced with a new planned order using the PDS assigned in the setup matrix. Whether the system should create a setup order (the first order within the production campaign), or it should create a cleanout order as the last order of the preceding campaign (still replacing the sequence dependent setup activity of the first order in the succeeding campaign) is determined by the configuration settings maintained in the campaign profile transaction. In this example, the configuration for the campaign profile, which is at the client level, is set as use-up orders. As shown in Figure 8.67, the setup activities 1 before the execu- tion of the heuristics are replaced with planned orders 2 using the dummy mate- rial’s PDS 3 assigned to the setup matrix after the execution of the heuristics.  Delete setup/cleanout orders This heuristic (SAP_PCM_ODEL) with algorithm /SAPAPO/HEUR_PCM_ORDERS_ DELETE can be used to delete the setup/cleanout orders in the production campaign. This heuristic works based on the selection of the product/location. So, in the detailed scheduling planning board, you need to select the product and execute this heuristic. As this heuristic will delete all orders, it’s important that you select the dummy material with which the setup/cleanout orders are created for the cam- paigns. If you’re using Detailed Scheduling Optimizer to optimize the setup times/ costs without leveraging the campaign optimization in Detailed Scheduling Opti- mizer, it’s required to delete the setup/cleanout orders before the execution of this heuristic, so that the setup activities are available in the corresponding planned orders, which Detailed Scheduling Optimizer can evaluate and optimize. © 533 8.6 Production Campaign Planning Figure 8.67 Create Setup/Cleanout Orders Heuristics in Campaign Planning Apart from the campaign planning specific heuristics, there are also functions pro- vided in the detailed scheduling planning board to interactively create and manage campaigns. The functions are available in the menu Functions  Production Campaign, as shown in Figure 8.68. Figure 8.68 Interactive Campaign Management Functions in the Detailed Scheduling Planning Board 8 Advanced PP/DS Features 534 Campaign Optimization Campaign optimization using the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer is the most powerful tool to automatically create campaigns and setup/cleanout orders, which are opti- mized for setup times/costs and storage costs. In the standard PP/DS system, the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer profile SAP_PCM is delivered with preset settings that are required for the campaign optimization. Apart from the objective functions and settings we’ve already covered in Chapter 6, the campaign-specific settings are avail- able in the Additional Strategies tab of the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer profile, as shown in Figure 8.69. Figure 8.69 Standard Detailed Scheduling Optimization Profile for Campaign Optimization The Bottleneck Optimization and Campaign Creatn option is selected, which enables the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer to create optimized campaigns. For the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer to create optimized campaigns, it’s mandatory that only one bottleneck is defined in the PDS. If there are alternative resources available in the PDS, all of the alternatives must be marked as bottleneck resources. You can allocate different weightages for the storage/setup/delay/mode costs and setup time. The © 535

sections.title: Segmentation
sections.en: 8.7 Segmentation Existing Campaigns option determines how existing campaigns are treated during optimization:  Dissolve Dissolve existing campaigns at the start of the optimization, so that new campaigns are created.  Extend Existing campaigns can be added with new orders, and/or the campaigns may be moved on the same resource in which they were originally created.  Retain The existing campaigns can only be moved in the same resource in which they were originally created. Orders can’t be added or removed from the campaign. At the end of the optimization, the campaigns are created with an optimized sequence of orders, so that the setup costs/times are reduced, and a balance between the setup/ storage/delay is achieved. Compared to Figure 8.65, shown earlier, in which the cam- paign was created using the heuristics, the optimizer-created campaigns, as shown in Figure 8.70, are finitely scheduled and optimized for changeovers 1. In addition, you can see that the setup orders 2 are created (replacing the setup activity of the first order in the campaign), which is also done by the optimizer. Figure 8.70 Result of Campaign Optimization in the Detailed Scheduling Planning Board The optimizer and heuristics can be either interactively used or scheduled as a back- ground job. Irrespective of the PP/DS tool used for creating and managing the cam- paigns, once the results are saved in PP/DS, they are transferred back to SAP S/4HANA, and PP/DS is updated with the external campaign number from the SAP S/4HANA sys- tem. 8.7 Segmentation Segmentation was originally developed for the fashion industry to segregate the sup- ply and demand elements for products. The segmentation could be based on different markets, customers, and so on. For example, if the same product with the same form, fit, and function is being sold to different markets with different regulatory require- 8 Advanced PP/DS Features 536 ments (e.g., a different statutory label on the product), then, in the SAP systems, sepa- rate material masters and corresponding BOMs/routings or master recipes are created for those separate materials. With segmentation in SAP S/4HANA, the demand and supply elements for the same product can be tagged with a segment value, which helps avoid the need to create separate master data elements. As similar solution require- ments are also relevant for other industries, such as life sciences, the segmentation solution in SAP S/4HANA was enhanced to support non-fashion industry–related mas- ter and transaction data objects as well. From SAP S/4HANA 2021, the SAP S/4HANA segmentation solution was improved to include the segmentation fields in many of the production planning data elements such as planned orders, process orders, and master recipes. Before SAP S/4HANA 2021, segmentation was supported in objects such as BOMs, routings, and production orders. Starting with the SAP S/4HANA 2022 release, the SAP S/4HANA segmentation is also integrated with embedded PP/DS for enabling segment-dependent planning in PP/DS. The segmentation supports using CDP as well (refer to Section 8.3 for the details on CDP). In this section, we’ll focus on an example of setting up basic data in SAP S/4HANA to create a segmentation strategy and integrate the CDP data to PP/DS, and illustrate examples of how master data and transaction data are integrated to PP/DS while respecting the segmentation data from SAP S/4HANA. We won’t cover the configura- tion and in-depth details of the segmentation functionality in the SAP S/4HANA side. Within PP/DS, because CDP is used for segmentation, the configuration schema of the embedded PP/DS system must be set as CDP.

sections.title: Master Data
sections.en: 8.7.1 Master Data Segmentation strategy is the basic master data for the segmentation functionality in SAP S/4HANA, where the possible segmentation values and combinations are defined. The first step is to create characteristics in the SAP S/4HANA system and include the possible segment values as the characteristics value. In this example, as shown in Fig- ure 8.71, the characteristics S4PPDS_SEGMENT3 is created, which represents the list of ship-to countries. Set the Char. Group with the Segmentation option 1, and maintain all possible characteristics values in the Values tab 2. In the additional data view of the characteristics master data, click on the Relevance button, as shown in Figure 8.72 1, and ensure the objects are selected 2. © 537 8.7 Segmentation Figure 8.71 Characteristics for Segmentation Figure 8.72 Checking the Relevancy Flag for the Segmentation Characteristics To create the segmentation strategy, launch Transaction SGT_SETUP. In this transac- tion, enter the characteristic name on which the segmentation strategy should be based. In this example, we’re using the characteristic S4PPDS_SEGMENT3. Execute the transaction (see Figure 8.73) 1, and in the next screen, you’ll see any segmentation structures that already exist in the system. As this is a new characteristic, there are no existing entries 2. Switch to change mode, and click on the Create button 3. In the popup window, enter a name for the segmentation structure and a description 4. 8 Advanced PP/DS Features 538 Figure 8.73 Creation of Segmentation Structure in SAP S/4HANA Once you save the popup, again switch to change mode, double-click on the segmenta- tion structure name (in our example, PPS3), as shown in Figure 8.74 1, and in the right side of the screen, click on the Add Line button 2. Enter the characteristic name (“S4PPDS_SEGMENT3”) in the Characteristic field 3, press (Enter), and save the trans- action. Click on the segment structure name (PPS3), and click on the New button 4. Figure 8.74 Segmentation Strategy: Creation in SAP S/4HANA © 539 8.7 Segmentation In the popup, enter a name and description for the segmentation strategy 5. For the segmentation scope 6, select value 1 (Requirement and Stock Segments Maintained) as we want both the receipt elements and requirement elements to be segregated by the segment. Click the Save button in the popup screen. Switch to change mode in the same transaction, and expand the segmentation struc- ture. As shown in Figure 8.75, double-click on the segmentation strategy (PPDSSTR) 1. In the right side of the screen, click on the Generate button 2. In the Generate Combi- nations popup screen 3, click on the Segment Value button 4. In the resulting Select Segment Values popup 5, select the values from the Characteristic Value list 6 that need to be part of the segmentation strategy, and click Continue. Now the segmenta- tion combinations are created 7. Save the transaction. Figure 8.75 Generating Segment Combinations for the Segmentation Strategy The next step is to generate the rules for the segmentation rules. In change mode, select the segmentation strategy, and click on the Generate Rules button 1, as shown in Figure 8.76. The rules will be generated, and you can see the Generate Rules column turn green for many of the categories 2. Select any of the nodes 3 under the segmentation strat- egy, and click on the Display Rules button 4 to display the allowed combinations for the 8 Advanced PP/DS Features 540 stock (receipt) and requirement segments (in this example the Dependent Require- ment/Stock transfer 5 is shown). Figure 8.76 Segmentation Strategy: Generate Rules This completes the basic settings in the SAP S/4HANA side of the segmentation strat- egy master data. In PP/DS, the segmentation strategy will be integrated as a CDP class (class type 400), and the segmentation rules are generated as SAP liveCache constraints (allowed com- binations of characteristics for the receipt and requirement elements) for the CDP planning. To accomplish this, as shown in Figure 8.77, in the same transaction, in change mode, select the segmentation strategy 1, and click on the Generate CDP Class button 2. You’ll see a success message if the class creation in PP/DS is successful, and the CDP Class and Characteristics field will be activated 3. You can display the CDP class via Transaction CL02 by using the segmentation strategy as the Class name and the Class type as 400 4. To generate the segmentation rules as SAP liveCache constraints, click on the Transfer to SAP liveCache button 5. If the transfer is successful, the live- Cache Transfer field 6 will be activated. Tip The BAdI BADI_SGT_PPDS_ORG_AREA can be implemented to determine the Org Areas (Transaction O1CL) for the integration of the segmentation class to PP/DS. In the material master, the segmentation strategy is assigned to the Basic Data 2 view, as shown in Figure 8.78. In addition, the plant-specific assignment is made in the Plant data / stor. 1 view. © 541 8.7 Segmentation Figure 8.77 Transfer of the CDP Class and SAP liveCache Constraints for Segmentation Figure 8.78 Segmentation Strategy Assignment to the Material Master When the segment strategy is assigned to the material master, and if the material is advanced planning–relevant, a core interface queue will be generated with the material 8 Advanced PP/DS Features 542 number as part of the core interface queue to update the classification of the material in the PP/DS side. You can verify the successful update of the classification in PP/DS using the product master (Transaction /SAPAPO/MAT1) in the Classification view, as shown in Figure 8.79. Figure 8.79 Segmentation: Classification in PP/DS the Product Master with Class Type 400 Production Data Structure The PDS is a combination of BOMs/routings/production versions or master recipes. In this example, we’ll see how segment-specific BOM components and routing operations are created and how the object dependencies are automatically generated in the PDS components and activities. In the BOM, in our example shown in Figure 8.80, we have a raw material (S4PPDS_ SGMT_RAW) that isn’t restricted by any segments. But the materials with the LABEL are segment specific. To assign the segment to the BOM components, select the BOM item 1, and click on the Segmentation button 2. In the next screen, select the conditions for the segment. In this example, we’re including this component S4PPDS_SGMT_LABEL_ USA to the segment USA 3. Click on the Accept 4 button, and map the segments for other components in the BOMs as required. Similarly, in the routing, you can assign segments to the operations if the operations/ resources need to be defined differently for different segments. As shown in Figure 8.81, select the operation in the routing 1, and click on the Segmentation button 2. Assign the segment value 3, and click on the Accept button 4 to copy the segment value to the routing operation. Assign segments to all relevant operations. © 543 8.7 Segmentation Figure 8.80 Assignment of Segments to BOM Components Figure 8.81 Assignment of Segment Values to Routing Operations 8 Advanced PP/DS Features 544 Create a production version, and assign the BOM and routing to the production ver- sion. You can use Transaction CURTOADV_CREATE to generate the PDS in PP/DS. In the PDS, you can see the dependencies assigned per the segment values in the BOM components and the routing operations, respectively, for the PDS components and activities. Figure 8.82 shows the object dependencies for the components 1 and the activities 2 of the PDS. Figure 8.82 Automatic Generation of Object Dependencies in PDS Components and Activities

sections.title: Transaction Data
sections.en: 8.7.2 Transaction Data All the transaction data objects in SAP S/4HANA for materials with segmentation assignments will require the segment value to be assigned while creating such transac- tion data. In PP/DS, these segment assignments from SAP S/4HANA will be transferred as characteristics assignments to the PP/DS transaction data. For example, as shown in Figure 8.83, a sales order is created in SAP S/4HANA. As you can see, the requirement segment becomes a mandatory field 1, and in the value help (F4) for this field, you can see the possible segments 2 for assignment. When this sales order is transferred to PP/DS, in the product view (Transaction /SAPAPO/RRP3), you can see the characteristics assignment 3 with the segment value assigned in the SAP S/4HANA sales order 4. © 545 8.7 Segmentation Figure 8.83 Transaction Data: Segment Value Transfer from SAP S/4HANA to PP/DS Within PP/DS, the segmentation characteristic is treated the same as any other CDP characteristic. The pegging and planning process respects the constraint to make sure only the receipts and requirements with the same segment (characteristics) value is pegged. For details of pegging and planning using CDP, refer to Section 8.3.1. As shown in Figure 8.84, when PP/DS creates a receipt element, the Segmentation Value 1 is assigned due to CDP, and the characteristics value is transferred along with the planned order to the SAP S/4HANA side. In SAP S/4HANA, the planned order is assigned with the corresponding segment value 2. Figure 8.84 Transaction Data: Transfer of Segment Value from PP/DS to SAP S/4HANA 8 Advanced PP/DS Features 546

sections.title: Summary
sections.en: 8.8 Summary Embedded PP/DS offers many advanced features, including some of the industry- specific functionalities (e.g., tank planning) covered in this chapter. Other industry- specific advanced features are also available in the PP/DS system that can be used across industries, although some of them have an industry flavor. Following are some of the other advanced PP/DS industry-specific features:  PP/DS repetitive manufacturing is used by automotive and automotive parts man- ufacturers or any industry with takt-based scheduling requirements where the prod- ucts pass through the production line with a predefined time duration at every assembly or workstation, and components are consumed at the backflushing points.  PP/DS length-based planning/multiple output planning is used in the mill industry (e.g., paper, steel, etc.) where the planning is dependent on the length requirement of the output product from a long raw material. We’ve covered the setup and working of the planning and scheduling features and also some of the advanced features offered by embedded PP/DS so far. In the next chapter, we’ll discuss some of the operations and administration tasks required to ensure the efficient use of embedded PP/DS. ©

chapters.title: SAP Digital Supply Chain Management, edition for SAP S/4HANA

sections.title: Solution Architecture
sections.en: 9.1 Solution Architecture Let’s get started with an overview of SAP Digital Supply Chain Management, edition for SAP S/4HANA. The following solutions are offered in SAP Digital Supply Chain Manage- ment, edition for SAP S/4HANA:  Enterprise portfolio and project management  Extended warehouse management  Transportation management  Yard logistics  Extended service parts planning  Manufacturing for planning and scheduling  Production engineering and operations 9 SAP Digital Supply Chain Management, edition for SAP S/4HANA 548 These solutions are also offered as embedded options in SAP S/4HANA. But for compa- nies who still leverage the SAP ERP system as their core ERP system and want to use these capabilities, SAP Digital Supply Chain Management is an option to deploy it side by side along with the SAP ERP system. In addition, multiple ERP systems can be con- nected to one SAP Digital Supply Chain system depending on the capability being lev- eraged, which simplifies the overall solution landscape. For companies that are already on SAP S/4HANA but want to leverage the new SAP Dig- ital Supply Chain capabilities that aren’t yet available in their SAP S/4HANA release, the SAP Digital Supply Chain system is an option to deploy a sidecar system with a higher SAP S/4HANA release to leverage the latest innovations in these solutions. Frequent upgrades can be performed in the sidecar SAP Digital Supply Chain systems, so that the latest features and functionalities introduced in SAP S/4HANA can be consumed for the available capabilities in the SAP Digital Supply Chain system. The modularity of the solutions usually brings in speed of consuming innovations in SAP solutions and flex- ibility in terms of changes to be introduced in the solution landscape. As shown in Figure 9.1, core ERP processes such as production planning and control or sales and distribution are executed in the core ERP system, and the advanced features are executed in the SAP Digital Supply Chain system. Standard integration options are available between the ERP and SAP Digital Supply Chain components. Figure 9.1 Application Architecture of SAP Digital Supply Chain SAP Digital Supply Chain Management, Edition for SAP S/4HANA System Production Engineering and Operations Extended Warehouse Management Transportation Management Yard Logistics Extended Service Part Planning Enterprise Portfolio and Project Management Manufacturing for Planning and Scheduling SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA System Sales and Distribution Production Planning and Control Material Management Plant Maintenance Financials and Controlling Project System Quality Management © 549 9.1 Solution Architecture Within SAP Digital Supply Chain Management, edition for SAP S/4HANA, the SAP S/4HANA Manufacturing for planning and scheduling solution is the focus of this chap- ter. SAP S/4HANA Manufacturing for planning and scheduling is another SAP S/4HANA system, but it only runs the embedded PP/DS solution. It can integrate to one or more SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA systems (core ERP) and integrate with components such as materials management for external procurement, production planning for manufac- turing, plant maintenance for resource downtimes and materials reservations, quality management for inspection lots, sales and distribution for sales orders, and so on. In SAP S/4HANA Manufacturing for planning and scheduling, the following scenarios are supported:  Discrete manufacturing  Process manufacturing  Repetitive manufacturing  Make-to-order (MTO)  Make-to-stock (MTS)  Characteristics-dependent planning (CDP)  Engineer-to-order (ETO), including variant configuration (VC) We’ll refer to the core ERP system—SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA—as the ERP system, and SAP S/4HANA Manufacturing for planning and scheduling as the planning and schedul- ing system, in this chapter. The technical architecture of the planning and scheduling system is shown in Figure 9.2. The ERP system is the master system for all the master data objects, such as mate- rial master, resource/work center master, BOMs/routings and production versions, master recipes, location master data such as plants/material requirements planning (MRP) areas/business partners, and external procurement master data such as pur- chasing info records/contracts/scheduling agreements. The master data objects are integrated from the ERP system to the planning and sched- uling system via the core interface leveraging integration models. There are certain master data objects that can’t be transferred to the planning and scheduling system via the core interface and need to be maintained manually, such as the location master data. We’ll cover the details in Section 9.4.1. The transaction data objects, including procurement proposals (planned orders, pur- chase requisitions), purchase orders, process/production orders, sales orders, and inventory/batches, are also integrated via the core interface and the corresponding integration models. The planning and scheduling system will have SAP liveCache in its SAP HANA database for PP/DS functionalities. In addition, the optimizer engine for the Production Plan- ning Optimizer and Detailed Scheduling Optimizer is also connected to the planning and scheduling system. 9 SAP Digital Supply Chain Management, edition for SAP S/4HANA 550 Figure 9.2 Architecture of SAP S/4HANA Manufacturing for Planning and Scheduling Connected to the ERP System For the SAP Fiori apps offered in the ERP system and in the planning and scheduling system, one SAP Gateway system, which is connected to both the ERP and planning and scheduling systems, can be in the landscape to support both systems. From the planning and scheduling functionalities perspective, all the chapters we’ve covered earlier for PP/DS are still applicable, except for any specific functionalities that are part of the restrictions list for the planning and scheduling solution. Following are the usage restrictions for the planning and schedulingsystem:  Available-to-promise (ATP) or advanced ATP (aATP) checks in the connected ERP sys- tem for planned orders, production orders, and process orders can’t be triggered from the planning and scheduling system. However, the order availability checks can be performed within the ERP system.  For executing planning runs, for materials integrated to the planning and schedul- ing system for PP/DS planning, the planning runs must be performed within the planning and scheduling system using the PP/DS planning run (Transaction /SAPAPO/CDPSB0). MRP Live in the ERP system can only plan the non-PP/DS mate- rials (materials that aren’t integrated to the planning and scheduling system, a cor- responding MRP type assigned in the material master such as PD, etc.).  Use of reference capacities in resource/work center master data isn’t supported as of SAP S/4HANA release 2022 for the planning and scheduling system.  Usage and integration of article master data, which is used in retail industry scenar- ios, isn’t supported. Master Data Transaction Data SAP HANA Database for S/4HANA; SAP HANA Database or Other Database for SAP ERP Systems Master Data Transaction Data SAP HANA Database SAP liveCache Optimizer Server Core Interface/ Manual Core Interface ERP System SAP S/4HANA Manufacturing for Planning and Scheduling SAP Gateway System SAP Fiori Apps © 551

sections.title: Prerequisites
sections.en: 9.2 Prerequisites  If the ERP system is an SAP ERP system, then the discrete industry and mill products (DIMP) business function called LAMA (activation of long material number) can’t be active in the ERP system.  Master data objects, such as plants/MRP areas, business partners, penalties for the Production Planning Optimizer maintained in the material master and work center master, and the time-dependent safety stock levels maintained in the ERP system can’t be transferred via core interface. These objects should be created and main- tained manually in the SAP Digital Supply Chain system. 9.2 Prerequisites For connecting an ERP system to the planning and scheduling system, there are certain software release-level restrictions. Only systems that are compatible with the release version can be connected, as shown in Table 9.1. Tip Many of the setup steps for configuring the ERP and SAP Digital Supply Chain systems are already covered in Chapter 3, so we won’t repeat such details in this chapter. Other prerequisites include the following:  In the SAP Digital Supply Chain system, SAP liveCache is installed in the SAP HANA database, and the SAP liveCache connections are set up. ERP System Manufacturing for Planning and Scheduling System Required SAP Notes SAP S/4HANA 2020 FPS1 or higher SAP S/4HANA 2020 FPS1 or higher 3020852 SAP S/4HANA 1909 with SP 6 or higher SAP S/4HANA 2020 FPS1 or higher 3126428 SAP ERP 6.0 EhP 8 with SP 17 or higher SAP S/4HANA 2020 FPS1 or higher 3004711 SAP ERP EhP 7 with SP 23 or higher SAP S/4HANA 2020 FPS1 or higher 3004711 Any version SAP S/4HANA 2021 or higher 3077933 (in the ERP system) Table 9.1 Software Release Version Compatibility for ERP and SAP Digital Supply Chain Systems 9 SAP Digital Supply Chain Management, edition for SAP S/4HANA 552  If the Production Planning Optimizer or Detailed Scheduling Optimizer functional- ities will be leveraged in the planning and scheduling system, ensure an optimizer server is installed and connected to the SAP Digital Supply Chain system.  Remote function call (RFC) users are created in the ERP and SAP Digital Supply Chain systems for the corresponding clients that will be connected via core interface.

sections.title: Customizing and Configuration
sections.en: 9.3 Customizing and Configuration In this section, we’ll cover the configuration settings required in the ERP system and in the planning and scheduling system for the integration of data. In addition, within the planning and scheduling system, we’ll also cover the PP/DS customization settings.

sections.title: Settings in the ERP System
sections.en: 9.3.1 Settings in the ERP System In this section, we’ll cover the customizing settings that need to be maintained in the ERP system. Basic Settings for Setting Up the System Landscape The following basic settings for setting up the landscape are available under Customiz- ing menu path SPRO  Integration with Other SAP Components  Advanced Planning and Optimization  Basic Settings for Setting Up the System Landscape:  Name logical system  Assign logical system to client  Specify the SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization release In the Customizing node, as shown in Figure 9.3, enter the logical system (Log.System) as the logical system ID for the SAP Digital Supply Chain system: “DSCCLNT001”, in the system type (Syst.Type) field, enter “SAP_S4HANA”, and in the Release field, enter the SAP S/4HANA release of the SAP Digital Supply Chain system. In our example, the SAP Digital Supply Chain system is an SAP S/4HANA 2022 system, so the release is main- tained as “107”. Figure 9.3 Specify the SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization Release for SAP Digital Supply Chain System’s Logical System © 553 9.3 Customizing and Configuration The next step is to set up the RFC destination. Follow SAP IMG menu path, SPRO  Inte- gration with Other SAP Components  Advanced Planning and Optimization  Basic Set- tings for Setting Up the System Landscape  Set Up RFC Destination. The RFC destination must be created with the same name as the logical system defined for the SAP Digital Supply Chain system. After the RFC destination is created, assign the RFC destination to the application. Nav- igate to SAP IMG menu path SPRO  Integration with Other SAP Components  Advanced Planning and Optimization  Basic Settings for Setting Up the System Landscape  Assign RFC Destinations to Different Application Cases. In this Customizing node, make a new entry, and, as shown in Figure 9.4, enter the SAP Digital Supply Chain system’s logical system in the Log.System field. Leave the application (Appl.) field with a blank value, and assign the RFC destination created for the SAP Digital Supply Chain system in the RFC Destination field. Figure 9.4 Assign the RFC Destination to Applications for the SAP Digital Supply Chain System The next step is to set the target system and the queue type. Navigate to SAP IMG menu path, SPRO  Integration with Other SAP Components  Advanced Planning and Optimi- zation  Basic Settings for Setting Up the System Landscape  Set Target System and Queue Type. In this Customizing transaction, make a new entry, and maintain the SAP Digital Supply Chain system’s logical system as the Log.System and maintain the Queue Type with value I (inbound queue). Basic Settings for Data Transfer The basic settings for setting up the landscape are available under Customizing menu path SPRO  Integration with Other SAP Components  Advanced Planning and Optimi- zation  Basic Settings for the Data Transfer. In the Configure Change Transfer for Mas- ter Data Customizing node or using Transaction CFC9, make the settings shown in Figure 9.5 for the change transfer of the master data objects. Under the Change Transfer for Master data area 1, use value 2 (BTE Transfer, Immedi- ately) for the Material Master Change Transfer, maintain a blank value (No Change 9 SAP Digital Supply Chain Management, edition for SAP S/4HANA 554 Transfer) for the Change Transfer for Customers and Change Transfer for Vendors fields, maintain the value 2 (BTE Transfer, Immediately) for Change Transfer for Setup Groups. Figure 9.5 Change Transfer Settings for Master Data in the ERP System Under Initial Data Transfer and Change Transfer for Resource, select the Immediate Transfer checkbox to enable the immediate transfer of changes made to the ERP resource/work center master data. Maintain a blank entry for Use Ext. Capacity (use external capacity), and for the Change Transf. Mode, maintain value A (Chng Trans. for Pl.-Vers-Indep. Res. and all PVs Model 000). The other settings available in this Customizing transaction (see Figure 9.5 2) are rele- vant in the SAP Digital Supply Chain system and not in the ERP system: © 555 9.3 Customizing and Configuration  Activation of Application Link Enabling (ALE) change pointers for message types In Transaction BD50, make sure that the change pointers are activated for the mes- sage type CIFSRC.  Activation of online transfer using business transfer events (BTEs) In Transaction BF11M, make sure the business transfer events New Dimension Plugin APO (ND-APO) and New Dimension Integration (NDI) are activated.  Register the RFC destination and register queue names For the outbound transfer of data from the ERP system to the planning and schedul- ing system, use Transaction SMQS to register the RFC destination. For processing inbound queues from the planning and scheduling system to the ERP system, regis- ter the CF* queue using Transaction SMQR in the ERP system.

sections.title: Settings in SAP S/4HANA Manufacturing for Planning and Scheduling
sections.en: 9.3.2 Settings in SAP S/4HANA Manufacturing for Planning and Scheduling Like the ERP system, in the planning and scheduling system as well the core interface, settings need to be maintained for processing master data and transaction data sent from the ERP system. In addition, settings are needed to integrate the planning and scheduling results in terms of procurement proposals, such as planned order and pur- chase requisitions, back to the ERP system. We’ll discuss the key settings required in the planning and scheduling system in the following sections. Basic Settings for Setting Up the System Landscape In the planning and scheduling system, the core interface settings are maintained in SAP IMG Customizing menu path SPRO  Advanced Planning  Integration via Core Interface (CIF). Under the basic settings for creating the system landscape, perform the following steps to define the basic settings for the core interface:  Name logical systems.  Assign the logical system to the client.  Set up the RFC destination (from the planning and scheduling system to the ERP sys- tem).  Assign RFC destinations to various application cases. In the Customizing node Assign RFC Destinations to various application cases, under the preceding SAP IMG menu path, assign an RFC Destination to the ERP system cre- ated with a dialog user assigned to it to the applications shown in Figure 9.6. In the CIF Applicatn (core interface application) column, select Display Application Log of another system to enable the selection and display of the application logs from the ERP systems in the planning and scheduling system in the core interface postprocessing transaction (Transaction /SAPAPO/CPP). Select Order Navigation from the same column to enable the navigation to transactions in the ERP system to display the order details from the 9 SAP Digital Supply Chain Management, edition for SAP S/4HANA 556 planning and scheduling system transactions, such as the product view (Transaction /SAPAPO/RRP3). Figure 9.6 Assigning RFC Destinations for Core Interface Applications in SAP S/4HANA Manufacturing for Planning and Scheduling Maintain Business System Group is an important Customizing setting. As multiple ERP systems can be connected to the planning and scheduling system, the business system group is the setting that differentiates the data coming in from different ERP systems into the planning and scheduling system. In the initial screen of this Customizing transaction, click on the New Entries button to create new entries for the business sys- tem group for all the ERP systems to be connected to the planning and scheduling sys- tem, as shown in Figure 9.7. Figure 9.7 Maintaining Business System Groups in SAP S/4HANA Manufacturing for Planning and Scheduling In the next step, we link the logical systems (ERP systems) to the corresponding busi- ness system group created in the steps. Navigate to SAP IMG menu path SPRO  Advanced Planning  Integration via Core Interface (CIF)  Integration  Basic Settings for Creating the System Landscape  Assign Logical System and Queue Type. In this transac- tion, as shown in Figure 9.8, maintain the business system group in the BusSystGrp field, and maintain the Logical system for the connected ERP systems. Set the value “X” for the SAP Ind. field, along with the Rel field with value “700”. In the Queue Type, select the Inbound Queues, and activate Postprocessing in the Err. Hndlg field. © 557 9.3 Customizing and Configuration Figure 9.8 Assignment of Logical System and Queue Type in SAP S/4HANA Manufacturing for Planning and Scheduling Next, register inbound queues using Transaction SMQR for processing inbound queues from the ERP systems. In addition, register the RFC destination for the outbound pro- cessing of data from SAP Digital Supply Chain to the ERP system using Transaction SMQS. Refer to Chapter 3, Section 3.2, for the details. In Transaction CFC9 settings in SAP Digital Supply Chain, make the same settings as mentioned in Section 9.3.1. In addition, you can also make the settings per specific requirements shown previously in Figure 9.5 1. In the SAP Digital Supply Chain sys- tem, you also activate the change pointers for message type CIFSRC in Transaction BD50. Then, using Transaction BF11, activate online transfer using BTEs for the NDI and ND-APO applications. Maintain distribution definitions under Customizing menu path, SPRO  Advanced Planning  Integration via Core Interface (CIF)  Basic Settings for Data Transfer  Publi- cation  Maintain Distribution Definition. In this transaction, make new entries for the External Procurement and In-House Production order objects for all the locations (plants and MRP areas; in our example, location PPS5), and enter the logical system of the connected ERP system in the LogSystem column, as shown in Figure 9.9. Figure 9.9 Creation of Distribution Definitions in SAP S/4HANA Manufacturing for Planning and Scheduling 9 SAP Digital Supply Chain Management, edition for SAP S/4HANA 558 This distribution definition determines the destination of the connected ERP system for the transactional data objects created and changed in the planning and scheduling system. This step must be performed after the PP/DS locations are created in the plan- ning and scheduling system, as described in Section 9.3.2. The last step is to maintain the retransfer settings for the in-house production orders under SAP IMG Customizing menu path SPRO  Advanced Planning  Integration via Core Interface (CIF)  Basic Settings for Data Transfer  Publication  Maintain Object- Specific Settings. In this transaction, create a new entry, select In-House Production in the Publ. Type (publication type) column, and select Always Retransfer in the Retrans- fer column, as shown in Figure 9.10. When orders are changed in the ERP system, the order is transferred to the planning and scheduling system via the core interface. If the order has to be changed in the planning and scheduling system when the core interface is updating (e.g., resource downtimes cause the order dates to be changed in the plan- ning and scheduling system), the retransfer settings make sure the new date for the orders is also immediately sent back to the ERP system. Figure 9.10 Retransfer Settings in SAP S/4HANA Manufacturing for Planning and Scheduling Global Settings Activate advanced planning in the planning and scheduling system using SAP IMG menu path SPRO  Advanced Planning  Basic Settings  Activate Advanced Planning and Scheduling  Activate Advanced Planning and Scheduling. In this Customizing transac- tion, select the Activate Advanced Planning and Scheduling checkbox, and save the transaction. Next, you need to set up the data transfer. Under SAP IMG menu path SPRO  Advanced Planning  Basic Settings  Settings for Data Transfer, as shown in Figure 9.11, deselect all the transaction data objects. As the transfer of the transaction data is initiated in the ERP system via the core interface, the data transfer settings within the planning and scheduling system aren’t relevant. © 559 9.3 Customizing and Configuration Figure 9.11 Data Transfer Settings in SAP S/4HANA Manufacturing for Planning and Scheduling The following steps are the basic PP/DS settings for the planning and scheduling sys- tem (refer to Chapter 3, Section 3.2, for details of these steps): 1. Define the configuration schema (CDP or VC). 2. Maintain the number ranges for orders in PP/DS. 3. Assign the number range for the orders in the PP/DS global settings and defaults (Transaction /SAPAPO/RRPCUST1). 4. For forecast and sales order consumption, maintain the corresponding settings for category groups and check mode. 5. When CDP functionalities are used in the planning and scheduling system, includ- ing shelf-life planning, maintain organizational areas for class type 023 under the object MARA. The organizational areas must be created with the same values as the organizational areas defined in the ERP system. 6. Create the active model (000) and active planning version (000) in the planning and scheduling system using Transaction /SAPAPO/MVM. The following steps are ERP Customizing for basic master data elements such as MRP controllers and person responsible for the work centers. We won’t cover these steps in detail as these are basic ERP customizations for SAP S/4HANA production planning. 1. Define the person responsible under the Customizing menu path SPRO  Advanced Planning  Master Data  Specify Person Responsible (Planner). In the planning and scheduling system, create the person responsible with the same names as that of the MRP controllers defined in the connected ERP systems. In the planning and schedul- ing and embedded PP/DS systems, the person responsible isn’t connected to the 9 SAP Digital Supply Chain Management, edition for SAP S/4HANA 560 location (plants or MRP areas). So, in the ERP system, define the MRP controllers in a way that they are unique values for different plants. 2. In the SAP Digital Supply Chain system, define the MRP groups and MRP controllers the same as in the connected ERP systems. 3. Define the special procurement keys and the plant-level maintenance of the special procurement settings in the SAP Digital Supply Chain system. Define the special pro- curement keys with the same name as defined in the ERP systems. 4. For the work centers, in the SAP Digital Supply Chain system, define the person responsible for the work centers under the ERP work center customization settings. In addition, if shift data is leveraged in the ERP system, define the corresponding shifts and related Customizing data in the planning and scheduling system. The work center formulas need to be created in the planning and scheduling system the same as the formulas defined in the ERP system. Material Master Settings In the planning and scheduling system, when material masters are transferred from the ERP system via the core interface integration model, it creates the material master first. This material master is made available to PP/DS in the planning and scheduling system by an automatic activation of the Advanced Planning indicator in the material master. Therefore, it’s important that the following Customizing settings in the plan- ning and scheduling system for the material master are maintained:  Field selection In SAP IMG menu path SPRO  Logistics – General  Material Master  Field Selection  Maintain Field Selection for Data Screens, compare the settings between the plan- ning and scheduling system and the ERP system. The fields marked as required entry (Reqd Entry), as shown in Figure 9.12, in the planning and scheduling system, should also be set as required entry in the ERP system. When certain fields are marked as mandatory fields in the planning and scheduling system, if those fields aren’t filled in for the ERP system (because they are set as optional fields in the ERP system), the transfer of material master from the ERP system to the planning and scheduling sys- tem will fail. So, for other fields in the planning and scheduling system that are rele- vant views in the material master (e.g., the MRP views), for the fields that are relevant in the ERP system (e.g., scrap-related fields, stock determination, etc.), mark them as optional fields in both systems so that the core interface transfer of the materials doesn’t fail in the inbound queues in the planning and scheduling system.  Quantity/value update and material types In the planning and scheduling system, the material master is created for facilitating the advanced planning, and the planning and scheduling system isn’t the system of record for inventory and its valuation. So, in SAP IMG menu path SPRO  Logistics – General  Material Master Basic Settings Material Types Define Attributes of Mate- rial Types, in the planning and scheduling system, deselect the Value updating checkboxes for all material types and valuation areas, as shown in Figure 9.13. © 561 9.3 Customizing and Configuration Figure 9.12 Material Master Field Selection in ERP and SAP S/4HANA Manufacturing for Planning and Scheduling Systems Figure 9.13 Deselecting Value Updating for Material Types in SAP S/4HANA Manufacturing for Planning and Scheduling 9 SAP Digital Supply Chain Management, edition for SAP S/4HANA 562 Apart from the Value updating, other settings ensure the material type details settings are the same in the planning and scheduling and ERP systems. In addition, ensure that the definition of key fields under Customizing menu path SPRO  Logistics – General  Material Master  Settings for Key Fields, are maintained the same in the ERP and plan- ning and scheduling systems.

sections.title: Integration
sections.en: 9.4 Integration The master data and the transaction data from the connected ERP system needs to be integrated to the planning and scheduling system for performing the planning and scheduling activities in the planning and scheduling system. In this section we will cover the details of the integration of master data and the transaction data objects.

sections.title: Integration of Master Data
sections.en: 9.4.1 Integration of Master Data Except for the location master data, all other master data is transferred from the ERP system to the planning and scheduling system via the core interface integration model. The details of creating and activating the integration model are already covered in Chapter 3. In this section, we’ll focus specifically on relevant master data for SAP Dig- ital Supply Chain Management, edition for SAP S/4HANA. Location Master Data The ERP plant, MRP areas, and business partners are required in the planning and scheduling system as the location master data. Transferring the material master from the ERP system to the planning and scheduling system first creates the material master in the planning and scheduling system and then activates the Advanced Planning indi- cator in an automatic way. So, to enable the creation of the material master in the plan- ning and scheduling system, the plant and MRP areas also need to be defined in the planning and scheduling system. The plant data needs to be assigned with the factory calendar in the planning and scheduling system, so before creating the plants in the planning and scheduling sys- tem, create the factory calendars the same as the factory calendars in the ERP systems. To create the plant in the planning and scheduling system, navigate to Customizing menu path SPRO  Enterprise Structure  Definition  Logistics – General  Define Copy Delete Check Plant  Define Plant. Here, create a new entry for all the plants correspond- ing to the plants defined in the connected ERP systems. Once the plant is created, assign the plant to a company code using SAP IMG menu path SPRO  Enterprise Structure  Assignment  Logistics – General  Assign Plant to Company Code. As the planning and scheduling system isn’t relevant for any financial or con- trolling processes, the company code in the planning and scheduling system can be © 563 9.4 Integration defined independently with only the mandatory fields, and the company codes need not match the ERP systems. The MRP area is another location master data item that needs to be defined in the plan- ning and scheduling system. As MRP areas will be assigned with storage locations or subcontracting vendors (business partners), create the corresponding storage loca- tions and the business partners in the planning and scheduling system. To create the MRP areas in the planning and scheduling system, follow SAP IMG menu path SPRO  Production  Material Requirement Planning  Master Data  MRP Areas  Define MRP Areas for Plants/Storage Locations or Define MRP Areas for Subcontractors. If the externally procured materials are also planned in the planning and scheduling system, it’s required to have the location master data representing the vendors (busi- ness partners) available in the planning and scheduling system. As the core interface integration model–based transfer for business partners isn’t supported in the planning and scheduling system, it’s required to create the business partners manually in the planning and scheduling system using Transaction BUP1. As the vendor business part- ner is only relevant in the planning and scheduling system to assign the vendor loca- tion to purchase requisitions during planning, it’s sufficient only to maintain the mandatory fields in the basic and purchasing organization views. Tip If the customer/vendor integration (CVI) is defined in the ERP systems, the ALE (IDocs) or Data Replication Framework (DRF) can be used to replicate the business partner data from the ERP system to the planning and scheduling system. Once all the required basic location master data items (e.g., plants, MRP areas, and busi- ness partners) are defined, execute program /SAPAPO/CREATE_LOCATION in the plan- ning and scheduling system to create the PP/DS locations in the planning and scheduling system. The steps and data flow are shown in Figure 9.14. Figure 9.14 Creation of Location Master Data in SAP S/4HANA Manufacturing for Planning and Scheduling Plants ERP System Storage Locations MRP Areas Business Partners (Vendors) Plants Storage Locations MRP Areas Business Partners (Vendors) SAP S/4HANA Manufacturing for Planning and Scheduling System Manual Creation Manual Creation Manual Creation Manual Creation ALE-IDocs/DRF PP/DS Locations with Corresponding Location Types Program /SAPAPO/ CREATE_ LOCATION 9 SAP Digital Supply Chain Management, edition for SAP S/4HANA 564 Other Master Data For other material master data objects, such as the material master, resource/work cen- ter master, BOMs/routings/production versions, master recipes, and external procure- ment master data (purchasing info records, contracts, scheduling agreements), create an integration model in the ERP system using Transaction CFM1, and activate the inte- gration model to transfer the data to the planning and scheduling system. Warning In the ERP system, don’t activate the Advanced Planning indicator in the Advanced Planning view of the material master for the materials that are integrated to the plan- ning and scheduling system. If the Advanced Planning indicator is selected in the SAP S/4HANA (ERP) system, it will be integrated to embedded PP/DS of the same SAP S/4HANA system. If you also integrate the material to the planning and scheduling sys- tem via the core interface integration model, this will lead to data inconsistencies in the system. After the activation of the integration model, the material master is available and the Advanced Planning flag is activated via a standard delivered enhancement (BAdI) CIF_ S4_BADI_PRODUCT_OUTBOUND in the planning and scheduling system. Within the planning and scheduling system, you can maintain PP/DS-specific fields such as product heuris- tics, safety stock settings, and so on. In addition, you can leverage the just-mentioned BAdI to also fill any other additional attributes of the material master with respect to the PP/DS-related fields. For the work centers and resources, the integration model activation will create the work center and resources in the planning and scheduling system, and the standard delivered enhancement BAdI CIF_S4_WORK_CENTER_OUTBOUND will set the Advanced Plan- ning indicator within the SAP S/4HANA Manufacturing for planning and scheduling system, which in turn creates the PP/DS resource master. For the in-house manufacturing master data, such as BOMs/routings/production ver- sions and master recipes, the creation and activation of integration models will create the production data structures (PDSs) in the planning and scheduling system. The BOMs/routings/production versions and master recipes aren’t replicated as the same objects in the planning and scheduling system; instead, the PDS is directly generated. Similarly for the external procurement master data, such as the purchasing info records, contracts, and scheduling agreements, the external procurement relation- ships are directly generated in the planning and scheduling system. For the classification data, such as classes and characteristics, you need to create an integration model in the ERP system with the filters for the organizational area assigned to the classes and characteristics and also apply filters for specific characteris- tics you want to transfer to the planning and scheduling system. Upon activation of the © 565 9.4 Integration integration model, the class and characteristics are available in the planning and sched- uling system. In addition, another integration needs to be created within the planning and scheduling system with the same filters applied in the ERP system. Upon activa- tion of the integration model within the planning and scheduling system, the classes and characteristics are available for PP/DS. Note Only the integration of class types 001, 023, and 300 are supported via the core inter- face integration from the ERP system to the planning and scheduling system. For maintenance of Production Planning Optimizer–specific penalties, use Transaction /SAPAPO/PPO_DPEN in the planning and scheduling system to maintain the penalty values. For time-dependent penalties and time-dependent safety stocks, use Transac- tion /SAPAPO/TDS in the planning and scheduling system. The steps and flow of master data objects from the ERP system to the planning and scheduling system are shown in Figure 9.15. Figure 9.15 Master Data Transfer from the ERP System to SAP S/4HANA Manufacturing for Planning and Scheduling

sections.title: Integration of Transaction Data
sections.en: 9.4.2 Integration of Transaction Data The integration of the transaction data between the ERP system and the planning and scheduling system is performed via the core interface using the integration models. In the ERP system, create the integration models for all the transaction data objects such as planned independent requirements (PIRs), sales orders, reservations, purchase orders, purchase requisitions, planned orders, production/process orders, stocks, Material Masters Work Centers/ Resources Production Data Structures (PDS) SAP S/4HANA Manufacturing for Planning and Scheduling System External Procurement Relationships PP/DS Product Masters PP/DS Resource Masters PP/DS Classes and Characteristics Core Interface – Integration Model Core Interface – Integration Model Material Masters ERP System Work Centers/ Resources BOMs/Routings/ Production Versions and Master Recipes Purchasing Info Records, Contracts, and Scheduling Agreements Classes and Characteristics Classes and Characteristics 9 SAP Digital Supply Chain Management, edition for SAP S/4HANA 566 batches, and so on. Activation of the integration models will send the data from the ERP system to the planning and scheduling system. Once the integration model is active, any changes made in the data in the ERP side will flow to the planning and scheduling system and vice versa via the core interface queues. For transaction data such as sales orders, PIRs, material reservations, stocks, and batches, the ERP system is the master system, and such data only flows from the ERP system to the planning and scheduling system. For purchase orders/requisitions and the produc- tion/planned order objects, these can be changed in both systems, and core interface transfers will be triggered as soon as the changes are saved in either of the systems. Note The administrative tools explained in Chapter 10 are applicable to the planning and scheduling system as well. The housekeeping/consistency check jobs with respect to the embedded PP/DS should be executed in the planning and scheduling system, and the jobs relevant for the SAP S/4HANA system should be executed in the ERP systems. For the correctness of the planning results, you need to ensure that a component at any BOM level is integrated to the planning and scheduling system for advanced planning, and all the components, semifinished products, and finished products above the com- ponent are also planned in SAP S/4HANA Manufacturing for planning and scheduling. For the planning and scheduling materials in the ERP system, the MRP type will be set as X0 - W/O MRP, with BOM explosion. So, such materials won’t be planned during the MRP Live or classic MRP planning in the ERP system. For example, component C1 (MRP type X0) is planned in the planning and scheduling system, the semifinished product S1 isn’t planned in SAP S/4HANA Manufacturing for planning and scheduling (MRP type PD), and the finished product F1 is planned in the planning and scheduling system (MRP type X0). During the planning run in the plan- ning and scheduling system, because the S1 material isn’t in the system, it doesn’t gen- erate a dependent demand for S1 in the planning and scheduling system. When the planned order for F1 is integrated back to the ERP system, in the next MRP planning in the ERP system, the planned order for F1 is re-exploded, the dependent demand is cre- ated, and a planned order is also created in the ERP system. Because S1 isn’t in the plan- ning and scheduling system, the planned order isn’t sent to the planning and scheduling system, so component C1 won’t get the dependent demand in the planning and scheduling system and scheduling (as the S1 planned order isn’t available in the planning and scheduling system and scheduling), and material C1 is left unplanned. In addition, when scheduling MRP runs in the ERP systems and the PP/DS planning runs in the planning and scheduling system, provide enough time gap between the completion of the PP/DS planning run before starting the MRP planning runs in the ERP systems. If the queues generated for the planned orders and purchase requisitions, © 567

sections.title: Summary
sections.en: 9.5 Summary which are created/changed/deleted during the planning runs, aren’t completely pro- cessed, the dependent demand for the non-planning and scheduling system materials are updated in the ERP system. This will lead to non-planning and scheduling system materials being missed in the ERP planning runs. 9.5 Summary In this chapter, we covered the application and technical architecture of SAP Digital Supply Chain Management, edition for SAP S/4HANA’s main solution for our area of focus, SAP S/4HANA Manufacturing for planning and scheduling. We covered the steps to set up the integration of the ERP systems to the SAP S/4HANA Manufacturing for planning and scheduling system and also the data flow for master data and transaction data. SAP S/4HANA Manufacturing for planning and scheduling can help companies with long-term plans for migrating to SAP S/4HANA from SAP ERP core systems to leverage the PP/DS capabilities in SAP S/4HANA in a sidecar fashion. In addition, for companies that want to leverage the latest improvements and innovations in PP/DS, SAP S/4HANA Manufacturing for planning and scheduling can aid them with frequent upgrades and keep the core ERP system to maintain its own upgrade cycles. In the next chapter, we’ll cover the details on administrating the embedded PP/DS sys- tem. ©

sections.title: Core Interface Queue Monitoring
sections.en: 10.1 Core Interface Queue Monitoring For most of the master data objects required in embedded PP/DS, the transfer is exe- cuted via the activation of the Advanced Planning checkbox in the master data object or by executing ABAP programs to generate such data for PP/DS (see Chapter 2). In these cases, no core interface queues are generated, and integration models aren’t required. For transaction data objects, except for the following transfers, all other transfers use the core interface qRFC communication:  Planned order and purchase requisitions from embedded PP/DS to the SAP S/4HANA system  Production orders, process orders, and purchase orders from embedded PP/DS to the SAP S/4HANA system For these data objects, a direct RFC will be executed to transfer the data from PP/DS to SAP S/4HANA. So, if there are any errors during the data transfer, the application log is updated with the error information in case background planning runs change the planned orders or purchase requisitions in PP/DS, and the transfer of data is termi- nated. In interactive mode, the error is displayed on the screen. The direction of the queues is determined by the configuration settings made in SAP S/4HANA and embedded PP/DS core interface settings. It’s recommended to have inbound queue communication for both directions. As shown in Figure 10.1, the queue directions are set in the following Customizing menu paths: 1 Embedded PP/DS: SAP IMG Menu  Advanced Planning  Integration via Core Inter- face (CIF)  Integration  Basic Settings for Creating the System Landscape  Assign Logical System and Queue Type 2 SAP S/4HANA: SAP IMG Menu  Integration with Other SAP Components  Advanced Planning and Optimization  Basic Settings for Setting Up the System Landscape  Set Target System and Queue Type © 571 10.1 Core Interface Queue Monitoring Because the queues are self-pointing (same logical system for SAP S/4HANA and embedded PP/DS), any queue failure can be monitored from the qRFC inbound moni- tor. The queue monitor can be launched from SAP Easy Access menu, Logistics  Advanced Planning  Administration  Integration  Monitor  Inbound Queue Monitor- ing, or Transaction SMQ2. Figure 10.1 Setting the Queue Direction in Embedded PP/DS and SAP S/4HANA The core interface queue name starts with the characters “CF”. As shown in Figure 10.2, in Transaction SMQ2, you enter the Queue Name as “CF*”, and ensure the correct Client is filled in. If you’re filtering queues with a Waiting status, you can enter the value “X” in the Waiting queues only field 1. Click Execute, and in the next screen, you’ll see the list of core interface queues, including the number of queues in the list 2 and the total number of RFCs 3, as shown on the lower portion of Figure 10.2. One queue can contain multiple RFCs. For example, when a production order goods receipt is posted, the sys- tem must ensure that the production order update and the stock update should hap- pen together successfully, so there will be two RFCs in the Transaction SMQ2 queue list. You can see this number in the Entries column 4. Following is the list of queue names for the commonly used objects for transfer between the ERP system and embedded PP/DS:  CFPLO* Planned orders, production orders, confirmations  CFPO* Purchase orders, purchase requisitions  CFSLS* Sales orders 10 Administering PP/DS with SAP S/4HANA 572  CFSTK* Stock  CFRSV* Manual reservations  CFSDS* Scheduling agreement items  CFSHP* Shipments  CFFCC* Reduction of planned independent requirements (PIRs)  CFPIR* PIRs Figure 10.2 Core Interface Inbound Queue Monitor The * is replaced by the corresponding order number. For example, if a purchase requi- sition with ERP number 10000222 is being transferred from the ERP system to embed- ded PP/DS, the queue name will be CFPO10000222. From the screen where the list of queues is displayed (refer to Figure 10.2), click on the Change view 5 button or use the keyboard shortcut (F8) to display the queues with their statuses. In addition, you can double-click on a queue to see its details and status. The queues are processed according to the settings maintained in the inbound queue scheduler (Transaction SMQR). You’ll see the following common statuses for the core interface inbound queues, the various actions of which can be performed according to the status of the queues, as shown in Figure 10.3: © 573 10.1 Core Interface Queue Monitoring  READY The queue is ready for processing. This is usually a temporary status, and after the scheduler picks up and processes the queue, it will be removed from the list. But if the queues are locked manually, this may also cause the queues to be in READY sta- tus. The queues need to be unlocked for processing.  RUNNING This is also a temporary status, indicating that the queue is currently being pro- cessed. If the RUNNING status stays for long, that may indicate an issue, and the queue status needs to be reset. As some of the RFCs within the queue might have already successfully reset processes, the status may update the data again in embed- ded PP/DS.  SYSFAIL This status indicates a serious error has occurred during the processing of the queue. This could be due to an application error or a runtime error generated during the queue processing. You can double-click on the error message to see the details regarding the reason for the failure. The SYSFAIL status queues aren’t automatically reprocessed by the system. After the reason for the error is corrected, these queues can be reprocessed.  WAITING The queue has dependency on other queues that weren’t successfully processed. The dependent logical unit of work (LUW) is also listed in the queue details. After the dependent queues are processed, the waiting queues will also be processed.  STOP An explicit lock or a generic queue lock on all CF* queues is set; for example, locks can be set for inbound CF* queue processing during a PP/DS planning run that is underway. Locks can be set using program RSTRFCI1 and unlocked using program RSTRFCI3.  RETRY For temporary problems encountered during the processing of the queues, the RETRY status is set. The temporary problems usually are due to locking conflicts. In such cases, the system will automatically schedule a background program to repro- cess these queues. In the background job monitor, you’ll see jobs with job name qRFC* followed by the transaction ID (TID) displayed in the queue for processing these retry queues.  CPICERR This status indicates a communication error or a network problem. The error details provide the technical information on the error.  NOEXEC This status is set usually when the queues are recorded for troubleshooting the applications. In the core interface user settings (Transaction /SAPAPO/C4 PP/DS and Transaction CFC2 in SAP S/4HANA), if the Debugging If the Value Is Set field is set to 10 Administering PP/DS with SAP S/4HANA 574 Debugging on, Recording of t/qRFCs (NO SEND), then the queues for such users will be set with the NOEXEC status. Figure 10.3 Core Interface Queue Monitoring: Details Double-click on the queue to display the status and the details of the queue, or click on the Change View button to display the status of all the queues, as shown in Figure 10.3 1. From the details of the queue, again double-click on the queue name to display all the LUWs within the queue. A failure of the first LUW processing can impact the whole queue. From there, you have the options to delete the queue 2 or process the individ- ual LUWs within the queue by clicking on the Activate Queue button 3; if no error occurs, it will process the queue. You can also choose the Unlock Queue option, which will immediately unlock the queue, removing the lock status and processing the queue if no error occurs 4. Clicking the Immediately button will immediately set the Lock sta- tus for the queue 5. You can also display the content of the queue. For example, a queue for a planned order will have the header, component list, operation details, and so on. In the standard sys- tem, the display of the queue is in binary format without assigning a correct display program. In the standard system, display program /SAPAPO/CIF_QUEUE_EVENT2 is delivered for displaying the core interface queues. In Transaction SMQE, choose More  Edit  Reg- ister Display Program. In the popup screen that appears, enter “CF*” as the Queue Name and “/SAPAPO/CIF_QUEUE_EVENT2” as the Program Name. Click on the Continue but- ton to save the display program. Click the queue name, and click the Display LUW button in the menu bar to display the queue contents, as shown in Figure 10.4. © 575 10.1 Core Interface Queue Monitoring Figure 10.4 Queue Monitor: Displaying the Queue Details The queue details are displayed without the display programs 1 and with the display programs 2 in Figure 10.5. After the display program is registered, the data contained in the queue is displayed in a structured and readable format when displaying the queue details. This is helpful when the queue failures are due to data errors, and you want to understand which exact data is being sent from SAP S/4HANA to embedded PP/DS in a specific queue. Figure 10.5 Core Interface: Display Queue Details and Contents 10 Administering PP/DS with SAP S/4HANA 576 If the direction of the core interface queues are configured as outbound queues, Trans- action SMQ1 can be used to monitor the outbound queues. Tip When automatic planning is used in a PP/DS planning procedure, during the planning run or when the automatic planning–relevant events occurs in the system, an out- bound queue with PP_PLANNING is created by the system, which will execute the plan- ning for the impacted products. So, if you use automatic planning in planning procedures, the outbound queues must be monitored from Transaction SMQ1. Note For the SAP Digital Supply Chain system, it’s recommended to have the inbound queue direction for data transfer from ERP systems (SAP S/4HANA or SAP ERP) to the SAP Dig- ital Supply Chain system and for the data transfer from the SAP Digital Supply Chain system to the ERP systems. In this case, you need to monitor Transaction SMQ2 for queue errors in both the SAP Digital Supply Chain system and the ERP system.

sections.title: Core Interface Postprocessing
sections.en: 10.2 Core Interface Postprocessing When queues are stuck in the inbound queue due to errors or WAITING status, this may lead to other queues being stuck due to dependencies on the queues. Eventually, this will lead to thousands of queues stuck, and the communication between SAP S/4HANA and PP/DS will come to a halt. To avoid such situations, it’s recommended to activate core interface postprocessing (CPP). With CPP, the queues that are to error out and stop in the inbound queue are transferred to the postprocessing queue, so that other queues are processed successfully if possible. With the following exceptions, all queues that run into issues during processing are moved to postprocessing:  When the queue processing generates a runtime error (short dumps)  When the initial data transfer is processed for objects that require a model-based integration (purchasing master data, maintenance orders, etc.)  When SAP liveCache isn’t available  When errors are triggered in enhancements (user exits, business add-ins [BAdIs]) in the core interface In all other circumstances, the faulty queue won’t be listed in the inbound queue mon- itor, and a postprocessing record will be generated. The activation of CPP in advanced planning is done from Customizing menu path, SAP IMG Menu  Advanced Planning  Integration via Core Interface (CIF)  Basic Settings for © 577 10.2 Core Interface Postprocessing Data Transfer  CIF Error Handling  Activate CIF Error Handling. You’ll arrive at the screen shown in Figure 10.6. Select the Postprocessing for Errors, No Splitting of LUWs option in the Err.Hndlg column, and click the Save button to save the changes. Figure 10.6 Activation of CPP for Queue Errors The postprocessing records can be displayed and processed from Transaction /SAPAPO/CPP, or you can follow SAP Easy Access menu, Logistics  Advanced Planning  Administration  Integration  CIF Error Handling  CIF Postprocessing. You’ll arrive at the screen shown in Figure 10.7. Figure 10.7 CPP: Selection Options 10 Administering PP/DS with SAP S/4HANA 578 In this transaction, select the Target System (embedded PP/DS always has one logical system for the core interface), and select other options as required. You can filter the records by the status of the postprocessing record and the error status of the records in the Restriction by Status area. The postprocessing status (Processing Status) indicates the status of the postprocessing after the record is created in CPP:  1 Still for Processing The record is created, not processed yet, and needs to be retransferred.  2 Processed The record has already been processed; no action is required.  3 Obsolete (Set Manually) The user has set the record as obsolete from the postprocessing transaction. This can be revoked manually.  4 Obsolete (Set Automatically by System) If the impacted transaction object is successfully transferred to PP/DS after the post- processing record is created during an earlier attempt to transfer the same object, the system sets the CPP record as obsolete.  5 Retransfer Not Allowed A retransfer of the data isn’t allowed for this postprocessing record. These records are for informational purposes and can be set as obsolete after the record is ana- lyzed. The Error Status of the postprocessing records can have the following values:  No Errors This object was successfully processed and didn’t raise any errors. These records are still displayed in CPP because, when one qRFC within a queue (LUW) isn’t processed in the core interface due to an error, all the objects in the same LUW queue are trans- ferred to CPP.  Errors The object was processed in the core interface and raised an error, so the postpro- cessing record is created.  Object Not Processed This object is part of the same LUW queue but is placed after the qRFC that raised an error, so the system didn’t attempt to process this (ignored). You won’t know whether this object will be successfully processed in the core interface or will raise an error until you process the CPP record and transfer the data. Tip If you want to troubleshoot the core interface queues generated from the postprocess- ing, you can enter the OK code “DEBUG_ON” in the transaction search box at the top left of the CPP’s initial screen. This will display additional options in the bottom of the screen to stop the queues for analysis. © 579 10.2 Core Interface Postprocessing Select the Select Data from ERP checkbox to also read and display any postprocessing records generated by SAP S/4HANA when processing inbound PP/DS data in SAP S/4HANA. After you’ve entered the required selection options, click the Execute button to display the list of the postprocessing records. In the next screen, you’ll see the list of CPP records organized by the direction of transfer (SAP S/4HANA to PP/DS or vice versa) and the type of object for which the record is created (in-house manufacturing, exter- nal procurement, stocks, etc.). Note Though the transfer of data from PP/DS to SAP S/4HANA for certain objects such as planned orders and purchase requisitions is synchronous, when any error occurs during the transfer, the postprocessing records are created with queue name CIF_SYN- CHRON_CALL in the postprocessing record. As shown in Figure 10.8, the postprocessing screen has four panels. The left side of the screen is the navigation tree that lists the records; you can load the records for the object by double-clicking on the nodes. The worklist contains the individual records available for postprocessing. You can change the layout of the table by clicking on the Choose Layout – Change Layout button A on the menu bar to add additional columns to display the status of the error or the status of the postprocessing and other informa- tional columns available for selection. The Objects Processed in this Session 6 panel lists the records you’ve selected from the worklist and processed. If the records are pro- cessed successfully, they will be marked with a green background. Any application log messages raised during the processing are displayed in the bottom panel of the screen. Figure 10.8 Working with CPP Records 10 Administering PP/DS with SAP S/4HANA 580 From the worklist shown in Figure 10.8, you can select a record and choose an option from the menu bar: 1 Display Application Log The postprocessing records have the TID of the queue/LUW when the queue was processed. The Display Application Log option reads the application log of the listed TID and displays the log. 2 Display History This button in the menu bar of the CPP worklist shows all the actions performed on the postprocessing record selected. It lists the time stamp and user details of the postprocessing record creation, along with the history of any further actions, such as processing of the records performed. 3 Set/Reset Obsolete If you don’t want to process a postprocessing record, you can mark them as obsolete using this option. Such records will be set with Obsolete (set manually) status. You can also revoke the manually set Obsolete indicator. 4 Send to ERP/Send to APO These buttons will be activated by the system depending on the direction of the transfer. When you select the records from the list of error records worklist, and process them by either clicking on Send to APO or Send to R/3, depending on the queue direction, the selected records will be processed 5, and in the middle part of the screen under Object Processes in this Session 6, you’ll see the records being processed and their processing status. The application log for the records processed are also displayed on the bottom of the screen 7. For reading the application logs from the SAP S/4HANA side for the CPP records, the system uses the default user maintained in the RFC destination in the core interface settings. As the default user is usually created with a System user type, you may not see any logs or may encounter an error while reading the logs.
